originalComment: Creates static initialization block that simply calls all advice static init methods in correct order.
codeComment: This method, `makeStaticInitBlock`, generates a static initialization block in a Java class using the ASM library. It checks if the `adviceClinits` list in the `wd` object is not null. If it's not null, it creates a `MethodVisitor` to define a static method (`<clinit>`). This method iterates over each method name in `adviceClinits`, invoking each as a static method on the current class. Finally, it returns from the method and marks the end of the method visit.
codeFunctions: protected void makeStaticInitBlock () { if (wd.adviceClinits != null) { MethodVisitor mv = wd.dest.visitMethod (AsmUtil.ACC_STATIC,CLINIT,DESC_VOID,null,null);mv.visitCode ();for (String name:wd.adviceClinits) { mv.visitMethodInsn (INVOKESTATIC,wd.thisReference,name,DESC_VOID,false);} mv.visitInsn (RETURN);mv.visitMaxs (0,0);mv.visitEnd ();} }

originalComment: Creates init method that simply calls all advice constructor methods in correct order.This created init method is called from each destination s constructor.
codeFunctions: protected void makeProxyConstructor () { MethodVisitor mv = wd.dest.visitMethod (AsmUtil.ACC_PRIVATE | AsmUtil.ACC_FINAL,ProxettaNames.initMethodName,DESC_VOID,null,null);mv.visitCode ();if (wd.adviceInits != null) { for (String name:wd.adviceInits) { mv.visitVarInsn (ALOAD,0);mv.visitMethodInsn (INVOKESPECIAL,wd.thisReference,name,DESC_VOID,false);} } mv.visitInsn (RETURN);mv.visitMaxs (0,0);mv.visitEnd ();}

originalComment: Checks for all public super methods that are not overridden.
codeComment: The `processSuperMethods` method iterates over the `superClassReaders` of the `targetClassInfo` and processes each class using an `EmptyClassVisitor`. For each class, it captures the declared class name and visits its methods. If the method is either the constructor (`<init>`) or the class initializer (`<clinit>`), it skips processing. Otherwise, it looks up a `MethodSignatureVisitor` for the method and applies a proxy if the visitor is found.
codeFunctions: protected void processSuperMethods () { for (ClassReader cr:targetClassInfo.superClassReaders) { cr.accept (new EmptyClassVisitor () { String declaredClassName;@ Override public void visit (final int version,final int access,final String name,final String signature,final String superName,final String [ ] interfaces) { declaredClassName = name;} @ Override public MethodVisitor visitMethod (final int access,final String name,final String desc,final String signature,final String [ ] exceptions) { if (name.equals (INIT) || name.equals (CLINIT)) { return null;} MethodSignatureVisitor msign = targetClassInfo.lookupMethodSignatureVisitor (access,name,desc,declaredClassName);if (msign == null) { return null;} return applyProxy (msign);} },0);} }

originalComment: Finds very last index of given element in inclusive index range.Returns negative value if element is not found.
codeComment: This method implements a binary search algorithm to find the last occurrence of a target value within a sorted array. It initializes `ndx` to -1 to track the index of the last found occurrence. The method uses a while loop to repeatedly divide the search range in half (`low` to `high`). It calculates the middle index `mid` and uses the `compare` method to determine the relationship between the target and the element at `mid`. If the target is greater than the element at `mid`, it narrows the search to the left half by setting `high` to `mid - 1`. If the target is equal to the element at `mid`, it updates `ndx` to `mid` and continues searching the right half by setting `low` to `mid + 1`. If the target is less than the element at `mid`, it narrows the search to the left half. After the loop, if `ndx` is still -1, it returns `-(low + 1)` to indicate the target is not found. Otherwise, it returns `ndx`, the index of the last occurrence of the target.
codeFunctions: public int findLast (int low,int high) { int ndx = - 1;while (low <= high) { int mid = (low + high) >>> 1;int delta = compare (mid);if (delta > 0) { high = mid - 1;} else { if (delta == 0) { ndx = mid;} low = mid + 1;} } if (ndx == - 1) { return - (low + 1);} return ndx;}

originalComment: Returns chalked string.

Otherwise, it constructs a new string using a `StringBuilder`. If a `prefix` is provided, it appends the prefix followed by "m" to the `StringBuilder`. Then, it appends the input string. If a `suffix` is provided, it appends the suffix followed by "m" to the `StringBuilder`. Finally, it returns the constructed string.
codeFunctions: public String on (final String string) { if (!enabled) { return string;} final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder ();if (prefix != null) { sb.append (prefix).append ("m");} sb.append (string);if (suffix != null) { sb.append (suffix).append ("m");} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Returns the equivalent of the given class file with the ASM specific instructions replaced with standard ones.This is done with a ClassReader - >ClassWriter round trip.
codeComment: This method, `replaceAsmInstructions`, processes a Java class file represented as a byte array. It initializes various fields to null and sets up attributes for processing. The method determines whether to compute frames based on the `hasFrames` parameter. It then uses a `ClassReader` to parse the class file, applying transformations and expanding instructions as needed. Finally, it returns the modified class file as a byte array.
codeFunctions: private byte [ ] replaceAsmInstructions (final byte [ ] classFile,final boolean hasFrames) { final Attribute [ ] attributes = getAttributePrototypes ();firstField = null;lastField = null;firstMethod = null;lastMethod = null;lastRuntimeVisibleAnnotation = null;lastRuntimeInvisibleAnnotation = null;lastRuntimeVisibleTypeAnnotation = null;lastRuntimeInvisibleTypeAnnotation = null;moduleWriter = null;nestHostClassIndex = 0;numberOfNestMemberClasses = 0;nestMemberClasses = null;firstAttribute = null;compute = hasFrames?MethodWriter.COMPUTE_INSERTED_FRAMES:MethodWriter.COMPUTE_NOTHING;new ClassReader (classFile,0,/* checkClassVersion = */ false).accept (this,attributes,(hasFrames?ClassReader.EXPAND_FRAMES:0) | ClassReader.EXPAND_ASM_INSNS);return toByteArray ();}

originalComment: Returns the prototypes of the attributes used by this class its fields and its methods.
codeComment: The method `getAttributePrototypes` initializes an `Attribute.Set` object to store attribute prototypes. It starts by adding the `firstAttribute` to the set. It then iterates through a linked list of `FieldWriter` objects, collecting attribute prototypes from each using the `collectAttributePrototypes` method. After processing all `FieldWriter` objects, it iterates through a linked list of `MethodWriter` objects, similarly collecting attribute prototypes. Finally, it converts the set of attribute prototypes to an array and returns it.
codeFunctions: private Attribute [ ] getAttributePrototypes () { Attribute.Set attributePrototypes = new Attribute.Set ();attributePrototypes.addAttributes (firstAttribute);FieldWriter fieldWriter = firstField;while (fieldWriter != null) { fieldWriter.collectAttributePrototypes (attributePrototypes);fieldWriter = (FieldWriter) fieldWriter.fv;} MethodWriter methodWriter = firstMethod;while (methodWriter != null) { methodWriter.collectAttributePrototypes (attributePrototypes);methodWriter = (MethodWriter) methodWriter.mv;} return attributePrototypes.toArray ();}

originalComment: Registers default set of SQL types.

originalComment: Registers sql type for provided type.

originalComment: Retrieves SQL type for provided type.All subclasses and interfaces are examined for matching sql type.
codeComment: The method `lookup` takes a `Class` object as input and attempts to find a corresponding `SqlType` by traversing the class hierarchy and implemented interfaces. It starts with the given class and iterates up through its superclasses, checking if the class or any of its interfaces are mapped to a `SqlType` in the `types` map. If a match is found, it returns the `SqlType`. If no match is found after checking all superclasses and interfaces, it returns `null`.
codeFunctions: public SqlType lookup (final Class clazz) { SqlType sqlType;for (Class x = clazz;x != null;x = x.getSuperclass ()) { sqlType = types.get (clazz);if (sqlType != null) { return sqlType;} Class [ ] interfaces = x.getInterfaces ();for (Class i:interfaces) { sqlType = types.get (i);if (sqlType != null) { return sqlType;} } } return null;}

originalComment: Returns sql type instance.Instances are stored for better performances.
codeComment: This method, `lookupSqlType`, retrieves an instance of a specified SQL type class. It first checks if the SQL type is already cached in the `sqlTypes` map. If not, it attempts to create a new instance of the SQL type class using `ClassUtil.newInstance`. If an exception occurs during instantiation, it throws a `DbSqlException`. The newly created SQL type instance is then cached in the `sqlTypes` map before being returned.
codeFunctions: public SqlType lookupSqlType (final Class <?extends SqlType > sqlTypeClass) { SqlType sqlType = sqlTypes.get (sqlTypeClass);if (sqlType == null) { try { sqlType = ClassUtil.newInstance (sqlTypeClass);} catch (Exception ex) { throw new DbSqlException ("SQL type not found: " + sqlTypeClass.getSimpleName (),ex);} sqlTypes.put (sqlTypeClass,sqlType);} return sqlType;}

originalComment: Returns total number of transactions associated with current thread.

originalComment: Returns total number of transactions of the specified status associated with current thread.
codeComment: This method, `totalThreadTransactionsWithStatus`, takes a `JtxStatus` object as a parameter and returns the count of transactions in the `txStack` that have the specified status. It first retrieves the list of transactions from `txStack`. If the list is null, it returns 0. Otherwise, it iterates through the list, increments a counter for each transaction that matches the given status, and finally returns the count.
codeFunctions: public int totalThreadTransactionsWithStatus (final JtxStatus status) { ArrayList < JtxTransaction > txlist = txStack.get ();if (txlist == null) { return 0;} int count = 0;for (JtxTransaction tx:txlist) { if (tx.getStatus () == status) { count ++;} } return count;}

If `txList` is null, it initializes a new `ArrayList` and sets it in `txStack`. Finally, it adds the transaction to `txList`.
codeFunctions: protected void associateTransaction (final JtxTransaction tx) { totalTransactions ++;ArrayList < JtxTransaction > txList = txStack.get ();if (txList == null) { txList = new ArrayList <> ();txStack.set (txList);} txList.add (tx);// add last }

originalComment: Check if propagation of a transaction is possible due to source and destination transaction modes.
codeComment:
The `continueTx` method is designed to validate and continue a transaction by comparing the transaction modes and isolation levels of the source and destination transactions. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Validation Check**: The method first checks if the existing transaction is valid. If not, it returns immediately.

2. **Retrieve Transaction Modes**: It retrieves the transaction mode of the source transaction (`sourceMode`) and the isolation level of the destination transaction (`destIsolationLevel`).

3. **Isolation Level Comparison**: If the destination isolation level is not the default, it compares it with the current isolation level of the source transaction. If they are different, it throws a `JtxException` indicating an incompatible isolation level.

4. **Read-Only Check**: It checks if the destination transaction is not read-only while the source transaction is read-only. If this condition is met, it throws a `JtxException` indicating a mismatch in read-only status.

This method ensures that the transaction modes and isolation levels are compatible before continuing the transaction.
codeFunctions: protected void continueTx (final JtxTransaction sourceTx,final JtxTransactionMode destMode) { if (!validateExistingTransaction) { return;} JtxTransactionMode sourceMode = sourceTx.getTransactionMode ();JtxIsolationLevel destIsolationLevel = destMode.getIsolationLevel ();if (destIsolationLevel != ISOLATION_DEFAULT) { JtxIsolationLevel currentIsolationLevel = sourceMode.getIsolationLevel ();if (currentIsolationLevel != destIsolationLevel) { throw new JtxException ("Participating TX specifies isolation level: " + destIsolationLevel + " which is incompatible with existing TX: " + currentIsolationLevel);} } if ((!destMode.isReadOnly ()) && (sourceMode.isReadOnly ())) { throw new JtxException ("Participating TX is not marked as read-only, but existing TX is");} }

originalComment: Lookups resource manager for provided type.Throws an exception if provider doesn t exists.

If the resource manager is not found, it throws a `JtxException` indicating that no registered resource manager exists for the given resource type. If found, it returns the resource manager.
codeFunctions: protected < E > JtxResourceManager < E > lookupResourceManager (final Class < E > resourceType) { //noinspection unchecked JtxResourceManager < E > resourceManager = this.resourceManagers.get (resourceType);if (resourceManager == null) { throw new JtxException ("No registered resource manager for resource type: " + resourceType.getSimpleName ());} return resourceManager;}

originalComment: Creates proxy object.
codeComment: The method `createProxyObject` creates a proxy object for a given target class. It first resolves the target class using `ProxettaUtil.resolveTargetClass`. It then checks if a proxy class for this target is already cached. If not, it defines a new proxy class using `proxetta.defineProxy` and caches it. Finally, it attempts to create an instance of the proxy class using `ClassUtil.newInstance` and returns it. If any exception occurs during this process, it throws a `PathrefException`.
codeFunctions: protected C createProxyObject (Class < C > target) { target = ProxettaUtil.resolveTargetClass (target);Class proxyClass = cache.get (target);if (proxyClass == null) { proxyClass = proxetta.defineProxy (target);cache.put (target,proxyClass);} C proxy;try { proxy = (C) ClassUtil.newInstance (proxyClass);} catch (Exception ex) { throw new PathrefException (ex);} return proxy;}

originalComment: Appends method name to existing path.
codeComment: The `append` method is designed to add a method name to a path string. It first checks if the path is not empty and appends a dot (`.`) if it is not. If the method name starts with a left square bracket (`[`), it removes the last character from the path. Finally, it appends the method name to the path.
codeFunctions: protected void append (final String methodName) { if (path.length () != 0) { path += StringPool.DOT;} if (methodName.startsWith (StringPool.LEFT_SQ_BRACKET)) { path = StringUtil.substring (path,0,- 1);} path += methodName;}

originalComment: Puts the text to the left and pads with spaces until the size is reached.
codeComment: This method, `alignLeftAndPad`, takes a string `text` and an integer `size` as input. It aligns the text to the left and pads it with spaces to match the specified size. If the text length exceeds the size, it truncates the text to the given size. Otherwise, it appends spaces to the end of the text until it reaches the specified size.
codeFunctions: public static String alignLeftAndPad (final String text,final int size) { int textLength = text.length ();if (textLength > size) { return text.substring (0,size);} final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (size);sb.append (text);while (textLength ++ < size) { sb.append (' ');} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Converts object into pretty string.All arrays are iterated.
codeComment: The `toPrettyString` method converts an object to a pretty-printed string representation. It handles different types of objects, including arrays and iterables, and recursively processes their elements. For arrays, it checks the component type and uses `ArraysUtil.toString` for primitive types. For object arrays and iterables, it recursively converts each element to a string and appends them with spaces. If the object is `null`, it returns a predefined `NULL` string.
codeFunctions: public static String toPrettyString (final Object value) { if (value == null) { return StringPool.NULL;} final Class <?> type = value.getClass ();if (type.isArray ()) { final Class componentType = type.getComponentType ();if (componentType.isPrimitive ()) { final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder ();sb.append (' ');if (componentType == int.class) { sb.append (ArraysUtil.toString ((int [ ]) value));} else if (componentType == long.class) { sb.append (ArraysUtil.toString ((long [ ]) value));} else if (componentType == double.class) { sb.append (ArraysUtil.toString ((double [ ]) value));} else if (componentType == float.class) { sb.append (ArraysUtil.toString ((float [ ]) value));} else if (componentType == boolean.class) { sb.append (ArraysUtil.toString ((boolean [ ]) value));} else if (componentType == short.class) { sb.append (ArraysUtil.toString ((short [ ]) value));} else if (componentType == byte.class) { sb.append (ArraysUtil.toString ((byte [ ]) value));} else { throw new IllegalArgumentException ();} sb.append (' ');return sb.toString ();} else { final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder ();sb.append (' ');final Object [ ] array = (Object [ ]) value;for (int i = 0;i < array.length;i ++) { if (i > 0) { sb.append (' ');} sb.append (toPrettyString (array [ i ]));} sb.append (' ');return sb.toString ();} } else if (value instanceof Iterable) { final Iterable iterable = (Iterable) value;final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder ();sb.append (' ');int i = 0;for (final Object o:iterable) { if (i > 0) { sb.append (' ');} sb.append (toPrettyString (o));i ++;} sb.append (' ');return sb.toString ();} return value.toString ();}

originalComment: Converts separated string value to CamelCase.
codeComment: The `toCamelCase` method converts a given string into camel case format. It takes three parameters: the input string, a boolean indicating whether the first character should be uppercase, and a character that serves as a separator. The method iterates through each character of the input string, converting characters following the separator to uppercase and appending them to a `StringBuilder`. Characters not following a separator are appended as they are. The resulting camel case string is then returned.
codeFunctions: public static String toCamelCase (final String input,final boolean firstCharUppercase,final char separator) { final int length = input.length ();final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (length);boolean upperCase = firstCharUppercase;for (int i = 0;i < length;i ++) { final char ch = input.charAt (i);if (ch == separator) { upperCase = true;} else if (upperCase) { sb.append (Character.toUpperCase (ch));upperCase = false;} else { sb.append (ch);} } return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Formats provided string as paragraph.
codeComment: The `formatParagraph` method formats a given source string (`src`) into paragraphs of a specified length (`len`). It can optionally break lines at whitespace (`breakOnWhitespace`). The method uses a `StringBuilder` to construct the formatted string. It iterates over the source string, determining where to break lines based on the specified length and whitespace conditions. Non-whitespace characters are trimmed at the start and end of each line segment before appending them to the `StringBuilder`. Finally, it returns the formatted string.
codeFunctions: public static String formatParagraph (final String src,final int len,final boolean breakOnWhitespace) { StringBuilder str = new StringBuilder ();int total = src.length ();int from = 0;while (from < total) { int to = from + len;if (to >= total) { to = total;} else if (breakOnWhitespace) { int ndx = StringUtil.lastIndexOfWhitespace (src,to - 1,from);if (ndx != - 1) { to = ndx + 1;} } int cutFrom = StringUtil.indexOfNonWhitespace (src,from,to);if (cutFrom != - 1) { int cutTo = StringUtil.lastIndexOfNonWhitespace (src,to - 1,from) + 1;str.append (src,cutFrom,cutTo);} str.append (' ');from = to;} return str.toString ();}

originalComment: Converts all tabs on a line to spaces according to the provided tab width.This is not a simple tab to spaces replacement since the resulting indentation remains the same.
codeComment: The `convertTabsToSpaces` method converts tabs in a given string to spaces based on a specified tab width. It iterates through the string, replacing each tab character with the appropriate number of spaces to align with the next tab stop. If the tab width is zero, it removes all spaces from the string. The method uses a `StringBuilder` to efficiently build the resulting string with spaces replacing tabs.
codeFunctions: public static String convertTabsToSpaces (final String line,final int tabWidth) { int tab_index,tab_size;int last_tab_index = 0;int added_chars = 0;if (tabWidth == 0) { return StringUtil.remove (line,' ');} StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder ();while ((tab_index = line.indexOf (' ',last_tab_index)) != - 1) { tab_size = tabWidth - ((tab_index + added_chars) % tabWidth);if (tab_size == 0) { tab_size = tabWidth;} added_chars += tab_size - 1;result.append (line,last_tab_index,tab_index);result.append (StringUtil.repeat (' ',tab_size));last_tab_index = tab_index + 1;} if (last_tab_index == 0) { return line;} result.append (line.substring (last_tab_index));return result.toString ();}

originalComment: Escapes a string using java rules.
codeComment: The `escapeJava` method takes a string as input and returns a new string with all Java escape sequences properly escaped. It iterates over each character in the input string, checks if it needs to be escaped, and appends the appropriate escape sequence to a `StringBuilder`. Characters that are not printable ASCII characters (outside the range 32 to 127) are converted to their Unicode escape sequences. The method returns the final escaped string.
codeFunctions: public static String escapeJava (final String string) { int strLen = string.length ();StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (strLen);for (int i = 0;i < strLen;i ++) { char c = string.charAt (i);switch (c) { case ' ':sb.append ("\\b");break;case ' ':sb.append ("\\t");break;case ' ':sb.append ("\\n");break;case ' ':sb.append ("\\f");break;case ' ':sb.append ("\\r");break;case ' ':sb.append ("\\\"");break;case ' ':sb.append ("\\\\");break;default:if ((c < 32) || (c > 127)) { String hex = Integer.toHexString (c);sb.append ("\\u");for (int k = hex.length ();k < 4;k ++) { sb.append (' ');} sb.append (hex);} else { sb.append (c);} } } return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Unescapes a string using java rules.
codeComment: The `unescapeJava` method processes a given string to remove Java escape sequences. It iterates through each character of the input string, appending non-space characters directly to a `StringBuilder`. For space characters, it checks the next character to determine if it's part of an escape sequence. If it is, it converts the hexadecimal value following the escape sequence into a character and appends it to the `StringBuilder`. If the escape sequence is invalid, it throws an `IllegalArgumentException`. The method returns the processed string.
codeFunctions: public static String unescapeJava (final String str) { char [ ] chars = str.toCharArray ();StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (str.length ());for (int i = 0;i < chars.length;i ++) { char c = chars [ i ];if (c != ' ') { sb.append (c);continue;} i ++;c = chars [ i ];switch (c) { case ' ':sb.append (' ');break;case ' ':sb.append (' ');break;case ' ':sb.append (' ');break;case ' ':sb.append (' ');break;case ' ':sb.append (' ');break;case ' ':sb.append (' ');break;case ' ':sb.append (' ');break;case ' ':char hex = (char) Integer.parseInt (new String (chars,i + 1,4),16);sb.append (hex);i += 4;break;default:throw new IllegalArgumentException ("Invalid escaping character: " + c);} } return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Returns Petite bean instance.Bean name will be resolved from provided type.
codeComment: The method `getBean` retrieves a bean of a specified type by first resolving the bean's name using the `resolveBeanName` method and then fetching the bean using the resolved name. The method is generic, allowing it to return beans of any type `T`. The `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked")` annotation is used to suppress unchecked warnings that may arise from the type casting.

originalComment: Returns Petite bean instance.Petite container will find the bean in corresponding scope and all its dependencies either by constructor or property injection.When using constructor injection cyclic dependencies can not be prevented but at least they are detected.
codeComment: The method `getBean` retrieves a bean instance by its name. It first looks up the bean definition. If the definition is not found, it checks for a provider and invokes it if available. If neither the bean definition nor the provider is found, it returns `null`. If the bean is found in its scope, it returns the bean. Otherwise, it initializes the bean definition, creates a new bean instance, registers it, wires dependencies, injects parameters, and invokes initialization methods before returning the bean.
codeFunctions: public < T > T getBean (final String name) { // Lookup for registered bean definition. BeanDefinition def = lookupBeanDefinition (name);if (def == null) { // try provider ProviderDefinition providerDefinition = providers.get (name);if (providerDefinition != null) { return (T) invokeProvider (providerDefinition);} return null;} // Find the bean in its scope Object bean = def.scopeLookup ();if (bean == null) { // Create new bean in the scope initBeanDefinition (def);final BeanData beanData = new BeanData (this,def);registerBeanAndWireAndInjectParamsAndInvokeInitMethods (beanData);bean = beanData.bean ();} return (T) bean;}

originalComment: Resolves and initializes bean definition.May be called multiple times.
codeComment:
The `initBeanDefinition` method initializes various properties of a `BeanDefinition` object. It checks if each property is null and, if so, resolves it using different resolvers or managers. The properties initialized include:

- `initMethods`: Resolved using `petiteResolvers.resolveInitMethodPoint(def.type)`.
- `destroyMethods`: Resolved using `petiteResolvers.resolveDestroyMethodPoint(def.type)`.
- `properties`: Resolved using `petiteResolvers.resolvePropertyInjectionPoint(def.type, def.wiringMode == WiringMode.AUTOWIRE)`.
- `methods`: Resolved using `petiteResolvers.resolveMethodInjectionPoint(def.type)`.
- `ctor`: Resolved using `petiteResolvers.resolveCtorInjectionPoint(def.type)`.
- `values`: Resolved using `paramManager.resolveParamInjectionPoints(def.type)`.
- `sets`: Resolved using `petiteResolvers.resolveSetInjectionPoint(def.type, def.wiringMode == WiringMode.AUTOWIRE)`.
- `params`: Filtered using `paramManager.filterParametersForBeanName(def.name, petiteConfig.getResolveReferenceParameters())`.

This method ensures that all necessary properties of the `BeanDefinition` are properly initialized before the bean is used.
codeFunctions: protected void initBeanDefinition (final BeanDefinition def) { // init methods if (def.initMethods == null) { def.initMethods = petiteResolvers.resolveInitMethodPoint (def.type);} // destroy methods if (def.destroyMethods == null) { def.destroyMethods = petiteResolvers.resolveDestroyMethodPoint (def.type);} // properties if (def.properties == null) { def.properties = petiteResolvers.resolvePropertyInjectionPoint (def.type,def.wiringMode == WiringMode.AUTOWIRE);} // methods if (def.methods == null) { def.methods = petiteResolvers.resolveMethodInjectionPoint (def.type);} // ctors if (def.ctor == null) { def.ctor = petiteResolvers.resolveCtorInjectionPoint (def.type);} // values if (def.values == null) { def.values = paramManager.resolveParamInjectionPoints (def.type);} // sets if (def.sets == null) { def.sets = petiteResolvers.resolveSetInjectionPoint (def.type,def.wiringMode == WiringMode.AUTOWIRE);} // params if (def.params == null) { def.params = paramManager.filterParametersForBeanName (def.name,petiteConfig.getResolveReferenceParameters ());} }

originalComment: Invokes provider to get a bean.
codeComment:
The `invokeProvider` method is designed to invoke a method on a bean or a static method, based on the `ProviderDefinition` object provided. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Check for Method**: The method first checks if the `provider.method` is not null.
2. **Determine Bean Type**:
   - If `provider.beanName` is not null, it retrieves the bean instance using `getBean(provider.beanName)`.
   - If `provider.beanName` is null, it assumes the method is static, and `bean` is set to null.
3. **Invoke Method**: The method attempts to invoke the specified method on the bean.
4. **Exception Handling**: If an exception occurs during the method invocation, it throws a `PetiteException` with a message indicating the invalid provider method.
5. **Invalid Provider**: If the `provider.method` is null, it throws a `PetiteException` indicating an invalid provider.
codeFunctions: protected Object invokeProvider (final ProviderDefinition provider) { if (provider.method != null) { final Object bean;if (provider.beanName != null) { // instance factory method bean = getBean (provider.beanName);} else { // static factory method bean = null;} try { return provider.method.invoke (bean);} catch (Exception ex) { throw new PetiteException ("Invalid provider method: " + provider.method.getName (),ex);} } throw new PetiteException ("Invalid provider");}

originalComment: Adds object instance to the container as singleton bean.
codeComment: This method, `addBean`, is responsible for adding a bean to a Petite container. It takes three parameters: `name` (a string representing the bean's name), `bean` (the object to be added), and `wiringMode` (the mode for wiring the bean). The method first resolves the wiring mode using the `petiteConfig` object. It then registers the bean with a singleton scope and the resolved wiring mode. After that, it looks up an existing bean definition with the given name and registers the bean, wires it, injects parameters, and invokes initialization methods.
codeFunctions: public void addBean (final String name,final Object bean,WiringMode wiringMode) { wiringMode = petiteConfig.resolveWiringMode (wiringMode);registerPetiteBean (bean.getClass (),name,SingletonScope.class,wiringMode,false,null);BeanDefinition def = lookupExistingBeanDefinition (name);registerBeanAndWireAndInjectParamsAndInvokeInitMethods (new BeanData (this,def,bean));}

originalComment: Sets petite bean property.
codeComment: The `setBeanProperty` method sets a property on a bean identified by a given name and value. It first parses the name to find the bean and then sets the property on that bean. If the bean is not found or an exception occurs during the property setting, it throws a `PetiteException`.
codeFunctions: public void setBeanProperty (final String name,final Object value) { Object bean = null;int ndx = name.length ();while (true) { ndx = name.lastIndexOf (' ',ndx);if (ndx == - 1) { break;} String beanName = name.substring (0,ndx);bean = getBean (beanName);if (bean != null) { break;} ndx --;} if (bean == null) { throw new PetiteException ("Invalid bean property: " + name);} try { BeanUtil.declared.setProperty (bean,name.substring (ndx + 1),value);} catch (Exception ex) { throw new PetiteException ("Invalid bean property: " + name,ex);} }

originalComment: Returns petite bean property value.
codeComment: This method retrieves a property value from a bean. It first checks if the input string contains a space to separate the bean name and the property name. If not, it throws an exception. It then extracts the bean name and attempts to retrieve the bean. If the bean is not found, it throws an exception. Finally, it uses `BeanUtil.declared.getProperty` to get the property value and handles any exceptions by throwing a `PetiteException`.
codeFunctions: public Object getBeanProperty (final String name) { int ndx = name.indexOf (' ');if (ndx == - 1) { throw new PetiteException ("Only bean name is specified, missing property name: " + name);} String beanName = name.substring (0,ndx);Object bean = getBean (beanName);if (bean == null) { throw new PetiteException ("Bean doesn't exist: " + name);} try { return BeanUtil.declared.getProperty (bean,name.substring (ndx + 1));} catch (Exception ex) { throw new PetiteException ("Invalid bean property: " + name,ex);} }

originalComment: Shutdowns container.After container is down it can t be used anymore.
codeComment: This method, `shutdown`, performs a series of cleanup operations to shut down a system or application. It iterates over a collection of `scopes` and calls the `shutdown` method on each `Scope` object. It then clears several caches and collections, including `externalsCache`, `beans`, `beansAlt`, `scopes`, `providers`, and `beanCollections`, to release resources and prepare the system for shutdown.

originalComment: Resolves method parameters from a method or constructor.Returns an empty array when target does not contain any parameter.No caching is involved in this process i.e.class bytecode is examined every time this method is called.
codeComment: The `resolveParameters` method takes an `AccessibleObject` (either a `Method` or a `Constructor`) and resolves its parameters. It first determines the parameter types, the declaring class, and the method name. If there are no parameters, it returns an empty array. It then attempts to read the class bytes using `ClassLoaderUtil` and processes them with a `ClassReader` and a `MethodFinder` visitor to extract the method parameters. If any I/O exceptions occur, it throws a `ParamoException`. Finally, it ensures the input stream is closed.
codeFunctions: public static MethodParameter [ ] resolveParameters (final AccessibleObject methodOrCtor) { Class [ ] paramTypes;Class declaringClass;String name;if (methodOrCtor instanceof Method) { Method method = (Method) methodOrCtor;paramTypes = method.getParameterTypes ();name = method.getName ();declaringClass = method.getDeclaringClass ();} else { Constructor constructor = (Constructor) methodOrCtor;paramTypes = constructor.getParameterTypes ();declaringClass = constructor.getDeclaringClass ();name = CTOR_METHOD;} if (paramTypes.length == 0) { return MethodParameter.EMPTY_ARRAY;} InputStream stream;try { stream = ClassLoaderUtil.getClassAsStream (declaringClass);} catch (IOException ioex) { throw new ParamoException ("Failed to read class bytes: " + declaringClass.getName (),ioex);} if (stream == null) { throw new ParamoException ("Class not found: " + declaringClass);} try { ClassReader reader = new ClassReader (stream);MethodFinder visitor = new MethodFinder (declaringClass,name,paramTypes);reader.accept (visitor,0);return visitor.getResolvedParameters ();} catch (IOException ioex) { throw new ParamoException (ioex);} finally { StreamUtil.close (stream);} }

originalComment: Performs smart form population.
codeComment:
This method, `doAfterBody`, is part of a JSP (JavaServer Pages) custom tag handler. It processes the body content of the tag, transforms it using the `populateForm` method, and writes the result to the output. Here's a summary of the steps:

1. **Retrieve Body Content**: It gets the `BodyContent` object, which contains the content between the start and end tags of the custom tag.
2. **Get Enclosing Writer**: It retrieves the `JspWriter` object that is used to write the output to the response.
3. **Transform Body Content**: It calls `populateForm` with the body content and a lambda expression that maps each name to its corresponding value using the `pageContext`.
4. **Write Output**: It attempts to write the transformed content to the output using `out.print`.
5. **Handle Exceptions**: If an `IOException` occurs during writing, it throws a `JspException` with the original exception as the cause.
6. **Return Control**: It returns `SKIP_BODY`, indicating that the body content should not be processed again.
codeFunctions: @ Override public int doAfterBody () throws JspException { BodyContent body = getBodyContent ();JspWriter out = body.getEnclosingWriter ();String bodytext = populateForm (body.getString (),name -> value (name,pageContext));try { out.print (bodytext);} catch (IOException ioex) { throw new JspException (ioex);} return SKIP_BODY;}

originalComment: Returns the property value with replaced macros.
codeComment: This method, `getValue`, takes a variable number of string arguments (`profiles`). It checks if `hasMacro` is true. If true, it resolves macros in the `value` using the `propsData.resolveMacros` method with the provided `profiles`. If `hasMacro` is false, it simply returns the `value`.
codeFunctions: public String getValue (final String ... profiles) { if (hasMacro) { return propsData.resolveMacros (value,profiles);} return value;}

originalComment: Finishes the tree building.Closes unclosed tags.
codeComment:
The `end` method performs several operations to finalize the parsing of an HTML document:

1. **Unclosed Tag Handling**: It checks if the current node (`parentNode`) is not the root node. If not, it iterates through the parent nodes to the root. If implied end tags are enabled in the configuration and the current node's tag should be implicitly closed, it moves to the parent node. Otherwise, it logs an error for an unclosed tag and moves to the parent node.

2. **Whitespace Removal**: If ignoring whitespaces between tags is enabled, it removes the last child node if it is an empty text node.

3. **Foster Rules Application**: If foster rules are enabled, it applies these rules to fix foster elements in the document.

4. **Root Node Finalization**: It calls the `end` method on the root node to finalize its processing.

5. **Logging**: If debugging is enabled, it logs the time taken to create the DOM tree.
codeFunctions: @ Override public void end () { if (parentNode != rootNode) { Node thisNode = parentNode;while (thisNode != rootNode) { if (domBuilder.config.isImpliedEndTags ()) { if (implRules.implicitlyCloseTagOnEOF (thisNode.getNodeName ())) { thisNode = thisNode.getParentNode ();continue;} } error ("Unclosed tag closed: <" + thisNode.getNodeName () + ">");thisNode = thisNode.getParentNode ();} } // remove whitespaces if (domBuilder.config.isIgnoreWhitespacesBetweenTags ()) { removeLastChildNodeIfEmptyText (parentNode,true);} // foster if (domBuilder.config.isUseFosterRules ()) { HtmlFosterRules fosterRules = new HtmlFosterRules ();fosterRules.fixFosterElements (rootNode);} // elapsed rootNode.end ();if (log.isDebugEnabled ()) { log.debug ("LagartoDom tree created in " + rootNode.getElapsedTime () + " ms");} }

originalComment: Creates new element with correct configuration.
codeComment: The `createElementNode` method creates an `Element` object based on the provided `Tag`. It first checks if there are any void tags defined by `htmlVoidRules`. If so, it determines if the given tag is a void tag and whether it should be self-closed based on the configuration. If no void tags are defined, it directly checks the configuration for self-closing behavior. Finally, it returns a new `Element` object initialized with the root node, the tag, and the determined void and self-closing statuses.
codeFunctions: protected Element createElementNode (final Tag tag) { boolean hasVoidTags = htmlVoidRules != null;boolean isVoid = false;boolean selfClosed = false;if (hasVoidTags) { isVoid = htmlVoidRules.isVoidTag (tag.getName ());// HTML and XHTML if (isVoid) { // it's void tag, lookup the flag selfClosed = domBuilder.config.isSelfCloseVoidTags ();} } else { // XML, no voids, lookup the flag selfClosed = domBuilder.config.isSelfCloseVoidTags ();} return new Element (rootNode,tag,isVoid,selfClosed);}

originalComment: Visits tags.
codeComment: This method processes a given `Tag` object and updates the DOM structure accordingly based on the tag type (START, END, or SELF_CLOSING). It handles configurations like ignoring whitespaces between tags and implied end tags. The method ensures that the DOM tree is correctly built by managing parent-child relationships and handling unclosed tags appropriately.
codeFunctions: @ Override public void tag (final Tag tag) { if (!enabled) { return;} TagType tagType = tag.getType ();Element node;switch (tagType) { case START:if (domBuilder.config.isIgnoreWhitespacesBetweenTags ()) { removeLastChildNodeIfEmptyText (parentNode,false);} node = createElementNode (tag);if (domBuilder.config.isImpliedEndTags ()) { while (true) { String parentNodeName = parentNode.getNodeName ();if (!implRules.implicitlyCloseParentTagOnNewTag (parentNodeName,node.getNodeName ())) { break;} parentNode = parentNode.getParentNode ();if (log.isDebugEnabled ()) { log.debug ("Implicitly closed tag <" + node.getNodeName () + "> ");} } } parentNode.addChild (node);if (!node.isVoidElement ()) { parentNode = node;} break;case END:if (domBuilder.config.isIgnoreWhitespacesBetweenTags ()) { removeLastChildNodeIfEmptyText (parentNode,true);} String tagName = tag.getName ().toString ();Node matchingParent = findMatchingParentOpenTag (tagName);if (matchingParent == parentNode) { // regular situation parentNode = parentNode.getParentNode ();break;} if (matchingParent == null) { // matching open tag not found, remove it error ("Orphan closed tag ignored: </" + tagName + "> " + tag.getTagPosition ());break;} // try to close it implicitly if (domBuilder.config.isImpliedEndTags ()) { boolean fixed = false;while (implRules.implicitlyCloseParentTagOnTagEnd (parentNode.getNodeName (),tagName)) { parentNode = parentNode.getParentNode ();if (log.isDebugEnabled ()) { log.debug ("Implicitly closed tag <" + tagName + ">");} if (parentNode == matchingParent) { parentNode = matchingParent.parentNode;fixed = true;break;} } if (fixed) { break;} } // matching tag found, but it is not a regular situation // therefore close all unclosed tags in between fixUnclosedTagsUpToMatchingParent (tag,matchingParent);break;case SELF_CLOSING:if (domBuilder.config.isIgnoreWhitespacesBetweenTags ()) { removeLastChildNodeIfEmptyText (parentNode,false);} node = createElementNode (tag);parentNode.addChild (node);break;} }

originalComment: Removes last child node if contains just empty text.
codeComment: This method, `removeLastChildNodeIfEmptyText`, checks if the last child node of a given parent node is a text node and if it is blank. If the text node is blank, it detaches it from the parent node. The method also includes a condition to prevent removing the last child node if the parent node has only one child and a closed tag is specified.
codeFunctions: protected void removeLastChildNodeIfEmptyText (final Node parentNode,final boolean closedTag) { if (parentNode == null) { return;} Node lastChild = parentNode.getLastChild ();if (lastChild == null) { return;} if (lastChild.getNodeType () != Node.NodeType.TEXT) { return;} if (closedTag) { if (parentNode.getChildNodesCount () == 1) { return;} } Text text = (Text) lastChild;if (text.isBlank ()) { lastChild.detachFromParent ();} }

originalComment: Returns the query string.
codeComment: The `getQueryString` method constructs a query string by replacing placeholders (`?`) in the `sqlTemplate` with corresponding values from the `parameterValues` list. If `sqlTemplate` is null, it returns the string representation of the object. If `parameterValues` is null, it returns the `sqlTemplate` as is. The method uses a `StringBuilder` to efficiently build the final query string, handling cases where the number of placeholders does not match the number of values gracefully. If an error occurs during the process, it appends an error message to the query string.
codeFunctions: public String getQueryString () { if (sqlTemplate == null) { return toString ();} if (parameterValues == null) { return sqlTemplate;} final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder ();int qMarkCount = 0;final StringTokenizer tok = new StringTokenizer (sqlTemplate + ' ',"?");while (tok.hasMoreTokens ()) { final String oneChunk = tok.nextToken ();sb.append (oneChunk);try { Object value = null;if (parameterValues.size () > 1 + qMarkCount) { value = parameterValues.get (1 + qMarkCount);qMarkCount ++;} else { if (!tok.hasMoreTokens ()) { value = "";} } if (value == null) { value = "?";} sb.append (value);} catch (Throwable th) { sb.append ("--- Building query failed: ").append (th.toString ());} } return sb.toString ().trim ();}

originalComment: Returns correct action class name.Detects Proxetta classes.
codeComment: This method, `getActionClassName`, takes an `Object` named `action` as input and returns the fully qualified name of the class associated with that object. It first retrieves the class of the `action` object using `getClass()`. If the object is a proxy, it resolves the target class using `ProxettaUtil.resolveTargetClass(clazz)`. Finally, it returns the name of the class using `clazz.getName()`.
codeFunctions: protected String getActionClassName (final Object action) { Class clazz = action.getClass ();clazz = ProxettaUtil.resolveTargetClass (clazz);return clazz.getName ();}

originalComment: Calculates TO.
codeComment: This method calculates the end index (`to`) for a range starting from a given index (`from`) with a specified count of elements (`count`). If `count` is not `-1`, it adds `count` to `from` to determine `to`. If `to` exceeds the given size, it sets `to` to the size. The method returns the calculated `to` value.
codeFunctions: protected int calculateTo (final int from,final int count,final int size) { int to = size;if (count != - 1) { to = from + count;if (to > size) { to = size;} } return to;}

originalComment: Iterates collection.
codeComment: The `iterateCollection` method is designed to iterate over a given collection, starting from a specified index (`from`) and iterating for a specified number of elements (`count`). It uses a `PageContext` to manage the iteration context and a `JspFragment` to handle the body content of the iteration. The method calculates the end index (`to`) based on the starting index and the count, ensuring it does not exceed the collection's size. During iteration, it sets the current item in the specified scope and invokes the body content for each item within the specified range.
codeFunctions: protected void iterateCollection (final Collection collection,final int from,final int count,final PageContext pageContext) throws JspException { JspFragment body = getJspBody ();Iterator iter = collection.iterator ();int i = 0;int to = calculateTo (from,count,collection.size ());while (i < to) { Object item = iter.next ();if (i >= from) { if (status != null) { iteratorStatus.next (!iter.hasNext ());} TagUtil.setScopeAttribute (var,item,scope,pageContext);TagUtil.invokeBody (body);} i ++;} }

originalComment: Iterates arrays.
codeComment:
This method, `iterateArray`, is designed to iterate over a portion of an array and execute a JSP body for each element within that portion. Here's a summary of its functionality:

1. **Parameters**:
   - `array`: The array to iterate over.
   - `from`: The starting index for the iteration.
   - `count`: The number of elements to iterate over.
   - `pageContext`: The current JSP page context.

2. **Initialization**:
   - Retrieves the JSP body content using `getJspBody()`.
   - Calculates the length of the array.
   - Determines the end index (`to`) of the iteration using `calculateTo(from, count, len)`.
   - Sets `last` to the last index of the iteration (`to - 1`).

3. **Iteration**:
   - Loops through the array from the `from` index to the `to` index.
   - For each element, it:
     - Retrieves the element (`item`).
     - If `status` is not null, updates the iterator status.
     - Sets the `item` as a scoped attribute in the `pageContext`.
     - Invokes the JSP body content.

4. **Exception Handling**:
   - Throws a `JspException` if any JSP-related error occurs during execution.
codeFunctions: protected void iterateArray (final Object [ ] array,final int from,final int count,final PageContext pageContext) throws JspException { JspFragment body = getJspBody ();int len = array.length;int to = calculateTo (from,count,len);int last = to - 1;for (int i = from;i < to;i ++) { Object item = array [ i ];if (status != null) { iteratorStatus.next (i == last);} TagUtil.setScopeAttribute (var,item,scope,pageContext);TagUtil.invokeBody (body);} }

originalComment: Replaces all occurrences of a certain pattern in a string with a replacement string.This is the fastest replace function known to author.
codeComment: The `replace` method takes three parameters: a string `s`, a substring `sub`, and a replacement string `with`. It replaces all occurrences of `sub` in `s` with `with`. If `sub` is empty, it returns the original string `s`. The method uses a `StringBuilder` to efficiently build the resulting string. It iterates through `s`, appending parts of `s` and the replacement string `with` to the `StringBuilder` until all occurrences of `sub` are replaced. Finally, it returns the modified string.
codeFunctions: public static String replace (final String s,final String sub,final String with) { if (sub.isEmpty ()) { return s;} int c = 0;int i = s.indexOf (sub,c);if (i == - 1) { return s;} int length = s.length ();StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (length + with.length ());do { sb.append (s,c,i);sb.append (with);c = i + sub.length ();} while ((i = s.indexOf (sub,c)) != - 1);if (c < length) { sb.append (s,c,length);} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Replaces all occurrences of a character in a string.
codeComment: The `replaceChar` method takes a string `s`, a character `sub`, and a character `with` as input. It searches for the first occurrence of `sub` in `s`. If `sub` is not found, it returns the original string `s`. Otherwise, it converts the string to a character array, iterates through the array starting from the index where `sub` was found, and replaces every occurrence of `sub` with `with`. Finally, it returns the modified string.
codeFunctions: public static String replaceChar (final String s,final char sub,final char with) { int startIndex = s.indexOf (sub);if (startIndex == - 1) { return s;} char [ ] str = s.toCharArray ();for (int i = startIndex;i < str.length;i ++) { if (str [ i ] == sub) { str [ i ] = with;} } return new String (str);}

originalComment: Replaces all occurrences of a characters in a string.
codeComment: The `replaceChars` method takes a string `s` and two character arrays `sub` and `with`. It converts the string into a character array and iterates through each character. If a character in the string matches any character in the `sub` array, it replaces it with the corresponding character from the `with` array. Finally, it returns the modified string.
codeFunctions: public static String replaceChars (final String s,final char [ ] sub,final char [ ] with) { char [ ] str = s.toCharArray ();for (int i = 0;i < str.length;i ++) { char c = str [ i ];for (int j = 0;j < sub.length;j ++) { if (c == sub [ j ]) { str [ i ] = with [ j ];break;} } } return new String (str);}

originalComment: Replaces the very first occurrence of a substring with supplied string.
codeComment: The `replaceFirst` method takes three parameters: a string `s`, a substring `sub`, and a replacement string `with`. It finds the first occurrence of `sub` in `s`. If `sub` is not found, it returns the original string `s`. Otherwise, it constructs a new string by replacing the first occurrence of `sub` with `with` and returns the result.
codeFunctions: public static String replaceFirst (final String s,final String sub,final String with) { int i = s.indexOf (sub);if (i == - 1) { return s;} return s.substring (0,i) + with + s.substring (i + sub.length ());}

originalComment: Replaces the very first occurrence of a character in a string.
codeComment: The `replaceFirst` method takes a string `s`, a character `sub`, and a character `with` as input. It finds the first occurrence of `sub` in `s`. If `sub` is not found, it returns the original string `s`. If `sub` is found, it replaces the first occurrence of `sub` with `with` and returns the modified string.
codeFunctions: public static String replaceFirst (final String s,final char sub,final char with) { int index = s.indexOf (sub);if (index == - 1) { return s;} char [ ] str = s.toCharArray ();str [ index ] = with;return new String (str);}

originalComment: Replaces the very last occurrence of a substring with supplied string.
codeComment: The `replaceLast` method replaces the last occurrence of a specified substring within a given string with another substring. It first finds the last index of the substring to be replaced. If the substring is not found, it returns the original string. Otherwise, it constructs a new string by concatenating the part of the original string before the last occurrence of the substring, the replacement substring, and the part of the original string after the last occurrence of the substring.
codeFunctions: public static String replaceLast (final String s,final String sub,final String with) { int i = s.lastIndexOf (sub);if (i == - 1) { return s;} return s.substring (0,i) + with + s.substring (i + sub.length ());}

originalComment: Replaces the very last occurrence of a character in a string.
codeComment: This method, `replaceLast`, takes a string `s`, a character `sub`, and a character `with` as input. It finds the last occurrence of `sub` in `s` and replaces it with `with`. If `sub` is not found, it returns the original string `s`.
codeFunctions: public static String replaceLast (final String s,final char sub,final char with) { int index = s.lastIndexOf (sub);if (index == - 1) { return s;} char [ ] str = s.toCharArray ();str [ index ] = with;return new String (str);}

originalComment: Removes all substring occurrences from the string.
codeComment: The method `remove` takes two strings, `s` and `sub`, and returns a new string with all occurrences of `sub` removed from `s`. It initializes a counter `c` to track the current position in `s` and calculates the length of `sub`. If `sub` is an empty string, it returns `s` as is. It then finds the first occurrence of `sub` in `s` starting from position `c`. If `sub` is not found, it returns `s`. Otherwise, it uses a `StringBuilder` to construct the result by appending parts of `s` that do not contain `sub`. It continues this process until all occurrences of `sub` are removed, and finally returns the resulting string.
codeFunctions: public static String remove (final String s,final String sub) { int c = 0;int sublen = sub.length ();if (sublen == 0) { return s;} int i = s.indexOf (sub,c);if (i == - 1) { return s;} StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (s.length ());do { sb.append (s,c,i);c = i + sublen;} while ((i = s.indexOf (sub,c)) != - 1);if (c < s.length ()) { sb.append (s,c,s.length ());} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Removes a single character from string.
codeComment: The method `remove` takes a string and a character as input and returns a new string with all occurrences of the specified character removed. It iterates through the input string, copying characters to a new character array except for the specified character. If no characters are removed, it returns the original string. Otherwise, it constructs and returns a new string from the character array up to the offset where the last valid character was copied.
codeFunctions: public static String remove (final String string,final char ch) { int stringLen = string.length ();char [ ] result = new char [ stringLen ];int offset = 0;for (int i = 0;i < stringLen;i ++) { char c = string.charAt (i);if (c == ch) { continue;} result [ offset ] = c;offset ++;} if (offset == stringLen) { return string;// no changes } return new String (result,0,offset);}

originalComment: Determines if string array contains empty strings.

originalComment: Converts an array object to array of strings where every element of input array is converted to a string.If input is not an array the result will still be an array with one element.
codeComment:
The `toStringArray` method converts a given object into a string array. If the object is `null`, it returns an empty string array. If the object is not an array, it returns a string array containing the string representation of the object. If the object is an array, it checks the component type of the array:

- If the component type is a primitive type (int, long, double, float, boolean, short, byte), it uses the corresponding `ArraysUtil.toStringArray` method to convert the array to a string array.

If the component type is an unsupported primitive type, it throws an `IllegalArgumentException`.

originalComment: Internal method for changing the first character case.
codeComment: This method, `changeFirstCharacterCase`, takes a boolean `capitalize` and a string `string` as parameters. It checks if the string is empty and returns it unchanged if so. Otherwise, it modifies the case of the first character based on the `capitalize` flag. Otherwise, it creates a new string with the modified first character and returns it.
codeFunctions: private static String changeFirstCharacterCase (final boolean capitalize,final String string) { int strLen = string.length ();if (strLen == 0) { return string;} char ch = string.charAt (0);char modifiedCh;if (capitalize) { modifiedCh = Character.toUpperCase (ch);} else { modifiedCh = Character.toLowerCase (ch);} if (modifiedCh == ch) { // no change, return unchanged string return string;} char [ ] chars = string.toCharArray ();chars [ 0 ] = modifiedCh;return new String (chars);}

originalComment: Makes a title - cased string from given input.
codeComment: The `title` method takes a string as input and converts it to title case. It iterates through each character of the string, checking if it is a whitespace. If a character is not a whitespace and the previous character was a whitespace, it converts the character to uppercase. Otherwise, it converts the character to lowercase. The method returns the modified string.
codeFunctions: public static String title (final String string) { char [ ] chars = string.toCharArray ();boolean wasWhitespace = true;for (int i = 0;i < chars.length;i ++) { char c = chars [ i ];if (CharUtil.isWhitespace (c)) { wasWhitespace = true;} else { if (wasWhitespace) { chars [ i ] = Character.toUpperCase (c);} else { chars [ i ] = Character.toLowerCase (c);} wasWhitespace = false;} } return new String (chars);}

originalComment: Compress multiple occurrences of given char into one appearance.
codeComment: The `compressChars` method takes a string `s` and a character `c` as input. It iterates through the string, appending characters to a `StringBuilder` while skipping consecutive occurrences of the specified character `c`. If the resulting string has the same length as the original, it returns the original string; otherwise, it returns the compressed string.
codeFunctions: public static String compressChars (final String s,final char c) { int len = s.length ();StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (len);boolean wasChar = false;for (int i = 0;i < len;i ++) { char c1 = s.charAt (i);if (c1 == c) { if (wasChar) { continue;} wasChar = true;} else { wasChar = false;} sb.append (c1);} if (sb.length () == len) { return s;} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Tests if this string starts with the specified prefix with ignored case and with the specified prefix beginning a specified index.
codeComment: This method checks if a given string `src` starts with a specified substring `subS` at a given index `startIndex`, ignoring case differences. It converts both the substring and the relevant part of the source string to lowercase and compares them character by character. If all characters match, it returns `true`; otherwise, it returns `false`.
codeFunctions: public static boolean startsWithIgnoreCase (final String src,final String subS,final int startIndex) { String sub = subS.toLowerCase ();int sublen = sub.length ();if (startIndex + sublen > src.length ()) { return false;} int j = 0;int i = startIndex;while (j < sublen) { char source = Character.toLowerCase (src.charAt (i));if (sub.charAt (j) != source) { return false;} j ++;i ++;} return true;}

originalComment: Returns if string ends with provided character.
codeComment: The method `endsWithChar` checks if a given string `s` ends with a specified character `c`. It returns `false` if the string is empty; otherwise, it compares the last character of the string with `c` and returns the result of this comparison.

originalComment: Count substring occurrences in a source string ignoring case.
codeComment: This method, `countIgnoreCase`, counts the number of times a substring `sub` appears in a string `source`, ignoring case differences. It initializes a count to zero and iterates through the `source` string, using a helper method `indexOfIgnoreCase` to find the index of each occurrence of `sub`. If an occurrence is found, it increments the count and updates the starting index for the next search. The process continues until no more occurrences are found, at which point the method returns the total count. If the substring is empty, the method immediately returns zero.
codeFunctions: public static int countIgnoreCase (final String source,final String sub) { int count = 0;int j = 0;int sublen = sub.length ();if (sublen == 0) { return 0;} while (true) { int i = indexOfIgnoreCase (source,sub,j);if (i == - 1) { break;} count ++;j = i + sublen;} return count;}

originalComment: Compares two string arrays.
codeComment: This method checks if two string arrays are equal, ignoring case differences. It first compares the lengths of the arrays; if they differ, it returns false. Then, it iterates through each element of the arrays, comparing them using the `equalsIgnoreCase` method. If any pair of elements are not equal (ignoring case), it returns false. If all elements are equal, it returns true.
codeFunctions: public static boolean equalsIgnoreCase (final String [ ] as,final String [ ] as1) { if (as.length != as1.length) { return false;} for (int i = 0;i < as.length;i ++) { if (!as [ i ].equalsIgnoreCase (as1 [ i ])) { return false;} } return true;}

originalComment: Returns first index of a whitespace character starting from specified index offset.
codeComment: This method, `indexOfWhitespace`, searches for the first occurrence of a whitespace character within a specified substring of a given string. It takes three parameters: the string to search (`string`), the starting index of the substring (`startindex`), and the ending index of the substring (`endindex`). The method iterates through the characters in the substring, checking each one to see if it is a whitespace character using the `CharUtil.isWhitespace` method. If a whitespace character is found, the method returns its index. If no whitespace character is found by the end of the loop, the method returns -1.
codeFunctions: public static int indexOfWhitespace (final String string,final int startindex,final int endindex) { for (int i = startindex;i < endindex;i ++) { if (CharUtil.isWhitespace (string.charAt (i))) { return i;} } return - 1;}

originalComment: Strips leading char if string starts with one.
codeComment: This method, `stripLeadingChar`, takes a string and a character as input. It checks if the string is not empty and if the first character of the string matches the given character. If both conditions are met, it returns a new string that is the original string without the leading character. If the conditions are not met, it returns the original string unchanged.
codeFunctions: public static String stripLeadingChar (final String string,final char c) { if (string.length () > 0) { if (string.charAt (0) == c) { return string.substring (1);} } return string;}

originalComment: Strips trailing char if string ends with one.

codeFunctions: public static String stripTrailingChar (final String string,final char c) { if (string.length () > 0) { if (string.charAt (string.length () - 1) == c) { return string.substring (0,string.length () - 1);} } return string;}

originalComment: Strips leading and trailing char from given string.
codeComment: The `stripChar` method removes leading and trailing occurrences of a specified character `c` from a given string. If the string is empty or contains only the character `c`, it returns an empty string. Otherwise, it trims the character from both ends and returns the modified string.
codeFunctions: public static String stripChar (final String string,final char c) { if (string.length () == 0) { return string;} if (string.length () == 1) { if (string.charAt (0) == c) { return StringPool.EMPTY;} return string;} int left = 0;int right = string.length ();if (string.charAt (left) == c) { left ++;} if (string.charAt (right - 1) == c) { right --;} return string.substring (left,right);}

originalComment: Strips everything up to the first appearance of given char.Character IS included in the returned string.
codeComment: The `stripToChar` method takes a string and a character as input. It finds the index of the first occurrence of the character in the string. codeFunctions: public static String stripToChar (final String string,final char c) { int ndx = string.indexOf (c);if (ndx == - 1) { return string;} return string.substring (ndx);}

originalComment: Crops all elements of string array.

codeFunctions: public static void cropAll (final String ... strings) { for (int i = 0;i < strings.length;i ++) { String string = strings [ i ];if (string != null) { string = crop (strings [ i ]);} strings [ i ] = string;} }

originalComment: Trim whitespaces from the left.
codeComment: The `trimLeft` method removes leading whitespace characters from a given string. If any leading whitespace is found, it returns a substring starting from the first non-whitespace character; otherwise, it returns the original string.
codeFunctions: public static String trimLeft (final String src) { int len = src.length ();int st = 0;while ((st < len) && (CharUtil.isWhitespace (src.charAt (st)))) { st ++;} return st > 0?src.substring (st):src;}

originalComment: Trim whitespaces from the right.
codeComment: The `trimRight` method removes trailing whitespace characters from a given string. It iterates from the end of the string towards the beginning, decrementing the length counter as long as it encounters whitespace characters. If the length counter is less than the original length of the string, it returns a substring from the start to the new length; otherwise, it returns the original string.
codeFunctions: public static String trimRight (final String src) { int len = src.length ();int count = len;while ((len > 0) && (CharUtil.isWhitespace (src.charAt (len - 1)))) { len --;} return (len < count)?src.substring (0,len):src;}

originalComment: Returns indexes of the first region without escaping character.
codeComment: This method, `indexOfRegion`, takes a string and two boundary strings (`leftBoundary` and `rightBoundary`) along with an offset. It searches for the first occurrence of `leftBoundary` starting from the given offset, then finds the first occurrence of `rightBoundary` after the `leftBoundary`. If either boundary is not found, it returns `null`. Otherwise, it returns an array of four integers representing the start and end indices of the `leftBoundary` and `rightBoundary` within the string.
codeFunctions: public static int [ ] indexOfRegion (final String string,final String leftBoundary,final String rightBoundary,final int offset) { int ndx = offset;int [ ] res = new int [ 4 ];ndx = string.indexOf (leftBoundary,ndx);if (ndx == - 1) { return null;} res [ 0 ] = ndx;ndx += leftBoundary.length ();res [ 1 ] = ndx;ndx = string.indexOf (rightBoundary,ndx);if (ndx == - 1) { return null;} res [ 2 ] = ndx;res [ 3 ] = ndx + rightBoundary.length ();return res;}

originalComment: Joins an collection of objects into one string with separator.
codeComment: This method joins elements of a collection into a single string, separated by a specified character. If the collection is null, it returns null. codeFunctions: public static String join (final Collection collection,final char separator) { if (collection == null) { return null;} if (collection.size () == 0) { return StringPool.EMPTY;} final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (collection.size () * 16);final Iterator it = collection.iterator ();for (int i = 0;i < collection.size ();i ++) { if (i > 0) { sb.append (separator);} sb.append (it.next ());} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Joins an array of objects into one string with separator.

codeFunctions: public static String join (final Object [ ] array,final String separator) { if (array == null) { return null;} if (array.length == 0) { return StringPool.EMPTY;} if (array.length == 1) { return String.valueOf (array [ 0 ]);} final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (array.length * 16);for (int i = 0;i < array.length;i ++) { if (i > 0) { sb.append (separator);} sb.append (array [ i ]);} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Converts string charset.If charset names are the same the same string is returned.

originalComment: Surrounds the string with provided prefix and suffix if such missing from string.
codeComment: The `surround` method takes a string and two additional strings, a prefix and a suffix. codeFunctions: public static String surround (String string,final String prefix,final String suffix) { if (!string.startsWith (prefix)) { string = prefix + string;} if (!string.endsWith (suffix)) { string += suffix;} return string;}

originalComment: Cuts the string from beginning to the first index of provided substring.

originalComment: Cuts prefix if exists.

originalComment: Removes surrounding prefix and suffixes.
codeComment: The `cutSurrounding` method removes a specified prefix and suffix from a given string. It first checks if the string starts with the specified prefix and adjusts the starting index accordingly. Then, it checks if the string ends with the specified suffix and adjusts the ending index. If the adjusted ending index is less than or equal to the starting index, it returns an empty string. Otherwise, it returns the substring of the original string, excluding the prefix and suffix.
codeFunctions: public static String cutSurrounding (final String string,final String prefix,final String suffix) { int start = 0;int end = string.length ();if (string.startsWith (prefix)) { start = prefix.length ();} if (string.endsWith (suffix)) { end -= suffix.length ();} if (end <= start) { return StringPool.EMPTY;} return string.substring (start,end);}

originalComment: Inserts a string on provided offset.
codeComment: This method inserts a specified string into another string at a given offset. If the offset is negative, it is set to 0. The method uses a `StringBuilder` to perform the insertion and returns the resulting string.
codeFunctions: public static String insert (final String src,final String insert,int offset) { if (offset < 0) { offset = 0;} if (offset > src.length ()) { offset = src.length ();} StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (src);sb.insert (offset,insert);return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Creates a new string that contains the provided string a number of times.

codeFunctions: public static String repeat (final String source,int count) { StringBand result = new StringBand (count);while (count > 0) { result.append (source);count --;} return result.toString ();}

originalComment: Reverse a string.
codeComment: The `reverse` method takes a string `s` as input and returns a new string that is the reverse of `s`. codeFunctions: public static String reverse (final String s) { StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder (s.length ());for (int i = s.length () - 1;i >= 0;i --) { result.append (s.charAt (i));} return result.toString ();}

originalComment: Returns max common prefix of two strings.
codeComment: The `maxCommonPrefix` method finds the longest common prefix between two input strings. It first determines the minimum length of the two strings to avoid index out-of-bounds errors. It then iterates through each character of the strings up to this minimum length, comparing characters at the same position in both strings. If a mismatch is found, the loop breaks. Otherwise, matching characters are appended to a `StringBuilder`. Finally, the method returns the common prefix as a string.
codeFunctions: public static String maxCommonPrefix (final String one,final String two) { final int minLength = Math.min (one.length (),two.length ());final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (minLength);for (int pos = 0;pos < minLength;pos ++) { final char currentChar = one.charAt (pos);if (currentChar != two.charAt (pos)) { break;} sb.append (currentChar);} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Finds common prefix for several strings.Returns an empty string if arguments do not have a common prefix.
codeComment: The method `findCommonPrefix` takes a variable number of strings as input and finds the longest common prefix among them. It uses a `StringBuilder` to build the prefix and iterates through each character position across all strings. If a character mismatch is found or if the end of any string is reached, the loop breaks. The method returns the common prefix as a string, or an empty string if no common prefix exists.
codeFunctions: public static String findCommonPrefix (final String ... strings) { StringBuilder prefix = new StringBuilder ();int index = 0;char c = 0;loop:while (true) { for (int i = 0;i < strings.length;i ++) { String s = strings [ i ];if (index == s.length ()) { break loop;} if (i == 0) { c = s.charAt (index);} else { if (s.charAt (index) != c) { break loop;} } } index ++;prefix.append (c);} return prefix.length () == 0?StringPool.EMPTY:prefix.toString ();}

originalComment: Shorten string to given length.
codeComment: The `shorten` method takes a string `s`, an integer `length`, and a string `suffix`. It shortens the string `s` to the specified `length` by removing characters from the end and appending the `suffix`. If the string `s` is longer than the specified `length`, the method looks for the last whitespace character within the `length` limit to ensure the shortened string ends at a word boundary. If no whitespace is found, it simply truncates the string. The method then returns the shortened string concatenated with the `suffix`.
codeFunctions: public static String shorten (String s,int length,final String suffix) { length -= suffix.length ();if (s.length () > length) { for (int j = length;j >= 0;j --) { if (CharUtil.isWhitespace (s.charAt (j))) { length = j;break;} } String temp = s.substring (0,length);s = temp.concat (suffix);} return s;}

originalComment: Converts all of the characters in the string to upper case based on the locale.
codeComment: The `toUpperCase` method converts a given string `s` to uppercase using a specified `Locale`. If the string is `null`, it returns `null`. It iterates through each character of the string. If a non-ASCII character is found, it falls back to using the `toUpperCase` method of the `String` class with the specified or default locale. For ASCII characters, it manually converts lowercase letters to uppercase by adjusting their ASCII values. If no non-ASCII characters are found and no changes are made, it returns the original string. Otherwise, it returns the modified string.
codeFunctions: public static String toUpperCase (final String s,Locale locale) { if (s == null) { return null;} StringBuilder sb = null;for (int i = 0;i < s.length ();i ++) { char c = s.charAt (i);if (c > 127) { // found non-ascii char, fallback to the slow unicode detection if (locale == null) { locale = Locale.getDefault ();} return s.toUpperCase (locale);} if ((c >= ' ') && (c <= ' ')) { if (sb == null) { sb = new StringBuilder (s);} sb.setCharAt (i,(char) (c - 32));} } if (sb == null) { return s;} return sb.toString ();}

codeFunctions: public static String removeQuotes (final String string) { if ((startsWithChar (string,' ') && endsWithChar (string,' ')) || (startsWithChar (string,' ') && endsWithChar (string,' ')) || (startsWithChar (string,' ') && endsWithChar (string,' '))) { return substring (string,1,- 1);} return string;}

originalComment: Converts bytes to hex string.

It then iterates over each byte in the input array, converting each byte into two hexadecimal characters and storing them in the `chars` array.
