codeFunctions: private void fetchSystemCounters (PerformanceCountersHolder countersHolder) { //go through all threads and accumulate statistic only for live threads //all dead threads will be removed and statistics from them will be //later accumulated in #deadThreadsStatistic field, then result statistic from this field //will be aggregated to countersHolder //To decrease inter thread communication delay we fetch snapshots first //and only after that we aggregate data from immutable snapshots final Collection < ORawPair < Thread,PerformanceSnapshot > > snapshots = new ArrayList <> (statistics.size ());final Collection < Thread > threadsToRemove = new ArrayList <> ();for (Map.Entry < Thread,OSessionStoragePerformanceStatistic > entry:statistics.entrySet ()) { final Thread thread = entry.getKey ();final OSessionStoragePerformanceStatistic statistic = entry.getValue ();snapshots.add (new ORawPair <> (thread,statistic.getSnapshot ()));} for (ORawPair < Thread,PerformanceSnapshot > pair:snapshots) { final Thread thread = pair.getFirst ();if (thread.isAlive ()) { final PerformanceSnapshot snapshot = pair.getSecond ();snapshot.performanceCountersHolder.pushData (countersHolder);} else { threadsToRemove.add (thread);} } if (!threadsToRemove.isEmpty ()) { updateDeadThreadsStatistic (threadsToRemove);} final ImmutableStatistic ds = deadThreadsStatistic;if (ds != null) { final PerformanceCountersHolder dch = ds.countersHolder;dch.pushData (countersHolder);} }

codeComment: The `fetchComponentCounters` method processes performance statistics for a specified component across all threads. codeFunctions: private void fetchComponentCounters (String componentName,PerformanceCountersHolder componentCountersHolder) { //go through all threads and accumulate statistic only for live threads //all dead threads will be removed and statistics from them will be //later accumulated in #deadThreadsStatistic field, then result statistic from this field //will be aggregated to componentCountersHolder //To decrease inter thread communication delay we fetch snapshots first //and only after that we aggregate data from immutable snapshots final Collection < ORawPair < Thread,PerformanceSnapshot > > snapshots = new ArrayList <> (statistics.size ());final List < Thread > threadsToRemove = new ArrayList <> ();for (Map.Entry < Thread,OSessionStoragePerformanceStatistic > entry:statistics.entrySet ()) { final Thread thread = entry.getKey ();final OSessionStoragePerformanceStatistic statistic = entry.getValue ();snapshots.add (new ORawPair <> (thread,statistic.getSnapshot ()));} for (ORawPair < Thread,PerformanceSnapshot > pair:snapshots) { final Thread thread = pair.getFirst ();if (thread.isAlive ()) { final PerformanceSnapshot snapshot = pair.getSecond ();final PerformanceCountersHolder holder = snapshot.countersByComponent.get (componentName);if (holder != null) holder.pushData (componentCountersHolder);} else { threadsToRemove.add (thread);} } if (!threadsToRemove.isEmpty ()) { updateDeadThreadsStatistic (threadsToRemove);} final ImmutableStatistic ds = deadThreadsStatistic;if (ds != null) { final PerformanceCountersHolder dch = ds.countersByComponents.get (componentName);if (dch != null) { dch.pushData (componentCountersHolder);} } }

originalComment: Computes the quorum response if possible by returning true and setting the field quorumResponse with the ODistributedResponse.
codeComment: The `computeQuorumResponse` method determines if a quorum response has been reached in a distributed system. It first checks if the quorum response has already been computed. If not, it processes the responses based on whether they are grouped by result or not. For grouped responses, it checks if any group meets the quorum size and if the nodes in the group concur. If the responses are not grouped, it checks if the total received responses meet the quorum size and if the nodes concur. If a quorum is reached, it sets the quorum response and returns true; otherwise, it returns false.
codeFunctions: private boolean computeQuorumResponse (boolean reachedTimeout) { if (quorumResponse != null) // ALREADY COMPUTED return true;if (groupResponsesByResult) { for (List < ODistributedResponse > group:responseGroups) { if (group.size () >= quorum) { int responsesForQuorum = 0;for (ODistributedResponse r:group) { if (nodesConcurInQuorum.contains (r.getExecutorNodeName ())) { final Object payload = r.getPayload ();if (payload instanceof Throwable) { if (payload instanceof ODistributedRecordLockedException) // JUST ONE ODistributedRecordLockedException IS ENOUGH TO FAIL THE OPERATION BECAUSE RESOURCES CANNOT BE LOCKED break;if (payload instanceof OConcurrentCreateException) // JUST ONE OConcurrentCreateException IS ENOUGH TO FAIL THE OPERATION BECAUSE RID ARE DIFFERENT break;} else if (++ responsesForQuorum >= quorum) { // QUORUM REACHED setQuorumResponse (r);return true;} } } } } } else { if (receivedResponses >= quorum) { int responsesForQuorum = 0;for (Map.Entry < String,Object > response:responses.entrySet ()) { if (response.getValue () != NO_RESPONSE && nodesConcurInQuorum.contains (response.getKey ()) && ++ responsesForQuorum >= quorum) { // QUORUM REACHED ODistributedResponse resp = (ODistributedResponse) response.getValue ();if (resp != null &&!(resp.getPayload () instanceof Throwable)) setQuorumResponse (resp);return true;} } } } return false;}

codeFunctions: boolean canBeUsedByOrderByAfterFilter (OIndex <?> index,List < String > equalsFilterFields,List < OPair < String,String > > orderedFields) { if (orderedFields.isEmpty ()) return false;if (!index.supportsOrderedIterations ()) return false;final OIndexDefinition definition = index.getDefinition ();final List < String > indexFields = definition.getFields ();int endIndex = Math.min (indexFields.size (),equalsFilterFields.size ());final String firstOrder = orderedFields.get (0).getValue ();//check that all the "equals" clauses are a prefix for the index for (int i = 0;i < endIndex;i ++) { final String equalsFieldName = equalsFilterFields.get (i);final String indexFieldName = indexFields.get (i);if (!equalsFieldName.equals (indexFieldName)) return false;} endIndex = Math.min (indexFields.size (),orderedFields.size () + equalsFilterFields.size ());if (endIndex == equalsFilterFields.size ()) { //the index is used only for filtering return false;} //check that after that prefix there all the Order By fields in the right order for (int i = equalsFilterFields.size ();i < endIndex;i ++) { int fieldOrderInOrderByClause = i - equalsFilterFields.size ();final OPair < String,String > pair = orderedFields.get (fieldOrderInOrderByClause);if (!firstOrder.equals (pair.getValue ())) return false;final String orderFieldName = pair.getKey ();final String indexFieldName = indexFields.get (i);if (!orderFieldName.equals (indexFieldName)) return false;} return true;}

codeComment: This method retrieves a map of console methods. It first checks if the `methods` map is already populated and returns it if so. If not, it searches for declared command collections using `ServiceLoader` and adds them to a list of candidates. For each candidate, it creates an instance, sets its context, and adds it to the list. It then initializes a `TreeMap` to store methods, sorted by priority and name. The method iterates over each candidate, retrieves its public methods, and adds them to the map if they meet certain criteria (not abstract, not static, public, and returning `void`). Finally, it returns the populated `methods` map.

1. **Validation**: Checks if the `indexName` is null and throws an exception if it is, indicating that the command has not been parsed yet.

2. **Database Access**: Retrieves the current database instance using `getDatabase()`.

3. **Collate Handling**: If `collates` are provided, it creates a list of `OCollate` objects. If any collate is null, it adds null to the list.

4. **Index Creation**:

   - If `fields` are provided, it checks for the presence of `keyTypes` and `collates`. If neither is present, it creates an index on the specified fields.
   - If `keyTypes` are provided, it extracts field types and creates an `OIndexDefinition` using `OIndexDefinitionFactory`. It then creates the index using this definition.

5. **Return Value**: If the index is successfully created, it returns the size of the index. Otherwise, it returns null.

because it has not been parsed yet");final ODatabaseDocument database = getDatabase ();final OIndex <?> idx;List < OCollate > collatesList = null;if (collates != null) { collatesList = new ArrayList < OCollate > ();for (String collate:collates) { if (collate != null) { final OCollate col = OSQLEngine.getCollate (collate);collatesList.add (col);} else collatesList.add (null);} } if (fields == null || fields.length == 0) { OIndexFactory factory = OIndexes.getFactory (indexType.toString (),null);if (keyTypes != null) idx = database.getMetadata ().getIndexManager ().createIndex (indexName,indexType.toString (),new OSimpleKeyIndexDefinition (keyTypes,collatesList),null,null,metadataDoc,engine);else if (serializerKeyId != 0) { idx = database.getMetadata ().getIndexManager ().createIndex (indexName,indexType.toString (),new ORuntimeKeyIndexDefinition (serializerKeyId),null,null,metadataDoc,engine);} else { throw new ODatabaseException ("Impossible to create an index without specify the key type or the associated property");} } else { if ((keyTypes == null || keyTypes.length == 0) && collates == null) { idx = oClass.createIndex (indexName,indexType.toString (),null,metadataDoc,engine,fields);} else { final List < OType > fieldTypeList;if (keyTypes == null) { for (final String fieldName:fields) { if (!fieldName.equals ("@rid") &&!oClass.existsProperty (fieldName)) throw new OIndexException ("Index with name : '" + indexName + "' cannot be created on class : '" + oClass.getName () + "' because field: '" + fieldName + "' is absent in class definition.");} fieldTypeList = ((OClassImpl) oClass).extractFieldTypes (fields);} else fieldTypeList = Arrays.asList (keyTypes);final OIndexDefinition idxDef = OIndexDefinitionFactory.createIndexDefinition (oClass,Arrays.asList (fields),fieldTypeList,collatesList,indexType.toString (),null);idx = database.getMetadata ().getIndexManager ().createIndex (indexName,indexType.name (),idxDef,oClass.getPolymorphicClusterIds (),null,metadataDoc,engine);} } if (idx != null) return idx.getSize ();return null;}

originalComment: Returns a Transactional OrientGraph implementation from the current database in thread local.
codeComment: This method retrieves an `OrientGraph` instance, either by reusing an active graph if conditions are met or by creating a new one. It checks if the current thread-local database matches the active graph's database and if the graph is not closed. If these conditions are satisfied, it sets the graph in the thread-local storage and optionally starts a transaction. If not, it sets the thread-local database and creates a new `OrientGraph` instance, starting a transaction if required. The method also updates a boolean flag to indicate whether the graph should be shut down.
codeFunctions: public static OrientGraph getGraph (final boolean autoStartTx,OModifiableBoolean shouldBeShutDown) { final ODatabaseDocumentInternal database = ODatabaseRecordThreadLocal.instance ().get ();final OrientBaseGraph result = OrientBaseGraph.getActiveGraph ();if (result != null && (result instanceof OrientGraph)) { final ODatabaseDocumentInternal graphDb = result.getRawGraph ();// CHECK IF THE DATABASE + USER IN TL IS THE SAME IN ORDER TO USE IT if (canReuseActiveGraph (graphDb,database)) { if (!graphDb.isClosed ()) { ODatabaseRecordThreadLocal.instance ().set (graphDb);if (autoStartTx && autoTxStartRequired (graphDb)) ((OrientGraph) result).begin ();shouldBeShutDown.setValue (false);return (OrientGraph) result;} } } // Set it again on ThreadLocal because the getRawGraph() may have set a closed db in the thread-local ODatabaseRecordThreadLocal.instance ().set (database);shouldBeShutDown.setValue (true);final OrientGraph g = (OrientGraph) OrientGraphFactory.getTxGraphImplFactory ().getGraph (database,false);if (autoStartTx && autoTxStartRequired (database)) g.begin ();return g;}

codeComment: The method `isAuthorized` checks if a given user has permission to access a specific resource. It first verifies that both the username and resource are not null. originalComment: Method to adjust line and column numbers for the start of a token.
codeComment: The `adjustBeginLineColumn` method adjusts the line and column numbers of tokens in a buffer. It takes two parameters, `newLine` and `newCol`, which represent the new starting line and column numbers, respectively. The method calculates the length of the buffer segment to be adjusted and iterates through the buffer to update the line and column numbers accordingly. It ensures that the line and column numbers are correctly updated even if the buffer wraps around. Finally, it updates the `line` and `column` variables to reflect the new starting position.
codeFunctions: public void adjustBeginLineColumn (int newLine,int newCol) { int start = tokenBegin;int len;if (bufpos >= tokenBegin) { len = bufpos - tokenBegin + inBuf + 1;} else { len = bufsize - tokenBegin + bufpos + 1 + inBuf;} int i = 0,j = 0,k = 0;int nextColDiff = 0,columnDiff = 0;while (i < len && bufline [ j = start % bufsize ] == bufline [ k = ++ start % bufsize ]) { bufline [ j ] = newLine;nextColDiff = columnDiff + bufcolumn [ k ] - bufcolumn [ j ];bufcolumn [ j ] = newCol + columnDiff;columnDiff = nextColDiff;i ++;} if (i < len) { bufline [ j ] = newLine ++;bufcolumn [ j ] = newCol + columnDiff;while (i ++ < len) { if (bufline [ j = start % bufsize ] != bufline [ ++ start % bufsize ]) bufline [ j ] = newLine ++;else bufline [ j ] = newLine;} } line = bufline [ j ];column = bufcolumn [ j ];}

originalComment: Ends the current atomic operation on this manager.
codeComment: This method, `endAtomicOperation`, finalizes an atomic operation in an OrientDB storage system. It checks if an atomic operation is currently active and throws an exception if not. It then decrements the operation counter and performs rollback if specified. If the counter reaches one, it commits changes using the write-ahead log (WAL) if enabled, releases locks, and updates tracking structures. Finally, it decrements the atomic operations count and returns the log sequence number (LSN) of the operation.
codeFunctions: public OLogSequenceNumber endAtomicOperation (boolean rollback) throws IOException { final OAtomicOperation operation = currentOperation.get ();if (operation == null) { OLogManager.instance ().error (this,"There is no atomic operation active",null);throw new ODatabaseException ("There is no atomic operation active");} int counter = operation.getCounter ();operation.decrementCounter ();assert counter > 0;final OLogSequenceNumber lsn;try { if (rollback) { operation.rollback ();} if (counter == 1) { try { final boolean useWal = useWal ();if (!operation.isRollback ()) { lsn = operation.commitChanges (useWal?writeAheadLog:null);} else { lsn = null;} if (trackAtomicOperations) { activeAtomicOperations.remove (operation.getOperationUnitId ());} } finally { final Iterator < String > lockedObjectIterator = operation.lockedObjects ().iterator ();while (lockedObjectIterator.hasNext ()) { final String lockedObject = lockedObjectIterator.next ();lockedObjectIterator.remove ();lockManager.releaseLock (this,lockedObject,OOneEntryPerKeyLockManager.LOCK.EXCLUSIVE);} currentOperation.set (null);} } else { lsn = null;} } catch (Error e) { final OAbstractPaginatedStorage st = storage;if (st != null) { st.handleJVMError (e);} counter = 1;throw e;} finally { if (counter == 1) { atomicOperationsCount.decrement ();} } return lsn;}

It first checks if the operation already contains the lock name in its locked objects. If it does, the method returns immediately, avoiding redundant locking. If the lock is not already held, it acquires an exclusive lock using the `lockManager` and adds the lock name to the operation's locked objects.
codeFunctions: public void acquireExclusiveLockTillOperationComplete (OAtomicOperation operation,String lockName) { if (operation.containsInLockedObjects (lockName)) { return;} lockManager.acquireLock (lockName,OOneEntryPerKeyLockManager.LOCK.EXCLUSIVE);operation.addLockedObject (lockName);}

originalComment: Changes amount of memory which may be used by given cache.This method may consume many resources if amount of memory provided in parameter is much less than current amount of memory.
codeComment: This method, `changeMaximumAmountOfMemory`, adjusts the maximum amount of memory allocated for a disk cache. It first normalizes the requested memory size and then checks if the new size is the same as the current size, in which case it returns immediately. If the new size would result in a higher percentage of pinned pages than allowed, it throws an `IllegalStateException`. It then creates a new `MemoryData` object with the updated size and attempts to update the memory data container atomically. If successful, it logs the change in disk cache size.
codeFunctions: public void changeMaximumAmountOfMemory (final long readCacheMaxMemory) throws IllegalStateException { MemoryData memoryData;MemoryData newMemoryData;final int newMemorySize = normalizeMemory (readCacheMaxMemory,pageSize);do { memoryData = memoryDataContainer.get ();if (memoryData.maxSize == newMemorySize) { return;} if ((100 * memoryData.pinnedPages / newMemorySize) > percentOfPinnedPages) { throw new IllegalStateException ("Cannot decrease amount of memory used by disk cache " + "because limit of pinned pages will be more than allowed limit " + percentOfPinnedPages);} newMemoryData = new MemoryData (newMemorySize,memoryData.pinnedPages);} while (!memoryDataContainer.compareAndSet (memoryData,newMemoryData));//    if (newMemorySize < memoryData.maxSize) //      removeColdestPagesIfNeeded(); OLogManager.instance ().info (this,"Disk cache size was changed from " + memoryData.maxSize + " pages to " + newMemorySize + " pages");}

originalComment: Initialize a server socket for communicating with the client.
codeComment: The `listen` method sets up a server to listen for incoming connections on a specified host and port range using a given protocol. It iterates through the ports in the specified range, attempting to bind a server socket to each port. If a port is successfully bound, it logs the successful connection and returns. originalComment: Finds closest power of two for given integer value.Idea is simple duplicate the most significant bit to the lowest bits for the smallest number of iterations possible and then increment result value by 1.
codeComment:
The `closestPowerOfTwo` method calculates the smallest power of two that is greater than or equal to the given integer `value`. It uses bitwise operations to achieve this efficiently. Here's a step-by-step summary of the method:

1. **Initialization**: Start with `n = value - 1`.
2. **Bitwise OR and Right Shift**: 
   - `n |= n >>> 1`: This operation sets all bits to the right of the highest set bit.
   - `n |= n >>> 2`: This operation further propagates the highest set bit to the right.
   - `n |= n >>> 4`: This continues the propagation process.
   - `n |= n >>> 8`: This continues the propagation process.
   - `n |= n >>> 16`: This continues the propagation process.
3. **Boundary Check**: 
   - If `n` is less than 0, return 1 (since the smallest power of two is 1).
   - If `n` is greater than or equal to \(2^{30}\), return \(2^{30}\) (to handle overflow and ensure the result fits within a 32-bit integer).
4. **Return Result**: Return `n + 1`, which is the smallest power of two greater than or equal to the original `value`.

This method efficiently computes the closest power of two using bitwise operations, which are generally faster than arithmetic operations.
codeFunctions: private static int closestPowerOfTwo (int value) { int n = value - 1;n |= n >>> 1;n |= n >>> 2;n |= n >>> 4;n |= n >>> 8;n |= n >>> 16;return (n < 0)?1:(n >= (1 << 30))?1 << 30:n + 1;}

codeComment: The `tryAcquireReadLock` method attempts to acquire a read lock with a specified timeout. It first checks if the current thread already holds a read lock or if a write lock is held, in which case it returns true without further action. If neither condition is met, it increments a distributed counter and waits in a loop until the lock becomes available or the timeout expires. The method uses `LockSupport.parkNanos` to park the thread until the lock is acquired or the timeout is reached. If the lock is acquired, it increments the lock holds count and returns true; otherwise, it returns false.
codeFunctions: public boolean tryAcquireReadLock (long timeout) { final OModifiableInteger lHolds = lockHolds.get ();final int holds = lHolds.intValue ();if (holds > 0) { // we have already acquire read lock lHolds.increment ();return true;} else if (holds < 0) { // write lock is acquired before, do nothing return true;} distributedCounter.increment ();WNode wNode = tail.get ();final long start = System.nanoTime ();while (wNode.locked) { distributedCounter.decrement ();while (wNode.locked && wNode == tail.get ()) { wNode.waitingReaders.put (Thread.currentThread (),Boolean.TRUE);if (wNode.locked && wNode == tail.get ()) { final long parkTimeout = timeout - (System.nanoTime () - start);if (parkTimeout > 0) { LockSupport.parkNanos (this,parkTimeout);} else { return false;} } wNode = tail.get ();if (System.nanoTime () - start > timeout) { return false;} } distributedCounter.increment ();wNode = tail.get ();if (System.nanoTime () - start > timeout) { distributedCounter.decrement ();return false;} } lHolds.increment ();assert lHolds.intValue () == 1;return true;}

codeComment: The `clear` method is designed to remove all entries from an SBTree Bonsai structure. It starts by initiating an atomic operation and acquiring an exclusive lock on the file. It then loads the root bucket for writing, shrinks it to remove all entries, and marks it as empty. Any sub-trees are added to a queue and recycled. If any exceptions occur, the method ensures that the atomic operation is rolled back, and the lock is released.
codeFunctions: @ Override public void clear () throws IOException { boolean rollback = false;final OAtomicOperation atomicOperation = startAtomicOperation (true);try { final Lock lock = FILE_LOCK_MANAGER.acquireExclusiveLock (fileId);try { final Queue < OBonsaiBucketPointer > subTreesToDelete = new LinkedList <> ();final OCacheEntry cacheEntry = loadPageForWrite (atomicOperation,fileId,rootBucketPointer.getPageIndex (),false,true);try { OSBTreeBonsaiBucket < K,V > rootBucket = new OSBTreeBonsaiBucket <> (cacheEntry,rootBucketPointer.getPageOffset (),keySerializer,valueSerializer,this);addChildrenToQueue (subTreesToDelete,rootBucket);rootBucket.shrink (0);rootBucket = new OSBTreeBonsaiBucket <> (cacheEntry,rootBucketPointer.getPageOffset (),true,keySerializer,valueSerializer,this);rootBucket.setTreeSize (0);} finally { releasePageFromWrite (atomicOperation,cacheEntry);} recycleSubTrees (subTreesToDelete,atomicOperation);} finally { lock.unlock ();} } catch (final Exception e) { rollback = true;throw e;} finally { endAtomicOperation (rollback);} }

If any exception occurs during this process, it sets a rollback flag and rethrows the exception. Finally, it ends the atomic operation, rolling back if necessary.

codeComment:
The `end` method is responsible for finalizing the batch import process in an OrientDB database. It performs the following steps:

1. Retrieves the class metadata for the specified vertex class.
2. Initializes an `AtomicInteger` named `runningThreads` to keep track of the number of active threads.
3. Starts multiple threads (`BatchImporterJob`) to handle the import process in parallel, except for the last thread which is executed directly on the main thread.
4. Waits for all threads to complete by synchronizing on the `runningThreads` object and using a `while` loop to check if any threads are still running.
5. Ensures that the database is properly closed and reactivates the current thread.
6. Resets the write-ahead logging (WAL) configuration if it was previously active.
codeFunctions: public void end () { final OClass vClass = db.getMetadata ().getSchema ().getClass (vertexClass);try { runningThreads = new AtomicInteger (parallel);for (int i = 0;i < parallel - 1;i ++) { Thread t = new BatchImporterJob (i,vClass);t.start ();} Thread t = new BatchImporterJob (parallel - 1,vClass);t.run ();if (runningThreads.get () > 0) { synchronized (runningThreads) { while (runningThreads.get () > 0) { try { runningThreads.wait ();} catch (InterruptedException e) { } } } } } finally { db.activateOnCurrentThread ();db.declareIntent (null);db.close ();if (walActive) OGlobalConfiguration.USE_WAL.setValue (true);} }

codeComment:
This method `execute` is part of a command execution system in an object-oriented database management system. It processes a command with arguments provided in a map (`iArgs`). The method checks if the command has been parsed and throws an exception if not. It then processes the command based on whether it involves an index, creating new documents, merging content, or executing a subquery.

1. **Index Handling**:
   - If an index name is specified, it checks if there are new records to process.
   - Retrieves the index from the database metadata.
   - Binds values from the new records to the index keys and values.
   - Updates the index if the record is not already present.
   - Returns the last processed entry.

2. **Document Creation**:
   - If no index is specified, it creates new documents.
   - Binds parameters from the new records to the documents.
   - Saves the documents to the database.
   - Returns the created documents.

3. **Content Merging**:
   - If content is provided, it merges the content into a new document.
   - Saves the document to the database.
   - Returns the merged document.

4. **Subquery Execution**:
   - If a subquery is specified, it executes the subquery.
   - Returns the result of the subquery or the number of saved records.

The method handles various scenarios and ensures that the command is executed correctly based on the provided arguments and the state of the database.

command because it has not been parsed yet");final OCommandParameters commandParameters = new OCommandParameters (iArgs);if (indexName != null) { if (newRecords == null) throw new OCommandExecutionException ("No key/value found");final OIndex <?> index = getDatabase ().getMetadata ().getIndexManager ().getIndex (indexName);if (index == null) throw new OCommandExecutionException ("Target index '" + indexName + "' not found");// BIND VALUES Map < String,Object > result = new HashMap < String,Object > ();for (Map < String,Object > candidate:newRecords) { Object indexKey = getIndexKeyValue (commandParameters,candidate);OIdentifiable indexValue = getIndexValue (commandParameters,candidate);if (index instanceof OIndexMultiValues) { final Collection < ORID > rids = ((OIndexMultiValues) index).get (indexKey);if (!rids.contains (indexValue.getIdentity ())) { index.put (indexKey,indexValue);} } else { index.put (indexKey,indexValue);} result.put (KEYWORD_KEY,indexKey);result.put (KEYWORD_RID,indexValue);} // RETURN LAST ENTRY return prepareReturnItem (new ODocument (result));} else { // CREATE NEW DOCUMENTS final List < ODocument > docs = new ArrayList < ODocument > ();if (newRecords != null) { for (Map < String,Object > candidate:newRecords) { final ODocument doc = className != null?new ODocument (className):new ODocument ();OSQLHelper.bindParameters (doc,candidate,commandParameters,context);saveRecord (doc);docs.add (doc);} if (docs.size () == 1) return prepareReturnItem (docs.get (0));else return prepareReturnResult (docs);} else if (content != null) { final ODocument doc = className != null?new ODocument (className):new ODocument ();doc.merge (content,true,false);saveRecord (doc);return prepareReturnItem (doc);} else if (subQuery != null) { subQuery.execute ();if (queryResult != null) return prepareReturnResult (queryResult);return saved.longValue ();} } return null;}

originalComment: Convert the item with the received key to a record.
codeComment:
This method, `convertLink2Record`, is designed to convert a link (represented by an `ORID` object) to its corresponding record in an OrientDB database. Here's a summary of its functionality:

1. **Check Status**: If the `status` is `MULTIVALUE_CONTENT_TYPE.ALL_RECORDS`, the method returns immediately without performing any further actions.

2. **Retrieve Value**: The method retrieves the value associated with the given `iKey`. If `iKey` is an instance of `ORID`, it is used directly as the value. Otherwise, the value is fetched using `super.get(iKey)`.

3. **Check Value Type**: If the retrieved value is not null and is an instance of `ORID`, the method proceeds to convert this link to a record.

4. **Convert Link to Record**:
   - The `ORID` is used to get the corresponding `ORecord`.
   - If the record is not null, the method untracks the `sourceRecord` from the `ORID` and tracks the `sourceRecord` with the retrieved record.
   - The method then puts the key-value pair (where the value is the retrieved record) into the super class.

5. **Handle Exceptions**: If an `ORecordNotFoundException` is thrown during the retrieval of the record, it is ignored.

6. **Reset Marshalling Flag**: Finally, the `marshalling` flag is set to false to indicate that the marshalling process is complete.
codeFunctions: private void convertLink2Record (final Object iKey) { if (status == MULTIVALUE_CONTENT_TYPE.ALL_RECORDS) return;final Object value;if (iKey instanceof ORID) value = iKey;else value = super.get (iKey);if (value != null && value instanceof ORID) { final ORID rid = (ORID) value;marshalling = true;try { try { // OVERWRITE IT ORecord record = rid.getRecord ();if (record != null) { ORecordInternal.unTrack (sourceRecord,rid);ORecordInternal.track (sourceRecord,record);} super.put (iKey,record);} catch (ORecordNotFoundException ignore) { // IGNORE THIS } } finally { marshalling = false;} } }

codeComment: The method `createIndexedProperty` processes a condition and an item to determine if an indexed property search result can be created. It checks if the item is null or not an instance of `OSQLFilterItemField`, returning null if true. It also returns null if both sides of the condition are fields. If the item has chain operators but is not a field chain, it returns null. The method then determines if the condition is inverted based on the position of the item. It adjusts the operator if the condition is inverted, handling specific operator types like `OQueryOperatorIn` and `OQueryOperatorContains`. If the operator is `OQueryOperatorBetween` or `OQueryOperatorIn`, it returns an `OIndexSearchResult` with the original value. Otherwise, it retrieves the value using `OSQLHelper.getValue` and returns an `OIndexSearchResult` with this value.
codeFunctions: private OIndexSearchResult createIndexedProperty (final OSQLFilterCondition iCondition,final Object iItem,OCommandContext ctx) { if (iItem == null ||!(iItem instanceof OSQLFilterItemField)) { return null;} if (iCondition.getLeft () instanceof OSQLFilterItemField && iCondition.getRight () instanceof OSQLFilterItemField) { return null;} final OSQLFilterItemField item = (OSQLFilterItemField) iItem;if (item.hasChainOperators () &&!item.isFieldChain ()) { return null;} boolean inverted = iCondition.getRight () == iItem;final Object origValue = inverted?iCondition.getLeft ():iCondition.getRight ();OQueryOperator operator = iCondition.getOperator ();if (inverted) { if (operator instanceof OQueryOperatorIn) { operator = new OQueryOperatorContains ();} else if (operator instanceof OQueryOperatorContains) { operator = new OQueryOperatorIn ();} else if (operator instanceof OQueryOperatorMajor) { operator = new OQueryOperatorMinor ();} else if (operator instanceof OQueryOperatorMinor) { operator = new OQueryOperatorMajor ();} else if (operator instanceof OQueryOperatorMajorEquals) { operator = new OQueryOperatorMinorEquals ();} else if (operator instanceof OQueryOperatorMinorEquals) { operator = new OQueryOperatorMajorEquals ();} } if (iCondition.getOperator () instanceof OQueryOperatorBetween || operator instanceof OQueryOperatorIn) { return new OIndexSearchResult (operator,item.getFieldChain (),origValue);} final Object value = OSQLHelper.getValue (origValue,null,ctx);return new OIndexSearchResult (operator,item.getFieldChain (),value);}

It skips fields that are marked as transient, version, or ID fields. For each relevant field, it retrieves the field's value, processes it using the `setValue` method, and then sets the processed value back to the field. The method handles exceptions related to illegal access, missing methods, and invocation targets. originalComment: Truncates all the clusters the class uses.
codeComment:
The `truncate` method is designed to remove all records from a class in an OrientDB database. It performs the following steps:

1. **Database and Security Checks**:
   - Retrieves the current database instance.
   - Checks if the user has the necessary update permissions for the class.
   - Throws an `OSecurityException` if the class has record-level security enabled.

2. **Storage and Locking**:
   - Acquires a schema read lock to ensure thread safety during the operation.
   - Retrieves the storage instance from the database.

3. **Cluster Truncation**:
   - Iterates over the cluster IDs associated with the class.
   - For each cluster, it retrieves the cluster instance and checks for cluster permissions.
   - Truncates the cluster, effectively removing all records.

4. **Index Management**:
   - Clears all indexes associated with the class.
   - Rebuilds indexes inherited from superclass to maintain consistency.

5. **Unlocking**:

This method ensures that all records and associated indexes are properly managed and secured during the truncation process.

codeComment:
This method, `rollback`, is designed to roll back a micro-transaction in a storage system. It performs the following steps:

1. **Check Openness**: Ensures that the storage is open.
2. **Acquire Read Lock**: Acquires a read lock on the state lock to ensure thread safety.
3. **Nested Try-Catch Block**:
   - **Check Openness Again**: Ensures the storage is still open.
   - **Transaction Check**: Verifies if there is an active transaction and if it matches the passed-in micro-transaction.
   - **Make Storage Dirty**: Marks the storage as dirty.
   - **Rollback Storage Transaction**: Rolls back the storage transaction.
   - **Update Record Cache**: Updates the record cache after the rollback.
   - **Increment Rollback Counter**: Increments the transaction rollback counter.
4. **Exception Handling**: Catches and wraps `IOException` in an `OStorageException`.
5. **Finally Block**: Resets the transaction to `null` and releases the read lock.
6. **Outer Exception Handling**: Catches and logs any `RuntimeException`, `Error`, or `Throwable` to prepare for rethrowing.

The method ensures that the rollback process is thread-safe and handles various exceptions to maintain the integrity of the storage system.
codeFunctions: public void rollback (final OMicroTransaction microTransaction) { try { checkOpenness ();stateLock.acquireReadLock ();try { try { checkOpenness ();if (transaction.get () == null) { return;} if (transaction.get ().getMicroTransaction ().getId () != microTransaction.getId ()) { throw new OStorageException ("Passed in and active micro-transaction are different micro-transactions. Passed in micro-transaction cannot be " + "rolled back.");} makeStorageDirty ();rollbackStorageTx ();microTransaction.updateRecordCacheAfterRollback ();txRollback.incrementAndGet ();} catch (final IOException e) { throw OException.wrapException (new OStorageException ("Error during micro-transaction rollback"),e);} finally { transaction.set (null);} } finally { stateLock.releaseReadLock ();} } catch (final RuntimeException ee) { throw logAndPrepareForRethrow (ee);} catch (final Error ee) { throw logAndPrepareForRethrow (ee);} catch (final Throwable t) { throw logAndPrepareForRethrow (t);} }

public static void mergeSort (final int from,final int to,final IntComparator c,final Swapper swapper) { /*

		 * the JDK mergesorts this is an "in-place" mergesort, i.e. does not allocate any temporary

originalComment: Calculate the differences
codeComment:
The `calculate` method performs the following steps:

1. **Reset Results**: Calls `resetResults()` to clear any previous results.
2. **Initialize Executor**: Creates a `SimultaneousExecutor` instance for parallel execution.
3. **Determine Number of Threads**: Retrieves the core pool size from the executor to determine the number of threads.
4. **Parallel Execution**: Iterates over the number of threads and assigns each thread a task to process a subset of data.
   - **Traverse and Match**: For each thread, it initializes `HollowIndexerValueTraverser` instances for `from` and `to` data. It then iterates over matched ordinals, traverses the data, and populates a hash table to count matches.
   - **Count Unmatched Elements**: After processing matched ordinals, it counts unmatched elements in `from` and `to` data.
5. **Await Completion**: Waits for all threads to complete their execution. If an exception occurs, it throws a `RuntimeException`.

This method efficiently processes data in parallel using multiple threads to improve performance.
codeFunctions: public void calculate () { resetResults ();SimultaneousExecutor executor = new SimultaneousExecutor (getClass (),"calculate");final int numThreads = executor.getCorePoolSize ();for (int i = 0;i < numThreads;i ++) { final int threadNumber = i;executor.execute (new Runnable () { public void run () { HollowIndexerValueTraverser fromTraverser = new HollowIndexerValueTraverser (from,type,elementPaths);HollowIndexerValueTraverser toTraverser = new HollowIndexerValueTraverser (to,type,elementPaths);int hashedResults [ ] = new int [ 16 ];for (int i = threadNumber;i < matcher.getMatchedOrdinals ().size ();i += numThreads) { long ordinalPair = matcher.getMatchedOrdinals ().get (i);int fromOrdinal = (int) (ordinalPair >>> 32);int toOrdinal = (int) ordinalPair;fromTraverser.traverse (fromOrdinal);toTraverser.traverse (toOrdinal);if (fromTraverser.getNumMatches () * 2 > hashedResults.length) hashedResults = new int [ hashTableSize (fromTraverser.getNumMatches ()) ];populateHashTable (fromTraverser,hashedResults);countMatches (fromTraverser,toTraverser,hashedResults);} for (int i = threadNumber;i < matcher.getExtraInFrom ().size ();i += numThreads) { fromTraverser.traverse (matcher.getExtraInFrom ().get (i));totalUnmatchedFromElements.addAndGet (fromTraverser.getNumMatches ());} for (int i = threadNumber;i < matcher.getExtraInTo ().size ();i += numThreads) { toTraverser.traverse (matcher.getExtraInTo ().get (i));totalUnmatchedToElements.addAndGet (toTraverser.getNumMatches ());} } });} try { executor.awaitSuccessfulCompletion ();} catch (Exception ex) { throw new RuntimeException (ex);} }

codeComment: The `writeHeader` method writes a `HollowBlobHeader` to a `DataOutputStream`. It first writes the FastBlob version, then the origin and destination randomized tags for state validation. It also writes a backwards compatibility envelope and header tags, which include input source data versions.

It iterates through all type states, computes their heap cost and populated ordinals, and stores these metrics in respective maps. The total heap footprint and total populated ordinals are also accumulated.
codeFunctions: void calculateTypeMetrics (HollowReadStateEngine hollowReadStateEngine) { Collection < HollowTypeReadState > typeStates = hollowReadStateEngine.getTypeStates ();if (typeStates == null) return;totalHeapFootprint = 0L;totalPopulatedOrdinals = 0;for (HollowTypeReadState typeState:typeStates) { long heapCost = typeState.getApproximateHeapFootprintInBytes ();totalHeapFootprint += heapCost;int populatedOrdinals = typeState.getPopulatedOrdinals ().cardinality ();totalPopulatedOrdinals += populatedOrdinals;String type = typeState.getSchema ().getName ();typeHeapFootprint.put (type,heapCost);typePopulatedOrdinals.put (type,populatedOrdinals);} }

originalComment: Write 4 consecutive bytes

originalComment: Write 8 consecutive bytes
codeComment: This method, `writeFixedLengthLong`, writes a 64-bit long integer (`intBits`) to a `ByteDataBuffer` in a fixed-length format. It does this by shifting the bits of the long integer right by multiples of 8 and casting each result to a byte, which is then written to the buffer. This process effectively breaks down the long integer into its constituent bytes and writes them in big-endian order.

originalComment: Return an ordinal to the pool after the object to which it was assigned is discarded.
codeComment: This method, `returnOrdinalToPool`, adds an integer `ordinal` to a pool of free ordinals. If the pool is full, it resizes the pool by increasing its capacity to 1.5 times its current size. After resizing, it adds the `ordinal` to the pool and increments the size counter.
codeFunctions: public void returnOrdinalToPool (int ordinal) { if (size == freeOrdinals.length) { freeOrdinals = Arrays.copyOf (freeOrdinals,freeOrdinals.length * 3 / 2);} freeOrdinals [ size ] = ordinal;size ++;}

originalComment: Ensure that all future ordinals are returned in ascending order.
codeComment: The `sort` method sorts an array `freeOrdinals` from index 0 to `size` using `Arrays.sort`. After sorting, it reverses the order of the elements in the array by swapping elements from the start and end moving towards the center.
codeFunctions: public void sort () { Arrays.sort (freeOrdinals,0,size);/// reverse the ordering int midpoint = size / 2;for (int i = 0;i < midpoint;i ++) { int temp = freeOrdinals [ i ];freeOrdinals [ i ] = freeOrdinals [ size - i - 1 ];freeOrdinals [ size - i - 1 ] = temp;} }

originalComment: Hash a key
codeComment: This method calculates a hash value for an array of objects (`key`) based on their corresponding field types (`fieldType`). It initializes a hash value to 0 and iterates through each element of the `key` array. For each element, it multiplies the current hash value by 31 and then performs an XOR operation with the hash value of the current element, computed using a separate `hash` method that takes an object and its field type as arguments. Finally, it returns the computed hash value.
codeFunctions: public static int hash (Object key [ ],FieldType fieldType [ ]) { int hash = 0;for (int i = 0;i < key.length;i ++) { hash *= 31;hash ^= hash (key [ i ],fieldType [ i ]);} return hash;}

originalComment: Hash a single key field
codeComment:
This method, `hash`, computes a hash code for a given key based on its field type. It uses the `switch` statement to handle different types of keys:

- **INT**: Converts the key to an integer and computes its hash.
- **LONG**: Converts the key to a long, performs a bitwise XOR operation, and then computes its hash.
- **REFERENCE**: Similar to INT, it converts the key to an integer and computes its hash.
- **BYTES**: Computes the hash of the byte array.
- **STRING**: Uses the `hashCode` method of the string to compute the hash.
- **BOOLEAN**: Converts the boolean to an integer (1231 for true, 1237 for false) and computes its hash.
- **DOUBLE**: Converts the key to a long using `doubleToRawLongBits`, performs a bitwise XOR operation, and then computes its hash.
- **FLOAT**: Converts the key to an integer using `floatToRawIntBits` and computes its hash.

If the field type is unknown, it throws an `IllegalArgumentException`.
codeFunctions: public static int hash (Object key,FieldType fieldType) { switch (fieldType) { case INT:return HashCodes.hashInt (((Integer) key).intValue ());case LONG:long longVal = ((Long) key).longValue ();return HashCodes.hashInt ((int) (longVal ^ (longVal >>> 32)));case REFERENCE:return HashCodes.hashInt (((Integer) key).intValue ());case BYTES:return HashCodes.hashInt (HashCodes.hashCode ((byte [ ]) key));case STRING:return HashCodes.hashInt (key.hashCode ());case BOOLEAN:return HashCodes.hashInt (((Boolean) key).booleanValue ()?1231:1237);case DOUBLE:long longBits = Double.doubleToRawLongBits (((Double) key).doubleValue ());return HashCodes.hashInt ((int) (longBits ^ (longBits >>> 32)));case FLOAT:return HashCodes.hashInt (Float.floatToRawIntBits (((Float) key).floatValue ()));default:throw new IllegalArgumentException ("Unknown field type: " + fieldType);} }

originalComment: Resize the underlying storage to a multiple of what it currently is.This method is not thread - safe.
codeComment: The `resizeStorage` method resizes the storage capacity of a fixed-length element array. It calculates the new number of elements per node by multiplying the current number by a resize factor (`RESIZE_MULTIPLE`). If the new size is not larger than the current size, it throws an `IllegalStateException`. It then creates a new `FixedLengthElementArray` with the updated size and copies elements from the old storage to the new storage. After copying, it destroys the old storage and updates the storage reference and the maximum elements per node.
codeFunctions: private void resizeStorage () { int currentElementsPerNode = maxElementsPerNode;int newElementsPerNode = (int) (currentElementsPerNode * RESIZE_MULTIPLE);if (newElementsPerNode <= currentElementsPerNode) { throw new IllegalStateException ("cannot resize fixed length array from " + currentElementsPerNode + " to " + newElementsPerNode);} FixedLengthElementArray newStorage = new FixedLengthElementArray (memoryRecycler,numNodes * bitsPerElement * newElementsPerNode);LongStream.range (0,numNodes).forEach (nodeIndex -> { long currentBucketStart = nodeIndex * currentElementsPerNode * bitsPerElement;long newBucketStart = nodeIndex * newElementsPerNode * bitsPerElement;for (int offset = 0;offset < currentElementsPerNode;offset ++) { long element = storage.getElementValue (currentBucketStart + offset * bitsPerElement,bitsPerElement,elementMask);if (element == NO_ELEMENT) { break;// we have exhausted the elements at this index } newStorage.setElementValue (newBucketStart + offset * bitsPerElement,bitsPerElement,element);} });storage.destroy (memoryRecycler);storage = newStorage;maxElementsPerNode = newElementsPerNode;}

originalComment: If the preferredOrdinal has not already been used mark it and use it.Otherwise delegate to the FreeOrdinalTracker.

codeFunctions: private int findFreeOrdinal (int preferredOrdinal) { if (preferredOrdinal != - 1 && unusedPreviousOrdinals.get (preferredOrdinal)) { unusedPreviousOrdinals.clear (preferredOrdinal);return preferredOrdinal;} return freeOrdinalTracker.getFreeOrdinal ();}

originalComment: Create an array mapping the ordinals to pointers so that they can be easily looked up when writing to blob streams.
codeComment: The `prepareForWrite` method processes an array of pointers and ordinals to prepare for writing operations. It first determines the maximum ordinal value from the array. Then, it creates a new array `pointersByOrdinal` of size `maxOrdinal + 1`, initializing all elements to `-1`. Finally, it populates `pointersByOrdinal` with the pointers, using the ordinal as the index.
codeFunctions: public void prepareForWrite () { int maxOrdinal = 0;AtomicLongArray pao = pointersAndOrdinals;for (int i = 0;i < pao.length ();i ++) { long key = pao.get (i);if (key != EMPTY_BUCKET_VALUE) { int ordinal = (int) (key >>> BITS_PER_POINTER);if (ordinal > maxOrdinal) { maxOrdinal = ordinal;} } } long [ ] pbo = new long [ maxOrdinal + 1 ];Arrays.fill (pbo,- 1);for (int i = 0;i < pao.length ();i ++) { long key = pao.get (i);if (key != EMPTY_BUCKET_VALUE) { int ordinal = (int) (key >>> BITS_PER_POINTER);pbo [ ordinal ] = key & POINTER_MASK;} } pointersByOrdinal = pbo;}

originalComment: Compare the byte sequence contained in the supplied ByteDataBuffer with the sequence contained in the map pointed to by the specified key byte by byte.
codeComment: This method, `compare`, checks if a given `ByteDataBuffer` matches the serialized representation stored at a specific key in a byte array. It first calculates the position using the key and a mask. It then reads the size of the data at that position and compares it with the length of the `ByteDataBuffer`. If they don't match, it returns `false`. If they match, it reads the data byte by byte and compares each byte with the corresponding byte in the `ByteDataBuffer`. If all bytes match, it returns `true`; otherwise, it returns `false`.
codeFunctions: private boolean compare (ByteDataBuffer serializedRepresentation,long key) { long position = key & POINTER_MASK;int sizeOfData = VarInt.readVInt (byteData.getUnderlyingArray (),position);if (sizeOfData != serializedRepresentation.length ()) { return false;} position += VarInt.sizeOfVInt (sizeOfData);for (int i = 0;i < sizeOfData;i ++) { if (serializedRepresentation.get (i) != byteData.get (position ++)) { return false;} } return true;}

originalComment: Grow the key array.All of the values in the current array must be re - hashed and added to the new array.
codeComment: The `growKeyArray` method doubles the size of the `pointersAndOrdinals` array. If the new size becomes negative, it throws an `IllegalStateException` indicating that the maximum capacity of the map has been exceeded. The method then calls itself recursively with the new size.
codeFunctions: private void growKeyArray () { int newSize = pointersAndOrdinals.length () << 1;if (newSize < 0) { throw new IllegalStateException ("New size computed to grow the underlying array for the map is negative. " + "This is most likely due to the total number of keys added to map has exceeded the max capacity of the keys map can hold. " + "Current array size :" + pointersAndOrdinals.length () + " and size to grow :" + newSize);} growKeyArray (newSize);}

originalComment: Get the hash code for the byte array pointed to by the specified key.
codeComment: The method `rehashPreviouslyAddedData` takes a `long` key as input and calculates a new position for the data associated with that key. It uses a bitwise AND operation with `POINTER_MASK` to determine the initial position. Then, it reads the size of the data at that position using `VarInt.readVInt` and adjusts the position by adding the size of the variable-length integer. Finally, it returns a hash code for the data at the new position using `HashCodes.hashCode`.
codeFunctions: private int rehashPreviouslyAddedData (long key) { long position = key & POINTER_MASK;int sizeOfData = VarInt.readVInt (byteData.getUnderlyingArray (),position);position += VarInt.sizeOfVInt (sizeOfData);return HashCodes.hashCode (byteData.getUnderlyingArray (),position,sizeOfData);}

originalComment: Determine size of hash table capable of storing the specified number of elements with a load factor applied.
codeComment: This method calculates the appropriate size for a hash table based on the number of elements it needs to store. It first checks if the number of elements is negative or exceeds a predefined maximum size, throwing an `IllegalArgumentException` if either condition is met. For zero elements, it returns 1. For fewer than three elements, it returns twice the number of elements. For other cases, it applies a load factor of 10/7 to the number of elements, then determines the next largest power of 2 that can fit in an integer and returns that value as the hash table size.
codeFunctions: public static int hashTableSize (int numElements) throws IllegalArgumentException { if (numElements < 0) { throw new IllegalArgumentException ("cannot be negative; numElements=" + numElements);} else if (numElements > HASH_TABLE_MAX_SIZE) { throw new IllegalArgumentException ("exceeds maximum number of buckets; numElements=" + numElements);} if (numElements == 0) return 1;if (numElements < 3) return numElements * 2;// Apply load factor to number of elements and determine next // largest power of 2 that fits in an int int sizeAfterLoadFactor = (int) ((long) numElements * 10 / 7);int bits = 32 - Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros (sizeAfterLoadFactor - 1);return 1 << bits;}

originalComment: Run a compaction cycle will produce a data state with exactly the same data as currently but reorganized so that ordinal holes are filled.This may need to be run multiple times to arrive at an optimal state.
codeComment: This method, `runCompactionCycle`, performs a compaction cycle using the provided configuration. It first checks if the configuration is not null and if there is a current read state available. If both conditions are met, it creates a new `HollowCompactor` instance with the write engine, the current read state's state engine, and the configuration. It then checks if compaction is needed. If compaction is required, it runs a cycle with a lambda function that calls the `compact` method of the compactor. If the configuration is null or there is no current read state, it returns `NO_ANNOUNCEMENT_AVAILABLE`.
codeFunctions: public long runCompactionCycle (HollowCompactor.CompactionConfig config) { if (config != null && readStates.hasCurrent ()) { final HollowCompactor compactor = new HollowCompactor (getWriteEngine (),readStates.current ().getStateEngine (),config);if (compactor.needsCompaction ()) { return runCycle (newState -> compactor.compact ());} } return NO_ANNOUNCEMENT_AVAILABLE;}

originalComment: Write the current state as a snapshot blob.
codeComment: The `writeSnapshot` method writes a snapshot of the current state of the system to an output stream. It first prepares the state engine for writing, then writes the header and schema information. It uses a `SimultaneousExecutor` to calculate the snapshot for each type state concurrently. After ensuring all calculations are complete, it writes the schema, number of shards, and snapshot data for each type state to the output stream, finally flushing the stream.
codeFunctions: public void writeSnapshot (OutputStream os) throws IOException { stateEngine.prepareForWrite ();DataOutputStream dos = new DataOutputStream (os);writeHeader (dos,stateEngine.getSchemas (),false);VarInt.writeVInt (dos,stateEngine.getOrderedTypeStates ().size ());SimultaneousExecutor executor = new SimultaneousExecutor (getClass (),"write-snapshot");for (final HollowTypeWriteState typeState:stateEngine.getOrderedTypeStates ()) { executor.execute (new Runnable () { public void run () { typeState.calculateSnapshot ();} });} try { executor.awaitSuccessfulCompletion ();} catch (Exception e) { throw new RuntimeException (e);} for (HollowTypeWriteState typeState:stateEngine.getOrderedTypeStates ()) { HollowSchema schema = typeState.getSchema ();schema.writeTo (dos);writeNumShards (dos,typeState.getNumShards ());typeState.writeSnapshot (dos);} os.flush ();}

originalComment: Serialize the changes necessary to transition a consumer from the previous state to the current state as a delta blob.
codeComment: The `writeDelta` method writes the delta of changed data to an output stream. It first prepares the state engine for writing and ensures all necessary states are restored if the engine is restored. It then retrieves a list of changed types and writes a header to the output stream. The method uses a `SimultaneousExecutor` to calculate deltas for each type state in parallel. After all calculations are complete, it writes the schema, number of shards, and delta data for each changed type state to the output stream, and finally flushes the output stream.
codeFunctions: public void writeDelta (OutputStream os) throws IOException { stateEngine.prepareForWrite ();if (stateEngine.isRestored ()) stateEngine.ensureAllNecessaryStatesRestored ();List < HollowSchema > changedTypes = changedTypes ();DataOutputStream dos = new DataOutputStream (os);writeHeader (dos,changedTypes,false);VarInt.writeVInt (dos,changedTypes.size ());SimultaneousExecutor executor = new SimultaneousExecutor (getClass (),"write-delta");for (final HollowTypeWriteState typeState:stateEngine.getOrderedTypeStates ()) { executor.execute (new Runnable () { public void run () { if (typeState.hasChangedSinceLastCycle ()) typeState.calculateDelta ();} });} try { executor.awaitSuccessfulCompletion ();} catch (Exception e) { throw new RuntimeException (e);} for (HollowTypeWriteState typeState:stateEngine.getOrderedTypeStates ()) { if (typeState.hasChangedSinceLastCycle ()) { HollowSchema schema = typeState.getSchema ();schema.writeTo (dos);writeNumShards (dos,typeState.getNumShards ());typeState.writeDelta (dos);} } os.flush ();}

originalComment: Adds the schema name to the set if the schema name doesn t correspond to a Hollow primitive type.Factored out to prevent bloat in the switch statement it is called from.

It iterates over each `schemaName` in `schemaNames` and checks if the `schemaName` is neither a collection type nor a primitive type using the `HollowCodeGenerationUtils` utility methods. If the `schemaName` does not meet these criteria, it is added to the `schemaNameSet`.
codeFunctions: private void addToSetIfNotPrimitiveOrCollection (Set < String > schemaNameSet,String ... schemaNames) { for (String schemaName:schemaNames) { // collections schemas get brought in by a star import if (!HollowCodeGenerationUtils.isCollectionType (schemaName,dataset) &&!HollowCodeGenerationUtils.isPrimitiveType (schemaName)) { schemaNameSet.add (schemaName);} } }

originalComment: Convert field path into Param name
codeComment: The `normalizeFieldPathToParamName` method takes a `fieldPath` string as input and normalizes it into a parameter name. If the `fieldPath` contains a period (`.`), it splits the string into parts, converts the first part to lowercase, and capitalizes the first letter of each subsequent part. If the `fieldPath` does not contain a period, it simply converts the entire string to lowercase. If the resulting string ends with an exclamation mark (`!`), it removes the exclamation mark before returning the final parameter name.
codeFunctions: public static String normalizeFieldPathToParamName (String fieldPath) { String result = null;if (fieldPath.contains (".")) { String [ ] parts = fieldPath.split ("\\.");StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder ();sb.append (lowercase (parts [ 0 ]));for (int i = 1;i < parts.length;i ++) { sb.append (uppercase (parts [ i ]));} result = sb.toString ();} else { result = lowercase (fieldPath);} if (result.endsWith ("!")) { return result.substring (0,result.length () - 1);} return result;}

originalComment: Query the index.
codeComment: The `findMatches` method is designed to search for matches in a hash index based on a given query. It calculates a hash code for the query and then iterates through the hash table to find matching entries. If a match is found, it creates and returns a `HollowHashIndexResult` object containing the result. The method handles null values in the query by throwing an `IllegalArgumentException`. It uses a volatile variable to ensure thread safety during the search process.
codeFunctions: public HollowHashIndexResult findMatches (Object ... query) { int hashCode = 0;for (int i = 0;i < query.length;i ++) { if (query [ i ] == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException ("querying by null unsupported; i=" + i);hashCode ^= HashCodes.hashInt (keyHashCode (query [ i ],i));} HollowHashIndexResult result;HollowHashIndexState hashState;do { result = null;hashState = hashStateVolatile;long bucket = hashCode & hashState.getMatchHashMask ();long hashBucketBit = bucket * hashState.getBitsPerMatchHashEntry ();boolean bucketIsEmpty = hashState.getMatchHashTable ().getElementValue (hashBucketBit,hashState.getBitsPerTraverserField () [ 0 ]) == 0;while (!bucketIsEmpty) { if (matchIsEqual (hashState.getMatchHashTable (),hashBucketBit,query)) { int selectSize = (int) hashState.getMatchHashTable ().getElementValue (hashBucketBit + hashState.getBitsPerMatchHashKey (),hashState.getBitsPerSelectTableSize ());long selectBucketPointer = hashState.getMatchHashTable ().getElementValue (hashBucketBit + hashState.getBitsPerMatchHashKey () + hashState.getBitsPerSelectTableSize (),hashState.getBitsPerSelectTablePointer ());result = new HollowHashIndexResult (hashState,selectBucketPointer,selectSize);break;} bucket = (bucket + 1) & hashState.getMatchHashMask ();hashBucketBit = bucket * hashState.getBitsPerMatchHashEntry ();bucketIsEmpty = hashState.getMatchHashTable ().getElementValue (hashBucketBit,hashState.getBitsPerTraverserField () [ 0 ]) == 0;} } while (hashState != hashStateVolatile);return result;}

originalComment: Triggers async refresh after the specified number of milliseconds has passed.
codeComment: This method schedules an asynchronous refresh of a HollowClient with a specified delay. It calculates the target begin time by adding the delay to the current time. The refresh is executed in a separate thread managed by a refreshExecutor. If the calculated delay is positive, the thread sleeps for that duration before triggering the refresh. Any exceptions during this process are logged at the SEVERE level.
codeFunctions: public void triggerAsyncRefreshWithDelay (int delayMillis) { final HollowClient client = this.client;final long targetBeginTime = System.currentTimeMillis () + delayMillis;refreshExecutor.execute (new Runnable () { public void run () { try { long delay = targetBeginTime - System.currentTimeMillis ();if (delay > 0) Thread.sleep (delay);client.triggerRefresh ();} catch (Throwable th) { log.log (Level.SEVERE,"Async refresh failed",th);} } });}

originalComment: Encode the specified long as a variable length integer into the supplied OuputStream
codeComment: The `writeVLong` method writes a variable-length long integer to an output stream. It uses a form of encoding where each byte represents 7 bits of the long value, with the most significant bit (MSB) indicating whether there are more bytes following. If the value is negative, it writes a special byte `0x81` at the beginning. The method checks the value against various thresholds to determine how many bytes are needed to represent the value, writing each byte with the appropriate bits set. The final byte written has its MSB cleared to indicate the end of the value.
codeFunctions: public static void writeVLong (OutputStream out,long value) throws IOException { if (value < 0) out.write ((byte) 0x81);if (value > 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFF L || value < 0) out.write ((byte) (0x80 | ((value >>> 56) & 0x7F L)));if (value > 0x1FFFFFFFFFFFF L || value < 0) out.write ((byte) (0x80 | ((value >>> 49) & 0x7F L)));if (value > 0x3FFFFFFFFFF L || value < 0) out.write ((byte) (0x80 | ((value >>> 42) & 0x7F L)));if (value > 0x7FFFFFFFF L || value < 0) out.write ((byte) (0x80 | ((value >>> 35) & 0x7F L)));if (value > 0xFFFFFFF L || value < 0) out.write ((byte) (0x80 | ((value >>> 28) & 0x7F L)));if (value > 0x1FFFFF L || value < 0) out.write ((byte) (0x80 | ((value >>> 21) & 0x7F L)));if (value > 0x3FFF L || value < 0) out.write ((byte) (0x80 | ((value >>> 14) & 0x7F L)));if (value > 0x7F L || value < 0) out.write ((byte) (0x80 | ((value >>> 7) & 0x7F L)));out.write ((byte) (value & 0x7F L));}

originalComment: Encode the specified int as a variable length integer into the supplied OutputStream
codeComment: The `writeVInt` method writes a variable-length integer to an `OutputStream`. It checks the value of the integer and writes bytes to the stream based on the value's size. Each byte is written with the most significant bit set to 1 if there are more bytes to follow, and the remaining 7 bits contain part of the integer's value. The process continues until the entire integer is written.
codeFunctions: public static void writeVInt (OutputStream out,int value) throws IOException { if (value > 0x0FFFFFFF || value < 0) out.write ((byte) (0x80 | ((value >>> 28))));if (value > 0x1FFFFF || value < 0) out.write ((byte) (0x80 | ((value >>> 21) & 0x7F)));if (value > 0x3FFF || value < 0) out.write ((byte) (0x80 | ((value >>> 14) & 0x7F)));if (value > 0x7F || value < 0) out.write ((byte) (0x80 | ((value >>> 7) & 0x7F)));out.write ((byte) (value & 0x7F));}

codeComment: The `writeVInt` method writes a variable-length integer (`value`) into a byte array (`data`) starting at position `pos`. It uses a series of conditional checks to determine how many bytes are needed to represent the integer in a compact form. Each byte is written with the most significant bit set to 1 if there are more bytes to follow, and the remaining 7 bits contain part of the integer value. The method returns the updated position in the array after writing the integer.

originalComment: Read a variable length integer from the supplied InputStream
codeComment: This method reads a variable-length integer (vInt) from an input stream. It starts by reading a byte and checking if it is 0x80, which would indicate a null value and throw an exception. It then initializes the value with the lower 7 bits of the byte. If the byte has the 8th bit set (indicating more bytes follow), it continues reading subsequent bytes, shifting the current value left by 7 bits and combining it with the lower 7 bits of the new byte. This process repeats until a byte without the 8th bit is read, at which point the complete vInt is returned.
codeFunctions: public static int readVInt (InputStream in) throws IOException { byte b = (byte) in.read ();if (b == (byte) 0x80) throw new RuntimeException ("Attempting to read null value as int");int value = b & 0x7F;while ((b & 0x80) != 0) { b = (byte) in.read ();value <<= 7;value |= (b & 0x7F);} return value;}

It starts by reading a byte and checking if it is 0x80, which would indicate a null value and throws an exception in that case. It then initializes a long variable with the lower 7 bits of the byte. The method continues to read bytes and update the value by shifting it left by 7 bits and adding the lower 7 bits of the new byte until a byte without the 8th bit set (indicating the end of the variable-length encoding) is read. Finally, it returns the decoded long value.
codeFunctions: public static long readVLong (InputStream in) throws IOException { byte b = (byte) in.read ();if (b == (byte) 0x80) throw new RuntimeException ("Attempting to read null value as long");long value = b & 0x7F;while ((b & 0x80) != 0) { b = (byte) in.read ();value <<= 7;value |= (b & 0x7F);} return value;}

codeComment: The `pullEvent` method handles the logic for pulling events in a pull-to-refresh mechanism. It determines the scroll direction (horizontal or vertical) and calculates the new scroll value based on the initial and last motion values. Depending on the current mode (pull from start or end), it adjusts the scroll value and updates the header or footer layout accordingly. The method also checks the state to transition between pull-to-refresh and release-to-refresh states based on the scroll value and the size of the header or footer.

It takes parameters such as the view, scroll deltas, current scroll positions, scroll range, and a scale factor. The method determines the scroll direction (horizontal or vertical) and checks if over-scrolling is enabled and if the view is not currently refreshing. It then calculates the new scroll value and adjusts the header or footer scroll based on the mode and whether the over-scrolling is from touch or a fling. If the new scroll value exceeds the scroll range or falls below zero, it updates the state to OVERSCROLLING and adjusts the header or footer scroll accordingly. If the over-scrolling stops, it resets the state.

We need to just reset. view.setState (State.RESET);} } }

codeComment:
This method, `addMissingServiceParts`, is designed to enhance a `Service` object by incorporating missing parts from a `defaultService` if necessary. Here's a summary of its functionality:

1. **Check for Missing Spec**: If the `service` does not have a specification (`spec`), it takes over the entire `spec` from the `defaultService`.

2. **Check for Missing Ports**: If the `service` does not have any ports defined, it copies the ports from the `defaultService`.

3. **Complete Missing Parts**: If the `service` already has ports, it calls `addMissingDefaultPorts` to ensure that any missing ports from the `defaultService` are added to the `service`.

The method ensures that the `service` is fully configured by leveraging the `defaultService` where necessary.
codeFunctions: private void addMissingServiceParts (ServiceBuilder service,Service defaultService) { // If service has no spec -> take over the complete spec from default service if (!service.hasSpec ()) { service.withNewSpecLike (defaultService.getSpec ()).endSpec ();return;} // If service has no ports -> take over ports from default service List < ServicePort > ports = service.buildSpec ().getPorts ();if (ports == null || ports.isEmpty ()) { service.editSpec ().withPorts (defaultService.getSpec ().getPorts ()).endSpec ();return;} // Complete missing parts: service.editSpec ().withPorts (addMissingDefaultPorts (ports,defaultService)).endSpec ();}

codeComment:
This method, `appendImageStreamResource`, is responsible for creating and appending an ImageStream resource to a target file. It takes an `ImageName` object and a `File` object as parameters. The method performs the following steps:

1. **Determine the Tag**: It checks if the tag from the `ImageName` object is blank. If it is, it sets the tag to "latest"; otherwise, it uses the provided tag.

2. **Create ImageStream**: It constructs an `ImageStream` object using the `ImageStreamBuilder`. The `ImageStream` is configured with metadata (name) and a spec that includes a tag with a reference to an `ImageStreamImage`.

3. **Create or Update ImageStream Tag**: It calls `createOrUpdateImageStreamTag` to ensure the ImageStream tag is created or updated in the Kubernetes client.

4. **Append to File**: It appends the ImageStream descriptor to the specified target file using `appendImageStreamToFile`.

5. **Logging**: It logs a success message indicating that the ImageStream has been written to the target file.

6. **Exception Handling**: 
   - It catches `KubernetesClientException` and handles it using `KubernetesResourceUtil.handleKubernetesClientException`.
   - It catches `IOException` and throws a `MojoExecutionException` with a detailed error message if the ImageStream descriptor cannot be written to the file.
codeFunctions: public void appendImageStreamResource (ImageName imageName,File target) throws MojoExecutionException { String tag = StringUtils.isBlank (imageName.getTag ())?"latest":imageName.getTag ();try { ImageStream is = new ImageStreamBuilder ().withNewMetadata ().withName (imageName.getSimpleName ()).endMetadata ().withNewSpec ().addNewTag ().withName (tag).withNewFrom ().withKind ("ImageStreamImage").endFrom ().endTag ().endSpec ().build ();createOrUpdateImageStreamTag (client,imageName,is);appendImageStreamToFile (is,target);log.info ("ImageStream %s written to %s",imageName.getSimpleName (),target);} catch (KubernetesClientException e) { KubernetesResourceUtil.handleKubernetesClientException (e,this.log);} catch (IOException e) { throw new MojoExecutionException (String.format ("Cannot write ImageStream descriptor for %s to %s : %s",imageName.getFullName (),target.getAbsoluteFile (),e.getMessage ()),e);} }

codeComment:
This method reads a resource file, validates its name, and enriches its content with metadata such as `apiVersion` and `kind`. Here's a summary of the steps:

1. **File Name Validation**: The method first checks if the file name matches a specific pattern (`<name>-<type>.(yaml|yml|json)`). If not, it throws an `IllegalArgumentException`.

2. **Extracting File Details**: It extracts the `name`, `type`, and file extension (`ext`) from the file name.

3. **Reading the File**: The method reads the file content into a `Map<String, Object>` using the `readFragment` method.

4. **Determine `kind`**: 
   - If a `type` is provided, it validates and uses it as the `kind`.
   - If no `type` is provided, it attempts to map the `name` to a `kind` using a predefined `FILENAME_TO_KIND_MAPPER`.

5. **Add `kind` to Fragment**: The `kind` is added to the fragment map.

6. **Determine `apiVersion`**: 
   - The `apiVersion` is set based on the `kind` and the platform mode.
   - Specific versions are assigned for `Ingress`, `StatefulSet`, `Deployment`, `Job`, and `DeploymentConfig` on OpenShift.

7. **Add `apiVersion` to Fragment**: The `apiVersion` is added to the fragment map if it doesn't already exist.

8. **Add Metadata**: 
   - The method retrieves the metadata from the fragment.
   - It ensures that the `name` field in the metadata is set, using the extracted `name` or the provided `appName` if the `name` is not available.

9. **Return the Fragment**: The enriched fragment map is returned.
codeFunctions: private static Map < String,Object > readAndEnrichFragment (PlatformMode platformMode,ResourceVersioning apiVersions,File file,String appName) throws IOException { Pattern pattern = Pattern.compile (FILENAME_PATTERN,Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE);Matcher matcher = pattern.matcher (file.getName ());if (!matcher.matches ()) { throw new IllegalArgumentException (String.format ("Resource file name '%s' does not match pattern <name>-<type>.(yaml|yml|json)",file.getName ()));} String name = matcher.group ("name");String type = matcher.group ("type");String ext = matcher.group ("ext").toLowerCase ();String kind;Map < String,Object > fragment = readFragment (file,ext);if (type != null) { kind = getAndValidateKindFromType (file,type);} else { // Try name as type kind = FILENAME_TO_KIND_MAPPER.get (name.toLowerCase ());if (kind != null) { // Name is in fact the type, so lets erase the name. name = null;} } addKind (fragment,kind,file.getName ());String apiVersion = apiVersions.getCoreVersion ();if (Objects.equals (kind,"Ingress")) { apiVersion = apiVersions.getExtensionsVersion ();} else if (Objects.equals (kind,"StatefulSet") || Objects.equals (kind,"Deployment")) { apiVersion = apiVersions.getAppsVersion ();} else if (Objects.equals (kind,"Job")) { apiVersion = apiVersions.getJobVersion ();} else if (Objects.equals (kind,"DeploymentConfig") && platformMode == PlatformMode.openshift) { apiVersion = apiVersions.getOpenshiftV1version ();} addIfNotExistent (fragment,"apiVersion",apiVersion);Map < String,Object > metaMap = getMetadata (fragment);// No name means: generated app name should be taken as resource name addIfNotExistent (metaMap,"name",StringUtils.isNotBlank (name)?name:appName);return fragment;}

originalComment: Download with showing the progress a given URL and store it in a file
codeComment:
This method, `download`, is responsible for downloading a file from a specified URL to a target file location. It uses an `OkHttpClient` to handle the HTTP request and response. The method logs the progress of the download and handles exceptions by throwing a `MojoExecutionException` if the download fails. Here's a summary of the steps:

1. **Initialize Logger and Client**: The method starts by logging the beginning of the download process. It then creates an `OkHttpClient` with a read timeout of 30 minutes.

2. **Create Request**: A `Request` object is built using the provided `downloadUrl`.

3. **Execute Request**: The request is executed, and the response is obtained.

4. **Write Response to File**: The response body is read in chunks using a buffer. The method logs the progress of the download using a progress bar. The data is written to the target file using an `OutputStream`.

5. **Handle Exceptions**: If an `IOException` occurs during the download, a `MojoExecutionException` is thrown with an appropriate error message.

6. **Finalize Logging**: Regardless of the outcome, the method logs the completion of the download process.
codeFunctions: public static void download (Logger log,URL downloadUrl,File target) throws MojoExecutionException { log.progressStart ();try { OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient.Builder ().readTimeout (30,TimeUnit.MINUTES).build ();Request request = new Request.Builder ().url (downloadUrl).build ();Response response = client.newCall (request).execute ();try (OutputStream out = new FileOutputStream (target);InputStream im = response.body ().byteStream ()) { long length = response.body ().contentLength ();InputStream in = response.body ().byteStream ();byte [ ] buffer = new byte [ 8192 ];long readBytes = 0;while (true) { int len = in.read (buffer);readBytes += len;log.progressUpdate (target.getName (),"Downloading",getProgressBar (readBytes,length));if (len <= 0) { out.flush ();break;} out.write (buffer,0,len);} } } catch (IOException e) { throw new MojoExecutionException ("Failed to download URL " + downloadUrl + " to  " + target + ": " + e,e);} finally { log.progressFinished ();} }

originalComment: Compares two version strings such that 1.10.1 > 1.4 etc
codeComment: The `compareVersions` method compares two version strings (`v1` and `v2`) by splitting them into components, comparing each component numerically if possible, and falling back to lexicographical comparison if not. It returns an integer indicating the order of the two versions.
codeFunctions:
public static int compareVersions (String v1,String v2) { String [ ] components1 = split (v1);String [ ] components2 = split (v2);int diff;int length = Math.min (components1.length,components2.length);for (int i = 0;i < length;i ++) { String s1 = components1 [ i ];String s2 = components2 [ i ];Integer i1 = tryParseInteger (s1);Integer i2 = tryParseInteger (s2);if (i1 != null && i2 != null) { diff = i1.compareTo (i2);} else { // lets assume strings instead diff = s1.compareTo (s2);} if (diff != 0) { return diff;} } diff = Integer.compare (components1.length,components2.length);if (diff == 0) { if (v1 == v2) { return 0;} /* if v1 == null then v2 can't be null here (see 'if' above).
               So for v1 == null its always smaller than v2 */;return v1 != null?v1.compareTo (v2):- 1;} return diff;}
