originalComment: Calculates the Activity TTL
codeComment: This method calculates the Time To Live (TTL) for a given resource. It takes two parameters: `lastAccess`, a string representing the last access time in milliseconds, and `timeout`, a long representing the total timeout period in milliseconds. The method computes the TTL by subtracting the elapsed time (since the last access) from the timeout. The elapsed time is calculated by subtracting the `lastAccess` time from the current time and converting it to seconds. The result is then converted to a string and returned.
codeFunctions: private static String toTTL (String lastAccess,long timeout) { Long ttl = timeout - ((System.currentTimeMillis () - Long.parseLong (lastAccess)) / 1000);return ttl.toString ();}

originalComment: Retrieves a local object valid for thus current transaction.
codeComment: This method, `getProfileObjectValidInCurrentTransaction`, retrieves a `ProfileObjectImpl` for a given `ProfileEntity` within the context of the current transaction. It ensures that the transaction is mandatory and checks if the object is already cached locally. If not, it fetches the object from the pool, activates it with the profile entity, and caches it for future use within the same transaction.
codeFunctions: ProfileObjectImpl getProfileObjectValidInCurrentTransaction (ProfileEntity profileEntity) throws TransactionRequiredLocalException { // check tx final SleeTransactionManager txManager = profileManagement.getSleeContainer ().getTransactionManager ();txManager.mandateTransaction ();// look for an assigned object in local map if (txData == null) { txData = new HashMap < ProfileEntity,ProfileObjectImpl > ();} ProfileObjectImpl profileObject = (ProfileObjectImpl) txData.get (profileEntity);if (profileObject == null) { // get an object from the table profileEntity.setReadOnly (true);profileEntity.setDirty (false);ProfileObjectPool pool = profileManagement.getObjectPoolManagement ().getObjectPool (profileEntity.getTableName ());profileObject = pool.borrowObject ();profileObject.profileActivate (profileEntity);ProfileTableTransactionView.passivateProfileObjectOnTxEnd (txManager,profileObject,pool);txData.put (profileEntity,profileObject);} return profileObject;}

codeComment: This method converts a tracer name and a notification source into a Log4J logger name. It starts by creating a `StringBuilder` with the prefix "javax.slee." followed by the string representation of the `notificationSource`. If the `tracerName` is not equal to `ROOT_TRACER_NAME`, it appends a space and the `tracerName` to the `StringBuilder`. Finally, it returns the constructed string.
codeFunctions: private String tracerNameToLog4JLoggerName (String tracerName,NotificationSource notificationSource) { final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder ("javax.slee.").append (notificationSource.toString ());if (!tracerName.equals (ROOT_TRACER_NAME)) { sb.append (' ').append (tracerName);} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: syncs the slee tracer level with the one that related logger has in log4j
codeComment: This method, `syncLevelWithLog4j`, synchronizes the logging level of a logger with the level set in Log4j. It first retrieves the effective level from Log4j, either from the root logger or a specific logger. If the current level is not set, it assigns the Log4j level to the logger. If the current level is set but differs from the Log4j level, it updates the logger's level. For the root logger, if no level is set, it defaults to `INFO`. Finally, it resets certain cache flags.
codeFunctions: void syncLevelWithLog4j () { // get the level from log4j, only the root one uses effective level Level log4jLevel = parent == null?logger.getEffectiveLevel ():logger.getLevel ();if (level == null) { // set the level assignLog4JLevel (log4jLevel);} else { // set the level only if differs, otherwise we may loose levels not present in log4j if (tracerToLog4JLevel (level) != log4jLevel) { assignLog4JLevel (log4jLevel);} } // the root must always have a level if (parent == null && level == null) { // defaults to INFO logger.setLevel (Level.INFO);level = TraceLevel.INFO;} // reset the flags resetCacheFlags (false);}

originalComment: assigns the equiv log4j level to the tracer
codeComment:
This method, `assignLog4JLevel`, maps a given Log4J `Level` to a corresponding `TraceLevel`. It first checks if the input `log4jLevel` is `null` and returns immediately if so. Otherwise, it uses a series of `if-else` statements to match the `log4jLevel` to the appropriate `TraceLevel` and assigns it to the `level` variable. The mappings are as follows:

- `Level.DEBUG` maps to `TraceLevel.FINE`
- `Level.INFO` maps to `TraceLevel.INFO`
- `Level.WARN` maps to `TraceLevel.WARNING`
- `Level.ERROR` maps to `TraceLevel.SEVERE`
- `Level.TRACE` maps to `TraceLevel.FINEST`
- `Level.OFF` maps to `TraceLevel.OFF`
codeFunctions: private void assignLog4JLevel (Level log4jLevel) { if (log4jLevel == null) { return;} if (log4jLevel == Level.DEBUG) { level = TraceLevel.FINE;} else if (log4jLevel == Level.INFO) { level = TraceLevel.INFO;} else if (log4jLevel == Level.WARN) { level = TraceLevel.WARNING;} else if (log4jLevel == Level.ERROR) { level = TraceLevel.SEVERE;} else if (log4jLevel == Level.TRACE) { level = TraceLevel.FINEST;} else if (log4jLevel == Level.OFF) { level = TraceLevel.OFF;} }

originalComment: manages the flags which cache if levels are enabled
codeComment: The `resetCacheFlags` method resets the trace level flags (`finestEnabled`, `finerEnabled`, `fineEnabled`, `configEnabled`, `infoEnabled`, `warningEnabled`, `severeEnabled`) based on the current trace level. It starts by checking if the trace level is `FINEST` and sets all flags to `true` if it is. If not, it proceeds to check for lower levels (`FINER`, `FINE`, `CONFIG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `SEVERE`) and sets the corresponding flags to `true` if the current level is equal to or higher than the checked level. If `resetChilds` is `true`, it recursively calls `resetCacheFlags` on child tracers that do not have a specified level.
codeFunctions: void resetCacheFlags (boolean resetChilds) { if (isTraceable (TraceLevel.FINEST)) { finestEnabled = true;finerEnabled = true;fineEnabled = true;configEnabled = true;infoEnabled = true;warningEnabled = true;severeEnabled = true;} else { finestEnabled = false;if (isTraceable (TraceLevel.FINER)) { finerEnabled = true;fineEnabled = true;configEnabled = true;infoEnabled = true;warningEnabled = true;severeEnabled = true;} else { finerEnabled = false;if (isTraceable (TraceLevel.FINE)) { fineEnabled = true;configEnabled = true;infoEnabled = true;warningEnabled = true;severeEnabled = true;} else { fineEnabled = false;if (isTraceable (TraceLevel.CONFIG)) { configEnabled = true;infoEnabled = true;warningEnabled = true;severeEnabled = true;} else { if (isTraceable (TraceLevel.INFO)) { infoEnabled = true;warningEnabled = true;severeEnabled = true;} else { infoEnabled = false;if (isTraceable (TraceLevel.WARNING)) { warningEnabled = true;severeEnabled = true;} else { warningEnabled = false;if (isTraceable (TraceLevel.SEVERE)) { severeEnabled = true;} else { severeEnabled = false;} } } } } } } if (resetChilds) { // implicit change of level demands that we update reset flags on childs without level for (TracerImpl child:childs) { if (child.level == null) { child.resetCacheFlags (true);} } } }

originalComment: This checks if the specified tracer name is ok.
codeComment: The `checkTracerName` method validates a tracer name by ensuring it does not contain consecutive dots and is not empty. It throws a `NullPointerException` if the input is null and an `InvalidArgumentException` if the tracer name is invalid. The method uses a `StringTokenizer` to split the tracer name by dots and checks for consecutive dots or a trailing dot.
codeFunctions: public static void checkTracerName (String tracerName,NotificationSource notificationSource) throws NullPointerException,InvalidArgumentException { if (tracerName.equals ("")) { // This is root return;} StringTokenizer stringTokenizer = new StringTokenizer (tracerName,".",true);String lastToken = null;while (stringTokenizer.hasMoreTokens ()) { String token = stringTokenizer.nextToken ();if (lastToken == null) { // this is start lastToken = token;} if (lastToken.equals (token) && token.equals (".")) { throw new InvalidArgumentException ("Passed tracer:" + tracerName + ", name for source: " + notificationSource + ", is illegal");} lastToken = token;} if (lastToken.equals (".")) { throw new IllegalArgumentException ("Passed tracer:" + tracerName + ", name for source: " + notificationSource + ", is illegal");} }

originalComment: Write the current object and vendor - specific data to the output stream.
codeComment: This method, `writeObject`, is responsible for serializing an object using an `ObjectOutputStream`. It first writes the non-transient fields of the object using `out.defaultWriteObject()`. Then, it checks if there is any vendor data to serialize. If `vendorData` is not null, it writes a boolean `true` to indicate the presence of vendor data, followed by the vendor data itself, wrapped in a `MarshalledObject` to defer deserialization. If `vendorData` is null, it writes a boolean `false` to indicate the absence of vendor data.
codeFunctions: public static void writeObject (ObjectOutputStream out,Object vendorData) throws IOException { // write non-transient fields out.defaultWriteObject ();// check if should we serialize vendor data? if (vendorData != null) { // serialize the vendor data out.writeBoolean (true);// write the vendor data in a marshalled object so deserialization can be deferred out.writeObject (new MarshalledObject (vendorData));} else out.writeBoolean (false);}

originalComment: Read the current object in the input stream from the stream optionally deserializing any vendor - specific data in the stream.
codeComment: The `readObject` method is designed to deserialize an object from an `ObjectInputStream`. It first reads the non-transient fields using `in.defaultReadObject()`. Then, it checks if there is any marshalled vendor data in the stream. If there is, it reads the `MarshalledObject` and, if `vendorDataDeserializationEnabled` is true, deserializes and returns the vendor data. If there is no vendor data or deserialization is disabled, it returns null.
codeFunctions: public static Object readObject (ObjectInputStream in,boolean vendorDataDeserializationEnabled) throws IOException,ClassNotFoundException { // read non-transient fields in.defaultReadObject ();// read any possible marshalled vendor data from the stream MarshalledObject vendorData = in.readBoolean ()?(MarshalledObject) in.readObject ():null;// now figure out what to return return (vendorData != null && vendorDataDeserializationEnabled)?vendorData.get ():null;}

originalComment: Finds a class locally i.e.in the URLs managed by the extended URLClassLoader.
codeComment: The method `findClassLocally` attempts to find a class by name within a local context. It first checks if tracing is enabled and logs the method call if so. It then acquires a global lock and, within a try-finally block, calls `findClassLocallyLocked` to perform the actual class lookup. Regardless of whether the lock was acquired, it ensures the lock is released in the finally block to prevent resource leaks. If the class is not found, it throws a `ClassNotFoundException`.
codeFunctions: protected Class <?> findClassLocally (String name) throws ClassNotFoundException { if (logger.isTraceEnabled ()) { logger.trace (toString () + " findClassLocally: " + name);} final boolean acquiredLock = acquireGlobalLock ();try { return findClassLocallyLocked (name);} finally { if (acquiredLock) { releaseGlobalLock ();} } }

originalComment: Finds a resource locally i.e.in the URLs managed by the extended URLClassLoader.
codeComment: The method `findResourceLocally` is a protected method that takes a `String` parameter `name`. It first checks if the logger is enabled for trace level logging. Please proceed.",e);throw new NestedException ("ADB init failed",e);} } bridge = AndroidDebugBridge.getBridge ();if (bridge == null) { bridge = AndroidDebugBridge.createBridge (AndroidSdk.adb ().getAbsolutePath (),false);} long timeout = System.currentTimeMillis () + 60000;while (!bridge.hasInitialDeviceList () && System.currentTimeMillis () < timeout) { try { Thread.sleep (50);} catch (InterruptedException e) { throw new RuntimeException (e);} } // Add the existing devices to the list of devices we are tracking. codeComment:
The `generateLabelValue` method processes a given field name to generate a label value. It uses a `StringBuilder` to build the resulting string and a nested `GenerationCommand` class to handle the transformation logic. The method iterates over each character in the input field name, applying various rules to determine how to format the output:

1. **Character Processing**:
   - **Numbers**: If a number is encountered and it follows a non-number character, a space is added before the number.
   - **Uppercase Letters**: If an uppercase letter is encountered and it follows a non-uppercase character, a space is added before the letter.
   - **Special Characters**: If a space or underscore is encountered, a space is added, and the next character is capitalized.
   - **First Character**: The first character of the field name is always capitalized.

2. **State Tracking**:
   - The method keeps track of whether the last character was a number, uppercase, special, or if the next character should be capitalized.

3. **Final Output**:
   - The resulting string is returned after processing all characters, with any double spaces replaced by a single space.

This method is designed to convert camelCase or snake_case field names into a more readable label format.
codeFunctions:
public static String generateLabelValue (final String fieldName) { final StringBuilder buffer = new StringBuilder (fieldName.length () * 2);class GenerationCommand { boolean capNextChar = false;boolean lastCharWasUpperCase = false;boolean lastCharWasNumber = false;boolean lastCharWasSpecial = false;boolean shouldContinue = true;char [ ] chars = fieldName.toCharArray ();void processFieldName () { for (int index = 0;index < chars.length;index ++) { char cchar = chars [ index ];shouldContinue = true;processCharWasNumber (buffer,index,cchar);if (!shouldContinue) { continue;} processCharWasUpperCase (buffer,index,cchar);if (!shouldContinue) { continue;} processSpecialChars (buffer,cchar);if (!shouldContinue) { continue;} cchar = processCapitalizeCommand (cchar);cchar = processFirstCharacterCheck (buffer,index,cchar);if (!shouldContinue) { continue;} buffer.append (cchar);} } private void processCharWasNumber (StringBuilder buffer,int index,char cchar) { if (lastCharWasSpecial) { return;} if (Character.isDigit (cchar)) { if (index != 0 &&!lastCharWasNumber) { buffer.append (' ');} lastCharWasNumber = true;buffer.append (cchar);this.shouldContinue = false;} else { lastCharWasNumber = false;} } private char processFirstCharacterCheck (final StringBuilder buffer,int index,char cchar) { /* Always capitalize the first character. */ if (index == 0) { cchar = Character.toUpperCase (cchar);buffer.append (cchar);this.shouldContinue = false;} return cchar;} private char processCapitalizeCommand (char cchar) { /* Capitalize the character. */ if (capNextChar) { capNextChar = false;cchar = Character.toUpperCase (cchar);} return cchar;} private void processSpecialChars (final StringBuilder buffer,char cchar) { lastCharWasSpecial = false;/* If the character is '.' or '_' then append a space and mark
                 * the next iteration to capitalize.
				 */ if (cchar == ' ' || cchar == ' ') { buffer.append (' ');capNextChar = true;lastCharWasSpecial = false;this.shouldContinue = false;} } private void processCharWasUpperCase (final StringBuilder buffer,int index,char cchar) { /* If the character is uppercase, append a space and keep track
                 * that the last character was uppercase for the next iteration.
				 */ if (Character.isUpperCase (cchar)) { if (index != 0 &&!lastCharWasUpperCase) { buffer.append (' ');} lastCharWasUpperCase = true;buffer.append (cchar);this.shouldContinue = false;} else { lastCharWasUpperCase = false;} } } GenerationCommand gc = new GenerationCommand ();gc.processFieldName ();/* This is a hack to get address.line_1 to work. */ return buffer.toString ().replace ("  "," ");}

codeComment: The `processWriteQueue` method processes a queue of write operations for a data store. It continuously polls the `writeOperationsQueue` for operations, adding them to a batch until the batch size reaches the configured maximum or the queue is empty. originalComment: Start up the queue handlers.
codeComment:
The `start` method initializes a scheduled executor service with a thread pool of size 2, where each thread is named based on the `source`. It then schedules two tasks to run at a fixed rate:

1. The first task processes the write queue. It checks if the `stop` flag is set, and if not, it attempts to process the write queue. If an `InterruptedException` occurs, it allows the task to restart or stop. Any other exceptions are logged as fatal.

2. The second task processes the read queue. Similar to the first task, it checks the `stop` flag, processes the read queue, and handles exceptions in the same manner.

Both tasks are scheduled to run immediately (0 delay) and repeat at a fixed rate determined by `dataStoreConfig.threadErrorResumeTimeMS()` in milliseconds.
codeFunctions: public void start () { scheduledExecutorService = Executors.newScheduledThreadPool (2,new ThreadFactory () { @ Override public Thread newThread (Runnable runnable) { Thread thread = new Thread (runnable);thread.setName (" DataQueue Process " + source);return thread;} });future = scheduledExecutorService.scheduleAtFixedRate (new Runnable () { @ Override public void run () { if (stop.get ()) { return;} try { processWriteQueue ();} catch (InterruptedException ex) { //let it restart or stop } catch (Exception ex) { logger.fatal (ex);} } },0,dataStoreConfig.threadErrorResumeTimeMS (),TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);future = scheduledExecutorService.scheduleAtFixedRate (new Runnable () { @ Override public void run () { if (stop.get ()) { return;} try { processReadQueue ();} catch (InterruptedException ex) { //let it restart or stop } catch (Exception ex) { logger.fatal (ex,"Problem with base data store running scheduled job");} } },0,dataStoreConfig.threadErrorResumeTimeMS (),TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);}

codeComment:
The method `num` takes a `Number` object as input and returns a formatted string representation of the number. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Null Check**: If the input `count` is `null`, the method returns an empty string.

2. **Double and BigDecimal Handling**:
   - If `count` is an instance of `Double` or `BigDecimal`, it converts the number to a string.
   - If the string representation has a space at the second position and is longer than 7 characters, it truncates the string to the first 5 characters.
   - Otherwise, it returns the full string representation.

3. **Integer, Long, Short, and BigInteger Handling**:
   - If `count` is an instance of `Integer`, `Long`, `Short`, or `BigInteger`, it converts the number to a string.
   - It reverses the string, then iterates through each character, adding a space every three characters.
   - If the last character is a space, it removes it.
   - Finally, it reverses the string again to restore the original order and returns it.

4. **Default Handling**: If `count` is none of the above types, it simply returns the string representation of `count`.
codeFunctions: public static String num (Number count) { if (count == null) { return "";} if (count instanceof Double || count instanceof BigDecimal) { String s = count.toString ();if (idx (s,1) == ' ' && s.length () > 7) { s = slc (s,0,5);return s;} else { return s;} } else if (count instanceof Integer || count instanceof Long || count instanceof Short || count instanceof BigInteger) { String s = count.toString ();s = new StringBuilder (s).reverse ().toString ();CharBuf buf = CharBuf.create (s.length ());int index = 0;for (char c:s.toCharArray ()) { index ++;buf.add (c);if (index % 3 == 0) { buf.add (' ');} } if (buf.lastChar () == ' ') { buf.removeLastChar ();} s = buf.toString ();s = new StringBuilder (s).reverse ().toString ();return s;} return count.toString ();}

             * required; length min=10, max=100
             * So we need to split on semi-colon.
             */ String [ ] validatorsParts = unparsedString.split ("[;]");/* Now we have the two strings as follows:
             *  ["required",
             *  ["length min=10, max=100"]
             *
             */ for (String validatorString:validatorsParts) { ValidatorMetaData validatorMetaData = new ValidatorMetaData ();validatorMetaDataList.add (validatorMetaData);/* Now we split one of the string (we will use length) 
                 * as follows: 
                 * parts=["length", "min=10", "max=100"]

                 * e.g., "length".
                 * 
                 */ validatorMetaData.setName (parts [ 0 ]);/* If the string has more than one part, then there must
                 * be arguments as in: ["min=10", "max=100"]

                 * Parse the arguments and addObject them to the list as well.

                     * 
                     * ["length", "min=10", "max=100"]

                     * into:

                     */ List < String > values = Arrays.asList (parts).subList (1,parts.length);/* For each value convert it into name value pairs. */ for (String value:values) { if (value.indexOf ("=") != - 1) { /* Split "min=10" into ["min", "10"] */ String [ ] valueParts = value.split ("[=]");/* Stick this value into validatorMetaData's

If the property is a digit, it attempts to index the object using the parsed integer value. It then retrieves the class of the object and tries to find the property using getter methods.    - If the resource is found within a JAR file (`dirURL.getProtocol().equals("jar")`), it extracts the JAR file path, decodes it, and opens the JAR file.
   - It then iterates over the entries in the JAR file, filtering entries that start with a specific directory (`SPRING_BOOT_DIR`) and match the specified `path`.
   - For each matching entry, it extracts the file name, removes any subdirectories, and adds it to a `Set<String>` to ensure uniqueness.
   - Finally, it closes the JAR file and returns the list of resource names.

4. **Exception Handling**: If any exceptions occur during the process, they are caught, and a `CouchDbException` is thrown.

5. **Return Value**: The method returns a list of resource names if found, or `null` if no resources are found at the specified path.
codeFunctions: public static List < String > listResources (String path) { try { Class < CouchDbUtil > clazz = CouchDbUtil.class;URL dirURL = clazz.getClassLoader ().getResource (path);if (dirURL != null && dirURL.getProtocol ().equals ("file")) { return Arrays.asList (new File (dirURL.toURI ()).list ());} if (dirURL != null && dirURL.getProtocol ().equals ("jar")) { String jarPath = dirURL.getPath ().substring (5,dirURL.getPath ().indexOf ("!"));JarFile jar = new JarFile (URLDecoder.decode (jarPath,"UTF-8"));Enumeration < JarEntry > entries = jar.entries ();Set < String > result = new HashSet < String > ();while (entries.hasMoreElements ()) { String name = entries.nextElement ().getName ();if (name.startsWith (SPRING_BOOT_DIR)) { name = name.substring (SPRING_BOOT_DIR.length ());} if (name.startsWith (path)) { String entry = name.substring (path.length ());int checkSubdir = entry.indexOf ("/");if (checkSubdir >= 0) { entry = entry.substring (0,checkSubdir);} if (entry.length () > 0) { result.add (entry);} } } close (jar);return new ArrayList < String > (result);} return null;} catch (Exception e) { throw new CouchDbException (e);} }

originalComment: Queries for scalar values.Internal use.
codeComment:
The `queryValue` method is designed to query a JSON stream, parse it, and extract a single value of a specified type. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Input Parameter**: 
   - `Class<V> classOfV`: The class type of the value to be returned.

2. **Process**:
   - Opens an input stream using `queryForStream()`.
   - Reads the stream into a `Reader` using UTF-8 character encoding.
   - Parses the JSON content into a `JsonArray` from the "rows" field of the JSON object.
   - Checks if the size of the array is exactly one. If not, it throws a `NoDocumentException`.
   - Converts the first element of the array to an object of type `V` using `JsonToObject` method and returns it.

3. **Resource Management**:
   - Ensures the input stream is closed in the `finally` block to prevent resource leaks.

4. **Exception Handling**:
   - Throws `NoDocumentException` if the expected single result is not found.

This method is useful for retrieving a single JSON object from a stream and converting it to a specified Java object type.
codeFunctions: private < V > V queryValue (Class < V > classOfV) { InputStream instream = null;try { Reader reader = new InputStreamReader (instream = queryForStream (),Charsets.UTF_8);JsonArray array = new JsonParser ().parse (reader).getAsJsonObject ().get ("rows").getAsJsonArray ();if (array.size () != 1) { throw new NoDocumentException ("Expecting a single result but was: " + array.size ());} return JsonToObject (gson,array.get (0),"value",classOfV);} finally { close (instream);} }

codeComment:
The `getFromDesk` method retrieves a `DesignDocument` object from a specified directory based on the provided `id`. It performs the following steps:

2. **Directory Initialization**: Constructs the root path for the design document using the `DESIGN_DOCS_DIR` and the provided `id`.

4. **Views Processing**:

   - If it does, initializes a `Map` to store views.
   - Iterates through each view sub-directory, creating a `MapReduce` object for each.
   - Reads and sets the map and reduce functions from the respective JavaScript files.
5. **Design Document Construction**: 
   - Sets the `id`, `language`, and `views` of the `DesignDocument`.
   - Populates `filters`, `shows`, `lists`, and `updates` using the `populateMap` method.
   - Reads and sets `validateDocUpdate`, `rewrites`, `fulltext`, and `indexes` from the respective files.
6. **Return**: Returns the constructed `DesignDocument` object.

For other status codes, it retrieves the reason phrase and throws exceptions such as `NoDocumentException` for 404, `DocumentConflictException` for 409, and `CouchDbException` for other error codes, including appending the response entity's content to the reason phrase.
codeFunctions: void validate (HttpResponse response) throws IOException { final int code = response.getStatusLine ().getStatusCode ();if (code == 200 || code == 201 || code == 202) { // success (ok | created | accepted) return;} String reason = response.getStatusLine ().getReasonPhrase ();switch (code) { case HttpStatus.SC_NOT_FOUND:{ throw new NoDocumentException (reason);} case HttpStatus.SC_CONFLICT:{ throw new DocumentConflictException (reason);} default:{ // other errors: 400 | 401 | 500 etc. throw new CouchDbException (reason += EntityUtils.toString (response.getEntity ()));} } }

This method, `isQuery`, determines whether an HTTP request represented by `HttpServerExchange` is a query. It checks the request method:

- If the method is "POST", it checks if the request path matches a predefined pattern (`postQuery`). If it does, it returns `true`; otherwise, it returns `false`.

codeFunctions: private boolean isQuery (HttpServerExchange serverExchange) { if (serverExchange.getRequestMethod ().toString ().equalsIgnoreCase ("GET") || serverExchange.getRequestMethod ().toString ().equalsIgnoreCase ("HEAD")) { // all GET requests are considered queries return true;} else if (serverExchange.getRequestMethod ().toString ().equalsIgnoreCase ("POST")) { // some POST requests may be queries we need to check. if (postQuery != null && postQuery.matcher (serverExchange.getRelativePath ()).find ()) { return true;} else { return false;} } else { return false;} }

This method, `findScheduledJobs`, retrieves scheduled jobs from a database session and processes them into `JobDetails` objects. It uses an RxJava `Observable` to handle asynchronous operations. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Database Query Execution**: The method executes a query using `session.executeAndFetch` with a bound statement `findAllScheduled` and a specified scheduler.

2. **Filtering**: It filters out null jobs and jobs whose timestamp is greater than the provided `timeSlice`.

3. **Mapping**: Each row from the query result is mapped to a `JobDetails` object, extracting necessary fields such as UUID, strings, maps, triggers, job status, and the time slice.

4. **Collecting**: The `JobDetails` objects are collected into a `HashMap` where the key is the job ID (`UUID`) and the value is a `SortedSet` of `JobDetails` sorted by trigger time.

5. **Flattening and Mapping**: The `HashMap` entries are flattened into an `Observable` of `SortedSet` entries, and then each set is mapped to its first element, effectively selecting the earliest scheduled job for each job ID.

6. **Return Value**: The method returns an `Observable` of `JobDetails` objects representing the earliest scheduled jobs for each job ID.
codeFunctions: public Observable < JobDetails > findScheduledJobs (Date timeSlice,rx.Scheduler scheduler) { return session.executeAndFetch (findAllScheduled.bind (),scheduler).filter (filterNullJobs).filter (row -> row.getTimestamp (0).compareTo (timeSlice) <= 0).map (row -> createJobDetails (row.getUUID (1),row.getString (2),row.getString (3),row.getMap (4,String.class,String.class),getTrigger (row.getUDTValue (5)),JobStatus.fromCode (row.getByte (6)),timeSlice)).collect (HashMap :: new,(Map < UUID,SortedSet < JobDetails > > map,JobDetails details) -> { SortedSet < JobDetails > set = map.get (details.getJobId ());if (set == null) { set = new TreeSet <> ((JobDetails d1,JobDetails d2) -> Long.compare (d1.getTrigger ().getTriggerTime (),d2.getTrigger ().getTriggerTime ()));} set.add (details);map.put (details.getJobId (),set);}).flatMap (map -> Observable.from (map.entrySet ())).map (entry -> entry.getValue ().first ());}

Otherwise, it calculates the number of buckets by dividing the range by the step and adjusting for any remainder. It ensures the count does not exceed `Integer.MAX_VALUE` and then returns the `Buckets` object with the calculated parameters.
codeFunctions: public static Buckets fromStep (long start,long end,long step) { checkTimeRange (start,end);checkArgument (step > 0,"step is not positive: %s",step);if (step > (end - start)) { return new Buckets (start,step,1);} long quotient = (end - start) / step;long remainder = (end - start) % step;long count;if (remainder == 0) { count = quotient;} else { count = quotient + 1;} checkArgument (count <= Integer.MAX_VALUE,"Computed number of buckets is too big: %s",count);return new Buckets (start,step,(int) count);}

originalComment: Insert the given categories and their entries into the any existing categories of the same title.If a category doesn t match an existing one add it to the list.
codeComment:
The `addCategories` method is designed to add new notification categories to an existing list of categories. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Null Check**: The method first checks if the `newCategories` list is null. If it is, the method returns immediately.

2. **Deep Copy**: A deep copy of the `newCategories` list is created using `parallelStream` and `map` to clone each `NotificationCategory` object. This simplifies the logic for subsequent operations.

3. **Mapping Current Categories**: The current categories are mapped into a `Map` called `catsByName`, where the key is the lowercase title of the category and the value is the `NotificationCategory` object itself.

4. **Partitioning New Categories**: The new categories are partitioned into two lists:
   - `matchingNewCats.get(Boolean.TRUE)`: Categories that have a matching title in the current categories.
   - `matchingNewCats.get(Boolean.FALSE)`: Categories that do not have a matching title in the current categories.

5. **Updating Existing Categories**: For categories that match an existing category, their entries are added to the existing category using `addEntries`.

6. **Adding New Categories**: Categories that do not match any existing category are added to the `categories` list.

This method ensures that new categories are either merged with existing ones or added as new entries, maintaining the integrity of the category list.
codeFunctions: private void addCategories (List < NotificationCategory > newCategories) { if (newCategories == null) { return;} // Start with a deep copy of the method parameter to simplify remaining logic newCategories = newCategories.parallelStream ().map (NotificationCategory :: cloneNoExceptions).collect (Collectors.toList ());// Create a map of current categories by title for processing Map < String,NotificationCategory > catsByName = this.categories.parallelStream ().collect (toMap (c -> c.getTitle ().toLowerCase (),c -> c));// Split new categories between those that match an existing category and those that are completely new Map < Boolean,List < NotificationCategory > > matchingNewCats = newCategories.stream ().collect (partitioningBy (c -> catsByName.containsKey (c.getTitle ().toLowerCase ())));// Add new entries to existing categories matchingNewCats.get (Boolean.TRUE).stream ().forEachOrdered (c -> catsByName.get (c.getTitle ().toLowerCase ()).addEntries (c.getEntries ()));// Add new categories this.categories.addAll (matchingNewCats.get (Boolean.FALSE));}

codeComment: This method, `fetch`, retrieves notifications for a user in a portlet environment. It first checks if notifications are enabled through portlet preferences. If the API request fails or returns an unsuccessful status, it logs the error and returns an error response. If successful, it maps the API response to a `NotificationResponse` and returns it.

originalComment: Map and SSP Response to a NotificationResponse.
codeComment: This method, `mapToNotificationResponse`, processes a `PortletRequest` and a `ResponseEntity<String>` to create a `NotificationResponse`. It uses JSONPath to parse the response body and extract relevant data. The method checks if the response indicates success; if not, it returns an error notification. It then reads task data, validates it, and maps it to `NotificationEntry` objects. Actions are attached to each entry, and the entries are added to a category, which is then set in the `NotificationResponse`. If no entries are found, the response is returned without categories.
codeFunctions: private NotificationResponse mapToNotificationResponse (PortletRequest request,ResponseEntity < String > response) { Configuration config = Configuration.builder ().options (Option.DEFAULT_PATH_LEAF_TO_NULL).build ();ReadContext readContext = JsonPath.using (config).parse (response.getBody ());// check the status embedded in the response too... String success = readContext.read (SUCCESS_QUERY);// grr. SSP returns this as a string... if (!"true".equalsIgnoreCase (success)) { String error = readContext.read (MESSAGE_QUERY);return notificationError (error);} // read the actual tasks... Object rows = readContext.read (ROWS_QUERY);if (!(rows instanceof JSONArray)) { throw new RuntimeException ("Expected 'rows' to be an array of tasks");} String source = getNotificationSource (request);List < NotificationEntry > list = new ArrayList <> ();for (int i = 0;i < ((JSONArray) rows).size ();i ++) { NotificationEntry entry = mapNotificationEntry (readContext,i,source);if (entry != null) { attachActions (request,entry);list.add (entry);} } // build the notification response... NotificationResponse notification = new NotificationResponse ();if (!list.isEmpty ()) { NotificationCategory category = getNotificationCategory (request);category.addEntries (list);notification.setCategories (Arrays.asList (category));} return notification;}

String dateStr = readContext.read (format (ROW_DUE_DATE_QUERY_FMT,index));if (!StringUtils.isBlank (dateStr)) { synchronized (dateFormat) { Date dueDate = dateFormat.parse (dateStr);entry.setDueDate (dueDate);} } } catch (Exception e) { log.warn ("Error parsing due date. originalComment: Some of the links I have seen from SSP are not well formed.Try to convert any URLs to a usable form.
codeComment:
This method, `normalizeLink`, takes a string `link` as input and attempts to normalize it into a valid `URL` object. Here's a summary of the steps it follows:

1. **Check for Empty String**: If the input `link` is empty, the method returns `null`.

2. **Relative Path Handling**: If the `link` starts with a forward slash (`/`), it is assumed to be a relative path. The method then uses `sspApi.getSSPUrl(link, true)` to convert it into a full URL.

3. **Absolute URL Handling**: If the `link` starts with `http://` or `https://`, it is already a valid URL. The method constructs a new `URL` object from this string.

4. **Fallback URL Construction**: If none of the above conditions are met, the method attempts to prepend `http://` to the `link` and constructs a new `URL` object. This is a fallback mechanism to handle cases where the URL might be missing the protocol.

5. **Exception Handling**: If any `MalformedURLException` is thrown during the URL construction, the method logs a warning message with the problematic `link` and returns `null`.
codeFunctions: private URL normalizeLink (String link) { try { if (StringUtils.isEmpty (link)) { return null;} if (link.startsWith ("/")) { return sspApi.getSSPUrl (link,true);} if (link.startsWith ("http://") || link.startsWith ("https://")) { return new URL (link);} // if all else fails, just tack on http:// and see if the URL parser can handle // it.  Perhaps, not ideal... return new URL ("http://" + link);} catch (MalformedURLException e) { log.warn ("Bad URL from SSP Entry: " + link,e);return null;} }

originalComment: Compute the error as a function of the distance between the model and target.The target is sampled at regular intervals and for each of these points the closest point on the model is found.The returned metric is the average of difference between paired points.
codeComment:
This method calculates the average of the closest point error between two polygons, `model` and `target`. It does so by:

1. **Calculating the total length of the target polygon** and storing the cumulative lengths at each corner.
2. **Sampling points** along the target polygon based on the specified number of samples.
3. **Finding the closest point** on the model polygon for each sampled point on the target polygon.
4. **Calculating the error** as the distance between the sampled point on the target and its closest point on the model.
5. **Returning the average error** over all samples.
codeFunctions: public static double averageOfClosestPointError (Polygon2D_F64 model,Polygon2D_F64 target,int numberOfSamples) { LineSegment2D_F64 line = new LineSegment2D_F64 ();double cornerLocationsB [ ] = new double [ target.size () + 1 ];double totalLength = 0;for (int i = 0;i < target.size ();i ++) { Point2D_F64 b0 = target.get (i % target.size ());Point2D_F64 b1 = target.get ((i + 1) % target.size ());cornerLocationsB [ i ] = totalLength;totalLength += b0.distance (b1);} cornerLocationsB [ target.size () ] = totalLength;Point2D_F64 pointOnB = new Point2D_F64 ();double error = 0;int cornerB = 0;for (int k = 0;k < numberOfSamples;k ++) { // Find the point on B to match to a point on A double location = totalLength * k / numberOfSamples;while (location > cornerLocationsB [ cornerB + 1 ]) { cornerB ++;} Point2D_F64 b0 = target.get (cornerB);Point2D_F64 b1 = target.get ((cornerB + 1) % target.size ());double locationCornerB = cornerLocationsB [ cornerB ];double fraction = (location - locationCornerB) / (cornerLocationsB [ cornerB + 1 ] - locationCornerB);pointOnB.x = (b1.x - b0.x) * fraction + b0.x;pointOnB.y = (b1.y - b0.y) * fraction + b0.y;// find the best fit point on A to the point in B double best = Double.MAX_VALUE;for (int i = 0;i < model.size () + 1;i ++) { line.a = model.get (i % model.size ());line.b = model.get ((i + 1) % model.size ());double d = Distance2D_F64.distance (line,pointOnB);if (d < best) { best = d;} } error += best;} return error / numberOfSamples;}

originalComment: Finds the point of intersection between two lines and returns the point.
codeComment: This method calculates the intersection point of two 2D parametric lines, `a` and `b`. It first computes the parameter `t_b` using the slopes and coordinates of the lines. codeComment: This method calculates the intersection point of a parametric line (`target`) with a line segment (`l`). codeComment: This method calculates the intersection area of two rectangles, `a` and `b`, represented by `Rectangle2D_F64` objects. It first checks if the rectangles intersect using the `intersects` method. If they do not intersect, it returns 0. If they do intersect, it computes the coordinates of the intersection rectangle by finding the maximum of the left x-coordinates and the minimum of the right x-coordinates, and similarly for the top and bottom y-coordinates. Finally, it returns the area of the intersection rectangle by multiplying the width and height.
codeFunctions: public static double intersectionArea (Rectangle2D_F64 a,Rectangle2D_F64 b) { if (!intersects (a,b)) return 0;double x0 = Math.max (a.p0.x,b.p0.x);double x1 = Math.min (a.p1.x,b.p1.x);double y0 = Math.max (a.p0.y,b.p0.y);double y1 = Math.min (a.p1.y,b.p1.y);return (x1 - x0) * (y1 - y0);}

originalComment: If the index is negative it returns the negative of the value at - index.Starts at 0
codeComment: This method retrieves a value from a `DMatrixRMaj` matrix based on the provided index. If the index is negative, it returns the value at the position corresponding to the absolute value of the index from the end of the matrix. If the index is positive, it returns the value at the position corresponding to the index from the start of the matrix.
codeFunctions: private static double get (DMatrixRMaj M,int index) { if (index < 0) { return - M.data [ - index - 1 ];} else { return M.data [ index - 1 ];} }

originalComment: Extracts quaternions from the provided rotation matrix.
codeComment: This method converts a 3x3 rotation matrix (`DMatrixRMaj R`) into a quaternion (`Quaternion_F64 quat`). The algorithm aims to minimize numerical errors by avoiding division by very small numbers. It first calculates the trace of the matrix. Depending on the value of the trace and the diagonal elements of the matrix, it determines the appropriate formula to compute the quaternion components (w, x, y, z). The method returns the resulting quaternion.
codeFunctions: public static Quaternion_F64 matrixToQuaternion (DMatrixRMaj R,Quaternion_F64 quat) { if (quat == null) quat = new Quaternion_F64 ();// algorithm from: // http://www.euclideanspace.com/maths/geometry/rotations/conversions/matrixToQuaternion/ // // Designed to minimize numerical error by not dividing by very small numbers double m00 = R.unsafe_get (0,0);double m01 = R.unsafe_get (0,1);double m02 = R.unsafe_get (0,2);double m10 = R.unsafe_get (1,0);double m11 = R.unsafe_get (1,1);double m12 = R.unsafe_get (1,2);double m20 = R.unsafe_get (2,0);double m21 = R.unsafe_get (2,1);double m22 = R.unsafe_get (2,2);double trace = m00 + m11 + m22;if (trace > 0) { double S = Math.sqrt (trace + 1.0) * 2;// S=4*qw quat.w = 0.25 * S;quat.x = (m21 - m12) / S;quat.y = (m02 - m20) / S;quat.z = (m10 - m01) / S;} else if ((m00 > m11) & (m00 > m22)) { double S = Math.sqrt (1.0 + m00 - m11 - m22) * 2;// S=4*qx quat.w = (m21 - m12) / S;quat.x = 0.25 * S;quat.y = (m01 + m10) / S;quat.z = (m02 + m20) / S;} else if (m11 > m22) { double S = Math.sqrt (1.0 + m11 - m00 - m22) * 2;// S=4*qy quat.w = (m02 - m20) / S;quat.x = (m01 + m10) / S;quat.y = 0.25 * S;quat.z = (m12 + m21) / S;} else { double S = Math.sqrt (1.0 + m22 - m00 - m11) * 2;// S=4*qz quat.w = (m10 - m01) / S;quat.x = (m02 + m20) / S;quat.y = (m12 + m21) / S;quat.z = 0.25 * S;} return quat;}

originalComment: Converts an Euler coordinate into a rotation matrix.Different type of Euler coordinates are accepted.
codeComment: The method `eulerToMatrix` converts Euler angles to a rotation matrix. It takes an `EulerType` object and three rotation angles (`rotA`, `rotB`, `rotC`) as input, and outputs a `DMatrixRMaj` representing the rotation matrix. The method first checks and declares a 3x3 matrix `R`. It then creates three rotation matrices `R_a`, `R_b`, and `R_c` for rotations about the axes specified by `type`. These matrices are multiplied in sequence to form the final rotation matrix `R`, which is returned.
codeFunctions: public static DMatrixRMaj eulerToMatrix (EulerType type,double rotA,double rotB,double rotC,DMatrixRMaj R) { R = checkDeclare3x3 (R);DMatrixRMaj R_a = rotationAboutAxis (type.getAxisA (),rotA,null);DMatrixRMaj R_b = rotationAboutAxis (type.getAxisB (),rotB,null);DMatrixRMaj R_c = rotationAboutAxis (type.getAxisC (),rotC,null);DMatrixRMaj A = new DMatrixRMaj (3,3);CommonOps_DDRM.mult (R_b,R_a,A);CommonOps_DDRM.mult (R_c,A,R);return R;}

originalComment: Creates a rotation matrix about the specified axis.
codeComment:
This method, `rotationAboutAxis`, takes an integer `axis`, a double `angle`, and a `DMatrixRMaj` object `R` as parameters. It applies a rotation transformation to the matrix `R` based on the specified `axis` and `angle`. The method uses a switch statement to determine which axis to rotate around:

- If `axis` is 0, it calls `ConvertRotation3D_F64.rotX(angle, R)` to rotate around the X-axis.
- If `axis` is 1, it calls `ConvertRotation3D_F64.rotY(angle, R)` to rotate around the Y-axis.
- If `axis` is 2, it calls `ConvertRotation3D_F64.rotZ(angle, R)` to rotate around the Z-axis.

If the `axis` value is not 0, 1, or 2, the method throws an `IllegalArgumentException` with the message "Unknown which".
codeFunctions: private static DMatrixRMaj rotationAboutAxis (int axis,double angle,DMatrixRMaj R) { switch (axis) { case 0:return ConvertRotation3D_F64.rotX (angle,R);case 1:return ConvertRotation3D_F64.rotY (angle,R);case 2:return ConvertRotation3D_F64.rotZ (angle,R);default:throw new IllegalArgumentException ("Unknown which");} }

originalComment: Converts a rigid body motion into a twist coordinate.The value of theta used to generate the motion is assumed to be one.
codeComment: This method computes the twist coordinates from a given 3D rigid body motion represented by a `Se3_F64` object. The twist coordinates are stored in a `TwistCoordinate_F64` object. The method first checks if the rotation part of the motion is the identity matrix. If it is, the twist's angular velocity (`w`) is set to zero, and the linear velocity (`v`) is set to the translation part of the motion. If the rotation is not the identity, the method converts the rotation matrix to a Rodrigues vector, calculates the angle of rotation (`theta`), and then computes the twist's angular velocity and linear velocity using matrix operations. The final twist coordinates are returned.
codeFunctions: public static TwistCoordinate_F64 twist (Se3_F64 motion,TwistCoordinate_F64 twist) { if (twist == null) twist = new TwistCoordinate_F64 ();if (MatrixFeatures_DDRM.isIdentity (motion.R,GrlConstants.TEST_F64)) { twist.w.set (0,0,0);twist.v.set (motion.T);} else { Rodrigues_F64 rod = new Rodrigues_F64 ();ConvertRotation3D_F64.matrixToRodrigues (motion.R,rod);twist.w.set (rod.unitAxisRotation);double theta = rod.theta;// A = (I-SO)*hat(w) + w*w'*theta DMatrixRMaj A = CommonOps_DDRM.identity (3);CommonOps_DDRM.subtract (A,motion.R,A);DMatrixRMaj w_hat = GeometryMath_F64.crossMatrix (twist.w,null);DMatrixRMaj tmp = A.copy ();CommonOps_DDRM.mult (tmp,w_hat,A);Vector3D_F64 w = twist.w;A.data [ 0 ] += w.x * w.x * theta;A.data [ 1 ] += w.x * w.y * theta;A.data [ 2 ] += w.x * w.z * theta;A.data [ 3 ] += w.y * w.x * theta;A.data [ 4 ] += w.y * w.y * theta;A.data [ 5 ] += w.y * w.z * theta;A.data [ 6 ] += w.z * w.x * theta;A.data [ 7 ] += w.z * w.y * theta;A.data [ 8 ] += w.z * w.z * theta;DMatrixRMaj y = new DMatrixRMaj (3,1);y.data [ 0 ] = motion.T.x;y.data [ 1 ] = motion.T.y;y.data [ 2 ] = motion.T.z;DMatrixRMaj x = new DMatrixRMaj (3,1);CommonOps_DDRM.solve (A,y,x);twist.w.scale (rod.theta);twist.v.x = (double) x.data [ 0 ];twist.v.y = (double) x.data [ 1 ];twist.v.z = (double) x.data [ 2 ];twist.v.scale (rod.theta);} return twist;}

originalComment: Specify the two transforms which values are to be interpolated between
codeComment: This method sets the transformation parameters between two poses represented by `Se3_F64` objects, `initial` and `end`. It calculates the translation vector by subtracting the corresponding components of the translation vectors of `initial` and `end`. It then computes the rotation matrix `R` by multiplying the transpose of the rotation matrix of `initial` with the rotation matrix of `end`. The rotation matrix `R` is converted to a Rodrigues vector, and the magnitude of the rotation is stored in `rotMagnitude`.
codeFunctions: public void setTransforms (Se3_F64 initial,Se3_F64 end) { this.initial.set (initial);translation.x = end.T.x - initial.T.x;translation.y = end.T.y - initial.T.y;translation.z = end.T.z - initial.T.z;CommonOps_DDRM.multTransA (initial.getR (),end.getR (),R);ConvertRotation3D_F64.matrixToRodrigues (R,rotation);rotMagnitude = rotation.theta;}

originalComment: Interpolates a value between the first and second transform.A value close to 0 will be more similar to the initial and 1 more similar to the end.
codeComment: This method, `interpolate`, performs linear interpolation between two poses represented by `Se3_F64` objects. It takes a parameter `where` which determines the interpolation factor, and an `output` object to store the interpolated pose. The method updates the rotation and translation components of the `output` pose based on the interpolation factor. Specifically, it scales the rotation angle by `where` and applies the Rodrigues formula to convert the rotation vector to a rotation matrix. The translation components are linearly interpolated by scaling the initial translation vector by `where` and adding it to the initial translation. Finally, it multiplies the initial rotation matrix by the interpolated rotation matrix to update the rotation of the `output` pose.
codeFunctions: public void interpolate (double where,Se3_F64 output) { rotation.setTheta (where * rotMagnitude);ConvertRotation3D_F64.rodriguesToMatrix (rotation,R);output.T.x = initial.T.x + where * translation.x;output.T.y = initial.T.y + where * translation.y;output.T.z = initial.T.z + where * translation.z;CommonOps_DDRM.mult (initial.R,R,output.R);}

originalComment: SVD based method for fitting a plane to a set of points.The plane s equation is returned as a point on the plane and the normal vector.
codeComment: The method `svd` calculates the centroid of a list of 3D points and then solves for the normal vector using another method `solvePoint`. It first computes the average of the x, y, and z coordinates of the points to find the centroid, which is stored in `outputCenter`. After finding the centroid, it calls `solvePoint` to determine the normal vector, which is stored in `outputNormal`. The method returns a boolean value indicating the success of the operation.
codeFunctions: public boolean svd (List < Point3D_F64 > points,Point3D_F64 outputCenter,Vector3D_F64 outputNormal) { final int N = points.size ();// find the centroid outputCenter.set (0,0,0);for (int i = 0;i < N;i ++) { Point3D_F64 p = points.get (i);outputCenter.x += p.x;outputCenter.y += p.y;outputCenter.z += p.z;} outputCenter.x /= N;outputCenter.y /= N;outputCenter.z /= N;return solvePoint (points,outputCenter,outputNormal);}

originalComment: SVD based method for fitting a plane to a set of points and a known point on the plane.The plane s equation is returned as a point on the plane and the normal vector.
codeComment: The method `solvePoint` calculates the normal vector of a plane defined by a list of 3D points and a point on the plane. It constructs a matrix `A` where each row represents the difference between a point in the list and the given point on the plane. The method then decomposes this matrix using a singular value decomposition (SVD) to find the null space, from which the normal vector is extracted and stored in `outputNormal`. If the decomposition fails, the method returns `false`; otherwise, it returns `true`.
codeFunctions: public boolean solvePoint (List < Point3D_F64 > points,Point3D_F64 pointOnPlane,Vector3D_F64 outputNormal) { final int N = points.size ();// construct the matrix A.reshape (N,3);int index = 0;for (int i = 0;i < N;i ++) { Point3D_F64 p = points.get (i);A.data [ index ++ ] = p.x - pointOnPlane.x;A.data [ index ++ ] = p.y - pointOnPlane.y;A.data [ index ++ ] = p.z - pointOnPlane.z;} // decompose and find the singular value if (!solverNull.process (A,1,nullspace)) return false;// the normal is the singular vector outputNormal.x = (double) nullspace.unsafe_get (0,0);outputNormal.y = (double) nullspace.unsafe_get (1,0);outputNormal.z = (double) nullspace.unsafe_get (2,0);return true;}

originalComment: Resturns the length of the specified side that is composed of point index and index + 1
codeComment: This method calculates the length of a side of a polygon. It takes an integer `index` as input, which represents the index of a vertex in the polygon. The method retrieves the vertex at the given index and the next vertex (wrapping around to the first vertex if necessary) from a list of vertices (`vertexes`). It then calculates and returns the Euclidean distance between these two vertices.
codeFunctions: public double getSideLength (int index) { Point2D_F64 a = vertexes.get (index);Point2D_F64 b = vertexes.get ((index + 1) % vertexes.size);return (double) a.distance (b);}

originalComment: Returns true if the point is inside the polygon.Points along the border are ambiguously considered inside or outside.
codeComment: The method `isInside` checks if a given point `p` is inside a polygon. It first determines if the polygon is convex using the `isConvex` method. If the polygon is convex, it uses the `containConvex` method from the `Intersection2D_F64` class to check if the point is inside. If the polygon is concave, it uses the `containConcave` method instead. The method returns `true` if the point is inside the polygon and `false` otherwise.
codeFunctions: public boolean isInside (Point2D_F64 p) { if (isConvex ()) { return Intersection2D_F64.containConvex (this,p);} else { return Intersection2D_F64.containConcave (this,p);} }

originalComment: Converts symmetric 3x3 matrix back into a conic.
codeComment: This method converts a `ConicGeneral_F64` object to a `DMatrixRMaj` matrix. If the destination matrix `dst` is null, it creates a new 3x3 matrix; otherwise, it reshapes the existing matrix to 3x3. The method then calculates intermediate values `B`, `D`, and `E` by dividing the corresponding elements of the source conic by 2. Finally, it fills the destination matrix with the calculated values and returns it.
codeFunctions: public static DMatrixRMaj convert (ConicGeneral_F64 src,DMatrixRMaj dst) { if (dst == null) dst = new DMatrixRMaj (3,3);else dst.reshape (3,3);double B = src.B / 2.0;double D = src.D / 2.0;double E = src.E / 2.0;dst.data [ 0 ] = src.A;dst.data [ 1 ] = B;dst.data [ 2 ] = D;dst.data [ 3 ] = B;dst.data [ 4 ] = src.C;dst.data [ 5 ] = E;dst.data [ 6 ] = D;dst.data [ 7 ] = E;dst.data [ 8 ] = src.F;return dst;}

originalComment: Converts the conic into a symmetric 3x3 matrix
codeComment: This method converts a `ConicGeneral_F64` object to a `DMatrix3x3` object. It initializes the destination matrix if it is null, then assigns the appropriate values from the source conic to the destination matrix, taking into account the division by 2 for certain coefficients.
codeFunctions: public static DMatrix3x3 convert (ConicGeneral_F64 src,DMatrix3x3 dst) { if (dst == null) dst = new DMatrix3x3 ();double B = src.B / 2.0;double D = src.D / 2.0;double E = src.E / 2.0;dst.a11 = src.A;dst.a12 = B;dst.a13 = D;dst.a21 = B;dst.a22 = src.C;dst.a23 = E;dst.a31 = D;dst.a32 = E;dst.a33 = src.F;return dst;}

originalComment: Converts the conic into a parabola.If the conic isn t a parabola then it is converted into one by adjusting the value of B.
codeComment: This method converts a `ConicGeneral_F64` object to a `ParabolaGeneral_F64` object. It initializes the destination `ParabolaGeneral_F64` object if it is null. The method then sets the `A` and `C` properties of the destination object by taking the signum and square root of the absolute values of the corresponding properties in the source object. The `D`, `E`, and `F` properties are directly copied from the source to the destination object. Finally, the method returns the destination `ParabolaGeneral_F64` object.
codeFunctions: public static ParabolaGeneral_F64 convert (ConicGeneral_F64 src,ParabolaGeneral_F64 dst) { if (dst == null) dst = new ParabolaGeneral_F64 ();// NOTE haven't put much through if this is the correct way to handle negative values of A or C dst.A = Math.signum (src.A) * Math.sqrt (Math.abs (src.A));dst.C = Math.signum (src.C) * Math.sqrt (Math.abs (src.C));dst.D = src.D;dst.E = src.E;dst.F = src.F;return dst;}

originalComment: Converts the parabola into a conic.
codeComment: Converts a `ParabolaGeneral_F64` object to a `ConicGeneral_F64` object by setting the appropriate coefficients.
codeFunctions: public static ConicGeneral_F64 convert (ParabolaGeneral_F64 src,ConicGeneral_F64 dst) { if (dst == null) dst = new ConicGeneral_F64 ();dst.A = src.A * src.A;dst.B = src.A * src.C * 2.0;dst.C = src.C * src.C;dst.D = src.D;dst.E = src.E;dst.F = src.F;return dst;}

originalComment: Converts a GeoTuple3D_F64 into DMatrixRMaj

codeFunctions: public static DMatrixRMaj toMatrix (GeoTuple3D_F64 in,DMatrixRMaj out) { if (out == null) out = new DMatrixRMaj (3,1);else if (out.getNumElements () != 3) throw new IllegalArgumentException ("Vector with 3 elements expected");out.data [ 0 ] = in.x;out.data [ 1 ] = in.y;out.data [ 2 ] = in.z;return out;}

codeComment: The method `toTuple3D` converts a 3D matrix (`DMatrixRMaj`) into a 3D geometric tuple (`GeoTuple3D_F64`). It extracts the first three elements from the matrix and assigns them to the `x`, `y`, and `z` components of the tuple, respectively.

originalComment: Assign the Rodrigues coordinates using a 3 element vector.Theta is the vector s magnitude and the axis of rotation is the unit vector.
codeComment: This method, `setParamVector`, takes three double parameters `x`, `y`, and `z`, representing a vector. It calculates the absolute values of these components and determines the maximum absolute value. If the maximum is zero, it sets the rotation angle `theta` to 0 and the unit axis of rotation to (1, 0, 0). Otherwise, it normalizes the vector by dividing each component by the maximum absolute value, calculates the magnitude `theta` of the normalized vector, and then sets the unit axis of rotation to the normalized vector components. Finally, it multiplies `theta` by the maximum absolute value to get the final rotation angle.
codeFunctions: public void setParamVector (double x,double y,double z) { double ax = Math.abs (x);double ay = Math.abs (y);double az = Math.abs (z);double max = Math.max (ax,ay);max = Math.max (max,az);if (max == 0) { theta = 0;unitAxisRotation.set (1,0,0);} else { x /= max;y /= max;z /= max;theta = Math.sqrt (x * x + y * y + z * z);unitAxisRotation.x = x / theta;unitAxisRotation.y = y / theta;unitAxisRotation.z = z / theta;theta *= max;} }

originalComment: Angular distance between two half circle angles.
codeComment: This method calculates the shortest angular distance between two angles, `angA` and `angB`, in radians. It first computes the absolute difference between the two angles. If this difference is less than or equal to π/2, it returns the difference directly. Otherwise, it returns π minus the difference, ensuring the result is the smallest possible angle between the two.
codeFunctions: public static double distHalf (double angA,double angB) { double a = Math.abs (angA - angB);if (a <= Math.PI / 2) return a;else return Math.PI - a;}

originalComment: Finds the line which is the intersection between the two planes.For a valid solution to be returned the planes must not be parallel to each other.If the planes are parallel then the slope of the returned line will have a value of zero for each element.
codeComment: The method `intersect` determines if two planes (`a` and `b`) intersect and, if they do, calculates the line of intersection. It first computes the slope of the line of intersection as the cross product of the normal vectors of the two planes. If the slope is zero, the planes are parallel and do not intersect. Otherwise, it finds the closest point on plane `a` to the origin and uses this point to determine the direction towards the intersection. It then calculates the intersection point by solving for the parameter `d` and updating the line's parameters accordingly. If successful, it returns `true`; otherwise, it returns `false`.
codeFunctions: public static boolean intersect (PlaneGeneral3D_F64 a,PlaneGeneral3D_F64 b,LineParametric3D_F64 line) { // Line's slope is the cross product of the two normal vectors GeometryMath_F64.cross (a.A,a.B,a.C,b.A,b.B,b.C,line.slope);if (line.slope.normSq () == 0) return false;// Closest point on plane 'a' to origin (0,0,0) double n2 = a.A * a.A + a.B * a.B + a.C * a.C;double closestX = a.A * a.D / n2;double closestY = a.B * a.D / n2;double closestZ = a.C * a.D / n2;// Cross product between normal of 'a' and the line's slope.  This points towards the intersection double slopeX = a.B * line.slope.z - a.C * line.slope.y;double slopeY = a.C * line.slope.x - a.A * line.slope.z;double slopeZ = a.A * line.slope.y - a.B * line.slope.x;// Now find the intersection of the plane and a line containing point 'closest' and pointing towards the // the intersection. double top = b.D - b.A * closestX - b.B * closestY - b.C * closestZ;double bottom = b.A * slopeX + b.B * slopeY + b.C * slopeZ;double d = top / bottom;line.p.x = closestX + d * slopeX;line.p.y = closestY + d * slopeY;line.p.z = closestZ + d * slopeZ;return true;}

originalComment: Determines if the point on the same plane as T is contained inside of T.
codeComment: The method `containedPlane` checks if a point `output` lies within a triangle defined by three points `T_v0`, `u`, and `v` in 3D space. It uses vector operations to determine if the point is inside the triangle by calculating parametric coordinates `s` and `t` and checking if they satisfy the conditions for the point to be within the triangle. If the point is outside the triangle, it returns `false`; otherwise, it returns `true`.
codeFunctions: private static boolean containedPlane (Point3D_F64 T_v0,Point3D_F64 output,Vector3D_F64 u,Vector3D_F64 v,Vector3D_F64 w0) { double uu,uv,vv,wu,wv,D;uu = u.dot (u);uv = u.dot (v);vv = v.dot (v);w0.minus (output,T_v0);wu = w0.dot (u);wv = w0.dot (v);D = uv * uv - uu * vv;// get and test parametric coords double s,t;s = (uv * wv - vv * wu) / D;if (s < 0.0 || s > 1.0) // I is outside T return false;t = (uv * wu - uu * wv) / D;return!(t < 0.0) &&!((s + t) > 1.0);// I is outside T }

originalComment: Finds the intersection of a line and sphere.There can be 0 1 or 2 intersections.If there is 1 intersection the same point is returned twice.
codeComment: This method determines if a 3D line intersects a sphere and calculates the intersection points. It uses the parametric equation of the line and the equation of the sphere to solve for the intersection points. The method returns `true` if there are intersection points and `false` otherwise. The intersection points are stored in the `a` and `b` parameters.
codeFunctions: public static boolean intersect (LineParametric3D_F64 line,Sphere3D_F64 sphere,Point3D_F64 a,Point3D_F64 b) { // this equation was found by solving for l: // ||(P + V*l) - X0|| == r double r2 = sphere.radius * sphere.radius;double PP = GeometryMath_F64.dot (line.p,line.p);double PV = GeometryMath_F64.dot (line.p,line.slope);double PX = GeometryMath_F64.dot (line.p,sphere.center);double VV = GeometryMath_F64.dot (line.slope,line.slope);double VX = GeometryMath_F64.dot (line.slope,sphere.center);double XX = GeometryMath_F64.dot (sphere.center,sphere.center);// Coefficients in the quadratic equation double A = VV;double B = 2.0 * (PV - VX);double C = PP + XX - 2.0 * PX - r2;// solve for the quadratic equation double inner = B * B - 4.0 * A * C;if (inner < 0) return false;double sqrt = Math.sqrt (inner);double t0 = (- B + sqrt) / (2.0 * A);double t1 = (- B - sqrt) / (2.0 * A);line.setPointOnLine (t0,a);line.setPointOnLine (t1,b);return true;}

originalComment: Perform linear interpolation
codeComment: This method, `interpolate`, performs linear interpolation between two 2D rigid body transformations represented by `Se2_F64` objects `a` and `b`. The interpolation is based on a parameter `where`, which ranges from 0 to 1. The method calculates the interpolated translation by linearly combining the x and y components of the translations of `a` and `b`. For the rotation, it calculates the clockwise and counterclockwise distances between the yaw angles of `a` and `b`. It then selects the shorter distance to interpolate the yaw angle, ensuring that the rotation interpolation is accurate even when the angles differ by more than 180 degrees. The interpolated transformation is stored in the `output` object.
codeFunctions: public static void interpolate (Se2_F64 a,Se2_F64 b,double where,Se2_F64 output) { double w0 = 1.0 - where;output.T.x = a.T.x * w0 + b.T.x * where;output.T.y = a.T.y * w0 + b.T.y * where;// interpolating rotation is more difficult // This only works well if the difference between the two angles is small double yaw0 = a.getYaw ();double yaw1 = b.getYaw ();double cw = UtilAngle.distanceCW (yaw0,yaw1);double ccw = UtilAngle.distanceCCW (yaw0,yaw1);double yaw;if (cw > ccw) { yaw = yaw0 + ccw * where;} else { yaw = yaw0 - cw * where;} output.setYaw (yaw);}

originalComment: The unit eigenvector corresponding to the maximum eigenvalue of Q is the rotation parameterized as a quaternion.
codeComment: This method extracts a quaternion from a given matrix `q` and normalizes it. It then converts the quaternion to a rotation matrix and assigns it to `motion.getR()`.
codeFunctions: private void extractQuaternionFromQ (SimpleMatrix q) { SimpleEVD < SimpleMatrix > evd = q.eig ();int indexMax = evd.getIndexMax ();SimpleMatrix v_max = evd.getEigenVector (indexMax);quat.w = (double) v_max.get (0);quat.x = (double) v_max.get (1);quat.y = (double) v_max.get (2);quat.z = (double) v_max.get (3);quat.normalize ();ConvertRotation3D_F64.quaternionToMatrix (quat,motion.getR ());}

originalComment: Computes the convex hull.The output will be in counter - clockwise order.
codeComment: This method processes an array of `Point2D_F64` objects to compute the convex hull using the Graham scan algorithm. It handles special cases where the input length is 2, sorts the input points, and constructs both the lower and upper hulls. The method ensures that the resulting hull is counter-clockwise and contains the minimum number of points necessary to form the convex hull. The final hull is stored in a `Polygon2D_F64` object.
codeFunctions: public void process (Point2D_F64 [ ] input,int length,Polygon2D_F64 hull) { // ahdnle special cases if (length == 2) { hull.vertexes.resize (length);for (int i = 0;i < length;i ++) { hull.get (i).set (input [ i ]);} return;} sorter.sort (input,length);work.reset ();// construct the lower hull for (int i = 0;i < length;i ++) { Point2D_F64 p = input [ i ];//Contains at least 2 points and the last two points and 'p' do not make a counter-clockwise turn while (work.size () >= 2 && subtractThenCross (p,work.getTail (0),work.getTail (1)) >= 0) { // remove the last points from the hull work.removeTail ();} // append p to the end work.add (p);} work.removeTail ();int minSize = work.size + 2;// construct upper hull for (int i = length - 1;i >= 0;i --) // Finding top layer from hull { //Contains at least 2 points and the last two points and 'p' do not make a counter-clockwise turn Point2D_F64 p = input [ i ];while (work.size () >= minSize && subtractThenCross (p,work.getTail (0),work.getTail (1)) >= 0) { work.removeTail ();} // append p to the end work.add (p);} work.removeTail ();// create a copy for the output // the work buffer contains references to the input points, but to be safe the output should have its // own instances hull.vertexes.resize (work.size);for (int i = 0;i < work.size ();i ++) { hull.vertexes.data [ i ].set (work.get (i));} }

originalComment: Converts it into a 4 by 4 homogeneous matrix.
codeComment: This method converts a `Se3_F64` object, which represents a 3D rigid body transformation, into a homogeneous transformation matrix of type `DMatrixRMaj`. The method takes two parameters: `se`, the `Se3_F64` object, and `ret`, the `DMatrixRMaj` matrix to store the result. If `ret` is `null`, a new `DMatrixRMaj` matrix of size 4x4 is created. The rotation part of the transformation is inserted into the upper-left 3x3 submatrix of `ret` using `CommonOps_DDRM.insert`. The translation part, obtained from `se.getT()`, is set in the last column of the first three rows. Finally, the last element of the matrix is set to 1 to complete the homogeneous transformation matrix, which is then returned.
codeFunctions: public static DMatrixRMaj toHomogeneous (Se3_F64 se,DMatrixRMaj ret) { if (ret == null) ret = new DMatrixRMaj (4,4);else { ret.set (3,0,0);ret.set (3,1,0);ret.set (3,2,0);} CommonOps_DDRM.insert (se.getR (),ret,0,0);Vector3D_F64 T = se.getT ();ret.set (0,3,T.x);ret.set (1,3,T.y);ret.set (2,3,T.z);ret.set (3,3,1);return ret;}

codeComment: This method converts a 2D rigid body transformation (`Se2_F64`) into a homogeneous transformation matrix (`DMatrixRMaj`).
