if (startString == null || p.length () > startString.length ()) { startString = p;prefix = e.getEntryArg (1);} } } if (prefix != null) { // return the systemId with the new prefix return prefix + uri.substring (startString.length ());} } // If there's a DELEGATE_URI entry in this catalog, use it enumt = catalogEntries.elements ();Vector delCats = new Vector ();while (enumt.hasMoreElements ()) { CatalogEntry e = (CatalogEntry) enumt.nextElement ();if (e.getEntryType () == DELEGATE_URI) { String p = e.getEntryArg (0);if (p.length () <= uri.length () && p.equals (uri.substring (0,p.length ()))) { // delegate this match to the other catalog delCats.addElement (e.getEntryArg (1));} } } if (delCats.size () > 0) { Enumeration enumCats = delCats.elements ();if (catalogManager.debug.getDebug () > 1) { catalogManager.debug.message (2,"Switching to delegated catalog(s):");while (enumCats.hasMoreElements ()) { String delegatedCatalog = (String) enumCats.nextElement ();catalogManager.debug.message (2,"\t" + delegatedCatalog);} } Catalog dcat = newCatalog ();enumCats = delCats.elements ();while (enumCats.hasMoreElements ()) { String delegatedCatalog = (String) enumCats.nextElement ();dcat.parseCatalog (delegatedCatalog);} return dcat.resolveURI (uri);} return null;}

codeComment: The method `resolveSubordinateCatalogs` is designed to resolve entity references using a list of catalogs. codeComment: The `normalizeURI` method takes a URI reference as input and returns a normalized version of it. The method first checks if the input is null and returns null if so. If refreshing fails, it destroys the entry and removes it from the map, then returns null. If the entry is current or successfully refreshed, it returns the value associated with the key.
codeFunctions: public Object get (Object key) { TimedEntry entry = (TimedEntry) entryMap.get (key);if (entry == null) return null;if (entry.isCurrent (now) == false) { // Try to refresh the entry if (entry.refresh () == false) { // Failed, remove the entry and return null entry.destroy ();entryMap.remove (key);return null;} } Object value = entry.getValue ();return value;}

originalComment: Remove all entries from the cache.
codeComment: The `flush` method clears the contents of `entryMap` by creating a temporary map, transferring the entries to it, and then notifying each entry to perform cleanup. If `threadSafe` is true, it replaces `entryMap` with a new synchronized map; otherwise, it replaces it with a new non-synchronized map.
codeFunctions: public void flush () { Map tmpMap = null;synchronized (this) { tmpMap = entryMap;if (threadSafe) entryMap = Collections.synchronizedMap (new HashMap ());else entryMap = new HashMap ();} // Notify the entries of their removal Iterator iter = tmpMap.values ().iterator ();while (iter.hasNext ()) { TimedEntry entry = (TimedEntry) iter.next ();entry.destroy ();} tmpMap.clear ();}

The method ensures thread safety by synchronizing on `entryMap` during the iteration.

originalComment: Returns an iterator over the children of the given element with the given tag name.
codeComment: This method, `getChildrenByTagName`, takes an `Element` and a `String` representing a tag name as input. It returns an `Iterator` containing all child elements of the given `Element` that match the specified tag name. The method first checks if the input `Element` is null and returns null if it is. It then retrieves all child nodes of the `Element` and iterates through them, adding only those that are elements and have the specified tag name to an `ArrayList`. Finally, it returns an iterator for the `ArrayList` of matching child elements.
codeFunctions: public static Iterator getChildrenByTagName (Element element,String tagName) { if (element == null) return null;// getElementsByTagName gives the corresponding elements in the whole  // descendance. We want only children NodeList children = element.getChildNodes ();ArrayList goodChildren = new ArrayList ();for (int i = 0;i < children.getLength ();i ++) { Node currentChild = children.item (i);if (currentChild.getNodeType () == Node.ELEMENT_NODE && ((Element) currentChild).getTagName ().equals (tagName)) { goodChildren.add (currentChild);} } return goodChildren.iterator ();}

codeFunctions: public static Element getUniqueChild (Element element,String tagName) throws Exception { Iterator goodChildren = getChildrenByTagName (element,tagName);if (goodChildren != null && goodChildren.hasNext ()) { Element child = (Element) goodChildren.next ();if (goodChildren.hasNext ()) { throw new Exception ("expected only one " + tagName + " tag");} return child;} else { throw new Exception ("expected one " + tagName + " tag");} }

codeFunctions: public static String getElementContent (Element element,String defaultStr) throws Exception { if (element == null) return defaultStr;NodeList children = element.getChildNodes ();String result = "";for (int i = 0;i < children.getLength ();i ++) { if (children.item (i).getNodeType () == Node.TEXT_NODE || children.item (i).getNodeType () == Node.CDATA_SECTION_NODE) { result += children.item (i).getNodeValue ();} else if (children.item (i).getNodeType () == Node.COMMENT_NODE) { // Ignore comment nodes } } return result.trim ();}

originalComment: This resets the work queue capacity.This requires recreating the work queue and ThreadPoolExecutor so this needs to be called before doing any work with the pool.

originalComment: Return the applicable SYSTEM system identifier resorting to external RESOLVERs if necessary.
codeComment: The `resolveSystem` method attempts to resolve a given `systemId` by first calling the superclass's `resolveSystem` method. If the superclass method returns a non-null result, it is returned immediately. If not, the method iterates through a list of catalog entries. For each entry, if it is of type `RESOLVER`, it attempts to resolve the `systemId` using the entry's argument. If successful, the resolved result is returned. If the entry is of type `SYSTEMSUFFIX`, it checks if the `systemId` ends with the specified suffix. If it does, it returns the corresponding result. If no resolution is found through these methods, the method attempts to resolve the `systemId` using subordinate catalogs.
codeFunctions: public String resolveSystem (String systemId) throws MalformedURLException,IOException { String resolved = super.resolveSystem (systemId);if (resolved != null) { return resolved;} Enumeration enumt = catalogEntries.elements ();while (enumt.hasMoreElements ()) { CatalogEntry e = (CatalogEntry) enumt.nextElement ();if (e.getEntryType () == RESOLVER) { resolved = resolveExternalSystem (systemId,e.getEntryArg (0));if (resolved != null) { return resolved;} } else if (e.getEntryType () == SYSTEMSUFFIX) { String suffix = e.getEntryArg (0);String result = e.getEntryArg (1);if (suffix.length () <= systemId.length () && systemId.substring (systemId.length () - suffix.length ()).equals (suffix)) { return result;} } } return resolveSubordinateCatalogs (Catalog.SYSTEM,null,null,systemId);}

codeFunctions: public String resolvePublic (String publicId,String systemId) throws MalformedURLException,IOException { String resolved = super.resolvePublic (publicId,systemId);if (resolved != null) { return resolved;} Enumeration enumt = catalogEntries.elements ();while (enumt.hasMoreElements ()) { CatalogEntry e = (CatalogEntry) enumt.nextElement ();if (e.getEntryType () == RESOLVER) { if (systemId != null) { resolved = resolveExternalSystem (systemId,e.getEntryArg (0));if (resolved != null) { return resolved;} } resolved = resolveExternalPublic (publicId,e.getEntryArg (0));if (resolved != null) { return resolved;} } } return resolveSubordinateCatalogs (Catalog.PUBLIC,null,publicId,systemId);}

originalComment: Query an external RFC2483 resolver.
codeComment: The `queryResolver` method constructs a URL using the provided resolver, command, and arguments, then attempts to open a connection to that URL. It sets the connection to not use caches and initializes a `Resolver` object. The method retrieves the content type of the response and, if necessary, strips any character set or subtype information. It then parses the catalog using the content type and the input stream from the URL connection. If any exceptions occur during this process, such as a catalog being unparseable, an unknown format, a malformed URL, or an I/O exception, the method logs an appropriate error message and returns `null`.
codeFunctions: protected Resolver queryResolver (String resolver,String command,String arg1,String arg2) { String RFC2483 = resolver + "?command=" + command + "&format=tr9401&uri=" + arg1 + "&uri2=" + arg2;try { URL url = new URL (RFC2483);URLConnection urlCon = url.openConnection ();urlCon.setUseCaches (false);Resolver r = (Resolver) newCatalog ();String cType = urlCon.getContentType ();// I don't care about the character set or subtype if (cType.indexOf (";") > 0) { cType = cType.substring (0,cType.indexOf (";"));} r.parseCatalog (cType,urlCon.getInputStream ());return r;} catch (CatalogException cex) { if (cex.getExceptionType () == CatalogException.UNPARSEABLE) { catalogManager.debug.message (1,"Unparseable catalog: " + RFC2483);} else if (cex.getExceptionType () == CatalogException.UNKNOWN_FORMAT) { catalogManager.debug.message (1,"Unknown catalog format: " + RFC2483);} return null;} catch (MalformedURLException mue) { catalogManager.debug.message (1,"Malformed resolver URL: " + RFC2483);return null;} catch (IOException ie) { catalogManager.debug.message (1,"I/O Exception opening resolver: " + RFC2483);return null;} }

originalComment: Find the URNs for a given system identifier in all catalogs.

If found, it appends the resolved entries to a `Vector`. If no local entry is found, it then searches through subordinate catalogs for the `systemId`. The resolved entries from both local and subordinate catalogs are combined and returned as a `Vector`. The method throws `MalformedURLException` and `IOException` if any issues occur during the resolution process.
codeFunctions: public Vector resolveAllSystemReverse (String systemId) throws MalformedURLException,IOException { Vector resolved = new Vector ();// If there's a SYSTEM entry in this catalog, use it if (systemId != null) { Vector localResolved = resolveLocalSystemReverse (systemId);resolved = appendVector (resolved,localResolved);} // Otherwise, look in the subordinate catalogs Vector subResolved = resolveAllSubordinateCatalogs (SYSTEMREVERSE,null,null,systemId);return appendVector (resolved,subResolved);}

It starts by checking if the `systemId` is not null. If it is not null, it resolves the `systemId` locally using the `resolveAllLocalSystem` method and appends the results to a `Vector` called `resolutions`. Next, it resolves the `systemId` in subordinate catalogs using the `resolveAllSubordinateCatalogs` method and appends these results to the same `Vector`. If the `resolutions` vector is not empty, it returns the vector; otherwise, it returns null.
codeFunctions: public Vector resolveAllSystem (String systemId) throws MalformedURLException,IOException { Vector resolutions = new Vector ();// If there are SYSTEM entries in this catalog, start with them if (systemId != null) { Vector localResolutions = resolveAllLocalSystem (systemId);resolutions = appendVector (resolutions,localResolutions);} // Then look in the subordinate catalogs Vector subResolutions = resolveAllSubordinateCatalogs (SYSTEM,null,null,systemId);resolutions = appendVector (resolutions,subResolutions);if (resolutions.size () > 0) { return resolutions;} else { return null;} }

originalComment: Return all applicable SYSTEM system identifiers in this catalog.
codeComment: The method `resolveAllLocalSystem` takes a `systemId` as input and returns a `Vector` containing all matching system entries from the catalog. It first checks the operating system name to determine if it is Windows. It then iterates through the catalog entries, checking if each entry is of type `SYSTEM` and if its first argument matches the input `systemId` (case-insensitive on Windows). Matching entries' second arguments are added to the `map` vector. If no matches are found, the method returns `null`; otherwise, it returns the `map` vector.
codeFunctions: private Vector resolveAllLocalSystem (String systemId) { Vector map = new Vector ();String osname = System.getProperty ("os.name");boolean windows = (osname.indexOf ("Windows") >= 0);Enumeration enumt = catalogEntries.elements ();while (enumt.hasMoreElements ()) { CatalogEntry e = (CatalogEntry) enumt.nextElement ();if (e.getEntryType () == SYSTEM && (e.getEntryArg (0).equals (systemId) || (windows && e.getEntryArg (0).equalsIgnoreCase (systemId)))) { map.addElement (e.getEntryArg (1));} } if (map.size () == 0) { return null;} else { return map;} }

originalComment: Search the subordinate catalogs in order looking for all match.
codeComment: The method `resolveAllSubordinateCatalogs` is designed to resolve entity references using a list of catalogs. It takes parameters for the entity type, entity name, public ID, and system ID. The method iterates through a list of catalogs, attempting to resolve the entity based on its type. If a resolution is found, it is added to a vector of resolutions, which is then returned. The method handles different entity types such as DOCTYPE, DOCUMENT, ENTITY, NOTATION, PUBLIC, SYSTEM, and SYSTEMREVERSE, using corresponding resolution methods from the `Resolver` class. If no resolution is found, the method returns null.
codeFunctions: private synchronized Vector resolveAllSubordinateCatalogs (int entityType,String entityName,String publicId,String systemId) throws MalformedURLException,IOException { Vector resolutions = new Vector ();for (int catPos = 0;catPos < catalogs.size ();catPos ++) { Resolver c = null;try { c = (Resolver) catalogs.elementAt (catPos);} catch (ClassCastException e) { String catfile = (String) catalogs.elementAt (catPos);c = (Resolver) newCatalog ();try { c.parseCatalog (catfile);} catch (MalformedURLException mue) { catalogManager.debug.message (1,"Malformed Catalog URL",catfile);} catch (FileNotFoundException fnfe) { catalogManager.debug.message (1,"Failed to load catalog, file not found",catfile);} catch (IOException ioe) { catalogManager.debug.message (1,"Failed to load catalog, I/O error",catfile);} catalogs.setElementAt (c,catPos);} String resolved = null;// Ok, now what are we supposed to call here? if (entityType == DOCTYPE) { resolved = c.resolveDoctype (entityName,publicId,systemId);if (resolved != null) { // Only find one DOCTYPE resolution resolutions.addElement (resolved);return resolutions;} } else if (entityType == DOCUMENT) { resolved = c.resolveDocument ();if (resolved != null) { // Only find one DOCUMENT resolution resolutions.addElement (resolved);return resolutions;} } else if (entityType == ENTITY) { resolved = c.resolveEntity (entityName,publicId,systemId);if (resolved != null) { // Only find one ENTITY resolution resolutions.addElement (resolved);return resolutions;} } else if (entityType == NOTATION) { resolved = c.resolveNotation (entityName,publicId,systemId);if (resolved != null) { // Only find one NOTATION resolution resolutions.addElement (resolved);return resolutions;} } else if (entityType == PUBLIC) { resolved = c.resolvePublic (publicId,systemId);if (resolved != null) { // Only find one PUBLIC resolution resolutions.addElement (resolved);return resolutions;} } else if (entityType == SYSTEM) { Vector localResolutions = c.resolveAllSystem (systemId);resolutions = appendVector (resolutions,localResolutions);break;} else if (entityType == SYSTEMREVERSE) { Vector localResolutions = c.resolveAllSystemReverse (systemId);resolutions = appendVector (resolutions,localResolutions);} } if (resolutions != null) { return resolutions;} else { return null;} }

originalComment: Parse an XML Catalog file.

It opens a connection to the URL and reads the catalog from the input stream.
codeFunctions: public void readCatalog (Catalog catalog,String fileUrl) throws MalformedURLException,IOException,CatalogException { URL url = null;try { url = new URL (fileUrl);} catch (MalformedURLException e) { url = new URL ("file:///" + fileUrl);} debug = catalog.getCatalogManager ().debug;try { URLConnection urlCon = url.openConnection ();readCatalog (catalog,urlCon.getInputStream ());} catch (FileNotFoundException e) { catalog.getCatalogManager ().debug.message (1,"Failed to load catalog, file not found",url.toString ());} }

originalComment: Parse an XML Catalog stream.
codeComment: The `readCatalog` method reads a catalog from an input stream using either a SAX parser or a traditional parser, depending on the configuration. It initializes a parser, sets up a handler to process the XML, and handles various exceptions that may occur during parsing. If the parser factory or class is not available, it throws a `CatalogException`. The method also sets an entity resolver if one is provided by the catalog manager.
codeFunctions: public void readCatalog (Catalog catalog,InputStream is) throws IOException,CatalogException { // Create an instance of the parser if (parserFactory == null && parserClass == null) { debug.message (1,"Cannot read SAX catalog without a parser");throw new CatalogException (CatalogException.UNPARSEABLE);} debug = catalog.getCatalogManager ().debug;EntityResolver bResolver = catalog.getCatalogManager ().getBootstrapResolver ();this.catalog = catalog;try { if (parserFactory != null) { SAXParser parser = parserFactory.newSAXParser ();SAXParserHandler spHandler = new SAXParserHandler ();spHandler.setContentHandler (this);if (bResolver != null) { spHandler.setEntityResolver (bResolver);} parser.parse (new InputSource (is),spHandler);} else { Parser parser = (Parser) Class.forName (parserClass).newInstance ();parser.setDocumentHandler (this);if (bResolver != null) { parser.setEntityResolver (bResolver);} parser.parse (new InputSource (is));} } catch (ClassNotFoundException cnfe) { throw new CatalogException (CatalogException.UNPARSEABLE);} catch (IllegalAccessException iae) { throw new CatalogException (CatalogException.UNPARSEABLE);} catch (InstantiationException ie) { throw new CatalogException (CatalogException.UNPARSEABLE);} catch (ParserConfigurationException pce) { throw new CatalogException (CatalogException.UNKNOWN_FORMAT);} catch (SAXException se) { Exception e = se.getException ();// FIXME: there must be a better way UnknownHostException uhe = new UnknownHostException ();FileNotFoundException fnfe = new FileNotFoundException ();if (e != null) { if (e.getClass () == uhe.getClass ()) { throw new CatalogException (CatalogException.PARSE_FAILED,e.toString ());} else if (e.getClass () == fnfe.getClass ()) { throw new CatalogException (CatalogException.PARSE_FAILED,e.toString ());} } throw new CatalogException (se);} }

codeComment: This method, `helpDelete`, is designed to assist in the deletion process of a node in a linked list. It takes two parameters, `b` and `f`, which are nodes of type `Node<K, V>`.    - Appends the `CodeSource` to the `results`. If the `CodeSource` is null, it appends "Null CodeSource".

   - For each interface, appends its name, hash code, class loader, and `CodeSource` to the `results`.

originalComment: Get the short name of the specified class by striping off the package name.
codeComment: This method, `stripPackageName`, takes a fully qualified class name as input and returns the class name without its package name. It does this by finding the last occurrence of the package separator (typically a dot `.`) in the class name string. If the separator is found, it extracts and returns the substring that comes after the separator. If the separator is not found, it simply returns the original class name.
codeFunctions: public static String stripPackageName (final String classname) { int idx = classname.lastIndexOf (PACKAGE_SEPARATOR);if (idx != - 1) return classname.substring (idx + 1,classname.length ());return classname;}

originalComment: Get the package name of the specified class.
codeComment: This method, `getPackageName`, takes a `String` parameter `classname` and returns the package name of the class. It first checks if the `classname` is empty and throws an `EmptyStringException` if it is. Then, it finds the last occurrence of the package separator (typically a dot `.`) in the `classname`. If the separator is found, it returns the substring from the start of the `classname` up to (but not including) the separator. If the separator is not found, it returns an empty string.
codeFunctions: public static String getPackageName (final String classname) { if (classname.length () == 0) throw new EmptyStringException ();int index = classname.lastIndexOf (PACKAGE_SEPARATOR);if (index != - 1) return classname.substring (0,index);return "";}

originalComment: Force the given class to be loaded fully.
codeComment:
The `forceLoad` method is designed to force a given class to load by invoking a static method or creating an instance of the class. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Input Validation**: The method first checks if the input `type` is `null` and throws a `NullArgumentException` if it is. It also returns immediately if the class is a primitive type or belongs to the `java.` or `javax.` packages.

2. **Package Name Check**: It retrieves the package name of the class and checks if it starts with `java.` or `javax.`. If so, it returns without attempting to load the class.

3. **Class Loading**: 
   - It retrieves all declared methods of the class.
   - It searches for a static method. If found, it invokes this static method with no arguments.
   - If no static method is found, it attempts to create a new instance of the class using `newInstance()`.

4. **Exception Handling**: Any exceptions thrown during the process are caught and added to a `ThrowableHandler`.

In essence, this method ensures that a specified class is loaded by either invoking a static method or creating an instance of the class, while handling exceptions gracefully.
codeFunctions: public static void forceLoad (final Class type) { if (type == null) throw new NullArgumentException ("type");// don't attempt to force primitives to load if (type.isPrimitive ()) return;// don't attempt to force java.* classes to load String packageName = Classes.getPackageName (type);// System.out.println("package name: " + packageName); if (packageName.startsWith ("java.") || packageName.startsWith ("javax.")) { return;} // System.out.println("forcing class to load: " + type); try { Method methods [ ] = type.getDeclaredMethods ();Method method = null;for (int i = 0;i < methods.length;i ++) { int modifiers = methods [ i ].getModifiers ();if (Modifier.isStatic (modifiers)) { method = methods [ i ];break;} } if (method != null) { method.invoke (null,(Object [ ]) null);} else { type.newInstance ();} } catch (Exception ignore) { ThrowableHandler.add (ignore);} }

originalComment: Get the wrapper class for the given primitive type.
codeComment: This method, `getPrimitiveWrapper`, takes a `Class` object representing a primitive type and returns its corresponding wrapper class. It first checks if the provided class is a primitive type; if not, it throws an `IllegalArgumentException`. Then, it iterates through a predefined array `PRIMITIVE_WRAPPER_MAP` to find a match for the primitive type. If a match is found, it returns the corresponding wrapper class. If no match is found, it throws an `UnreachableStatementException`, indicating that the `PRIMITIVE_WRAPPER_MAP` needs to be updated.
codeFunctions: public static Class getPrimitiveWrapper (final Class type) { if (!type.isPrimitive ()) { throw new IllegalArgumentException ("type is not a primitive class");} for (int i = 0;i < PRIMITIVE_WRAPPER_MAP.length;i += 2) { if (type.equals (PRIMITIVE_WRAPPER_MAP [ i ])) return PRIMITIVE_WRAPPER_MAP [ i + 1 ];} // should never get here, if we do then PRIMITIVE_WRAPPER_MAP // needs to be updated to include the missing mapping throw new UnreachableStatementException ();}

originalComment: Populates a list with all the interfaces implemented by the argument class c and all its superclasses.
codeComment: This method, `getAllInterfaces`, recursively retrieves all interfaces implemented by a given class and its superclasses. It takes a `List` to store the interfaces and a `Class` object as input. The method iterates through the class hierarchy, adding each interface to the list until it reaches the top of the hierarchy (i.e., when `c` becomes `null`).
codeFunctions: public static void getAllInterfaces (List allIfaces,Class c) { while (c != null) { Class [ ] ifaces = c.getInterfaces ();for (int n = 0;n < ifaces.length;n ++) { allIfaces.add (ifaces [ n ]);} c = c.getSuperclass ();} }

originalComment: Returns an array containing all the unique interfaces implemented by the argument class c and all its superclasses.Interfaces that appear multiple times through inheritence are only accounted for once.
codeComment: This method, `getAllUniqueInterfaces`, takes a `Class` object as input and returns an array of all unique interfaces implemented by the class and its superclasses. It uses a `HashSet` to store unique interfaces, iterating through the class hierarchy by repeatedly getting the superclass until it reaches `null`. For each class in the hierarchy, it retrieves the interfaces and adds them to the set. Finally, it converts the set to an array and returns it.
codeFunctions: public static Class [ ] getAllUniqueInterfaces (Class c) { Set uniqueIfaces = new HashSet ();while (c != null) { Class [ ] ifaces = c.getInterfaces ();for (int n = 0;n < ifaces.length;n ++) { uniqueIfaces.add (ifaces [ n ]);} c = c.getSuperclass ();} return (Class [ ]) uniqueIfaces.toArray (new Class [ uniqueIfaces.size () ]);}

originalComment: Check if the given class is a primitive wrapper class.
codeComment: The method `isPrimitiveWrapper` checks if a given `Class` type is a primitive wrapper type. It iterates through an array `PRIMITIVE_WRAPPER_MAP` in steps of two, comparing the input `type` with each wrapper class in the array. If a match is found, it returns `true`; otherwise, it returns `false`.
codeFunctions: public static boolean isPrimitiveWrapper (final Class type) { for (int i = 0;i < PRIMITIVE_WRAPPER_MAP.length;i += 2) { if (type.equals (PRIMITIVE_WRAPPER_MAP [ i + 1 ])) { return true;} } return false;}

originalComment: Instantiate a java class object
codeComment:
The `instantiate` method is designed to create an instance of a class based on a property value. It follows these steps:

1. **Retrieve Class Name**: It retrieves the class name from a property, using a default class name if the property is not found.
2. **Load Class**: It attempts to load the class using the retrieved class name. If the class cannot be found, it throws a `NestedRuntimeException`.
3. **Instantiate Class**: It tries to create an instance of the loaded class. If instantiation fails due to issues like `InstantiationException` or `IllegalAccessException`, it throws a `NestedRuntimeException`.
4. **Type Check**: It checks if the instantiated class is assignable from the expected class. If not, it throws a `NestedRuntimeException`.
5. **Return Instance**: If all checks pass, it returns the instantiated object.
codeFunctions: public static Object instantiate (Class expected,String property,String defaultClassName) { String className = getProperty (property,defaultClassName);Class clazz = null;try { clazz = loadClass (className);} catch (ClassNotFoundException e) { throw new NestedRuntimeException ("Cannot load class " + className,e);} Object result = null;try { result = clazz.newInstance ();} catch (InstantiationException e) { throw new NestedRuntimeException ("Error instantiating " + className,e);} catch (IllegalAccessException e) { throw new NestedRuntimeException ("Error instantiating " + className,e);} if (expected.isAssignableFrom (clazz) == false) throw new NestedRuntimeException ("Class " + className + " from classloader " + clazz.getClassLoader () + " is not of the expected class " + expected + " loaded from " + expected.getClassLoader ());return result;}

originalComment: Returns attribute s getter method.If the method not found then NoSuchMethodException will be thrown.
codeComment: This method, `getAttributeGetter`, takes a `Class` object and a `String` representing an attribute name as input. It constructs a method name by prepending "get" to the attribute name, capitalizing the first letter if it is lowercase. It then attempts to retrieve the method from the class using this name. If the method is not found, it replaces "get" with "is" and tries again. If the method is still not found, it throws a `NoSuchMethodException`.
codeFunctions: public final static Method getAttributeGetter (Class cls,String attr) throws NoSuchMethodException { StringBuffer buf = new StringBuffer (attr.length () + 3);buf.append ("get");if (Character.isLowerCase (attr.charAt (0))) { buf.append (Character.toUpperCase (attr.charAt (0))).append (attr.substring (1));} else { buf.append (attr);} try { return cls.getMethod (buf.toString (),(Class [ ]) null);} catch (NoSuchMethodException e) { buf.replace (0,3,"is");return cls.getMethod (buf.toString (),(Class [ ]) null);} }

originalComment: Convert a given String into the appropriate Class.
codeComment:
The method `convertToJavaClass` takes a class name as a string and a `ClassLoader` as input, and returns the corresponding Java `Class` object. It handles both primitive types and array types. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Array Handling**: The method first checks if the class name ends with "[]", indicating an array type. It counts the number of array dimensions and removes the "[]" suffix from the class name.

2. **Primitive Type Check**: It checks if the class name corresponds to a primitive type using a predefined map (`PRIMITIVE_NAME_TYPE_MAP`). If it does, it returns the corresponding `Class` object.

3. **Class Loading**: If the class is not a primitive, it attempts to load the class using the provided `ClassLoader`. If the class is not found, it throws a `ClassNotFoundException` with a descriptive message.

4. **Array Class Creation**: If the class name originally indicated an array type, it creates an array of the specified dimensions using `Array.newInstance` and returns the class of the created array.

5. **Return**: Finally, it returns the `Class` object representing the specified class, whether it's a primitive type, a regular class, or an array type.
codeFunctions: private final static Class convertToJavaClass (String name,ClassLoader cl) throws ClassNotFoundException { int arraySize = 0;while (name.endsWith ("[]")) { name = name.substring (0,name.length () - 2);arraySize ++;} // Check for a primitive type Class c = (Class) PRIMITIVE_NAME_TYPE_MAP.get (name);if (c == null) { // No primitive, try to load it from the given ClassLoader try { c = cl.loadClass (name);} catch (ClassNotFoundException cnfe) { throw new ClassNotFoundException ("Parameter class not found: " + name);} } // if we have an array get the array class if (arraySize > 0) { int [ ] dims = new int [ arraySize ];for (int i = 0;i < arraySize;i ++) { dims [ i ] = 1;} c = Array.newInstance (c,dims).getClass ();} return c;}

originalComment: Maintain the elements in the set.Removes objects from the set that have been reclaimed due to GC.
codeComment: The `maintain` method is a protected final method that processes a queue of `WeakObject` instances. It repeatedly retrieves objects from the queue using `poll()` until the queue is empty. For each retrieved `WeakObject`, it removes the object from a set named `set`. This method ensures that the set only contains valid, non-weakly-referenced objects by removing any that have been enqueued for removal.
codeFunctions: protected final void maintain () { WeakObject weak;while ((weak = (WeakObject) queue.poll ()) != null) { set.remove (weak);} }

originalComment: Return an iteration over the elements in the set.
codeComment: This code defines an `iterator` method that returns an `Iterator` for a set of `WeakObject` instances. The iterator handles null values and multiple invocations of `hasNext()`. It uses a `WeakObject` to wrap the actual objects, allowing them to be garbage collected if they are no longer strongly referenced. The iterator's `hasNext()` method checks if there are more elements available, and the `next()` method retrieves the next element. The `remove()` method removes the current element from the underlying set.
codeFunctions: public Iterator iterator () { return new Iterator () { /** The set's iterator */ Iterator iter = set.iterator ();/** JBCOMMON-24, handle null values and multiple invocations of hasNext() */ Object UNKNOWN = new Object ();/** The next available object. */ Object next = UNKNOWN;public boolean hasNext () { if (next != UNKNOWN) { return true;} while (iter.hasNext ()) { WeakObject weak = (WeakObject) iter.next ();Object obj = null;if (weak != null && (obj = weak.get ()) == null) { // object has been reclaimed by the GC continue;} next = obj;return true;} return false;} public Object next () { if ((next == UNKNOWN) &&!hasNext ()) { throw new NoSuchElementException ();} Object obj = next;next = UNKNOWN;return obj;} public void remove () { iter.remove ();} };}

originalComment: Create a URL lister for the supplied protocol
codeComment: The `createURLLister` method takes a `String` parameter `protocol` and returns an instance of `URLLister`. It first retrieves the class name associated with the given protocol from a map called `classes`. If no class name is found, it throws a `MalformedURLException`. It then attempts to load the class using the current thread's context class loader and instantiate it. If any exceptions occur during this process, such as `ClassNotFoundException`, `InstantiationException`, or `IllegalAccessException`, they are caught and rethrown as `MalformedURLException` with the original exception's message.
codeFunctions: public URLLister createURLLister (String protocol) throws MalformedURLException { try { String className = (String) classes.get (protocol);if (className == null) { throw new MalformedURLException ("No lister class defined for protocol " + protocol);} Class <?> clazz = Thread.currentThread ().getContextClassLoader ().loadClass (className);return (URLLister) clazz.newInstance ();} catch (ClassNotFoundException e) { throw new MalformedURLException (e.getMessage ());} catch (InstantiationException e) { throw new MalformedURLException (e.getMessage ());} catch (IllegalAccessException e) { throw new MalformedURLException (e.getMessage ());} }

originalComment: Returns an entry set for all properties in this group.
codeComment: This method, `entrySet`, is designed to return a filtered set of entries from a map. It first retrieves the entire entry set from the superclass using `super.entrySet(true)`. Then, it creates a new `AbstractSet` that only includes entries whose keys start with a specified `basename`. The `isInGroup` method checks if a given entry's key starts with `basename`. The `size` method counts the number of entries that meet this criterion by iterating through the `superSet`. The `iterator` method returns an iterator that filters entries on-the-fly, ensuring only those with keys starting with `basename` are returned. The iterator also supports removing entries from the original set.
codeFunctions: @ SuppressWarnings ("unchecked") public Set entrySet () { final Set superSet = super.entrySet (true);return new java.util.AbstractSet () { private boolean isInGroup (Map.Entry entry) { String key = (String) entry.getKey ();return key.startsWith (basename);} public int size () { Iterator iter = superSet.iterator ();int count = 0;while (iter.hasNext ()) { Map.Entry entry = (Map.Entry) iter.next ();if (isInGroup (entry)) { count ++;} } return count;} public Iterator iterator () { return new Iterator () { private Iterator iter = superSet.iterator ();private Object next;public boolean hasNext () { if (next != null) return true;while (next == null) { if (iter.hasNext ()) { Map.Entry entry = (Map.Entry) iter.next ();if (isInGroup (entry)) { next = entry;return true;} } else { break;} } return false;} public Object next () { if (next == null) throw new java.util.NoSuchElementException ();Object obj = next;next = null;return obj;} public void remove () { iter.remove ();} };} };}

originalComment: Add a bound property listener.
codeComment: This method, `addPropertyListener`, is designed to add a `BoundPropertyListener` to a list of listeners for a specific property. It first constructs the property name using the `makePropertyName` method. It then retrieves the list of listeners associated with that property from a map called `boundListeners`. If the list does not exist, it creates a new one and adds it to the map. Finally, it checks if the listener is already in the list; if not, it adds the listener to the list and notifies the listener that it has been bound to the property.
codeFunctions: protected void addPropertyListener (final BoundPropertyListener listener) { // get the bound property name String name = makePropertyName (listener.getPropertyName ());// get the bound listener list for the property List list = (List) boundListeners.get (name);// if list is null, then add a new list if (list == null) { list = new ArrayList ();boundListeners.put (name,list);} // if listener is not in the list already, then add it if (!list.contains (listener)) { list.add (listener);// notify listener that is is bound listener.propertyBound (this);} }

originalComment: Remove a bound property listener.
codeComment: This method, `removePropertyListener`, removes a specified `BoundPropertyListener` from the list of listeners associated with a property. It first constructs the property name using the listener's property name. Then, it retrieves the list of listeners for that property. If the list is not null, it attempts to remove the listener from the list. If the listener is successfully removed, it notifies the listener that it has been unbound from the property. The method returns a boolean indicating whether the listener was successfully removed.
codeFunctions: protected boolean removePropertyListener (final BoundPropertyListener listener) { // get the bound property name String name = makePropertyName (listener.getPropertyName ());// get the bound listener list for the property List list = (List) boundListeners.get (name);boolean removed = false;if (list != null) { removed = list.remove (listener);// notify listener that is was unbound if (removed) listener.propertyUnbound (this);} return removed;}

originalComment: Locate a value editor for a given target type.
codeComment: The method `findEditor` attempts to locate a `PropertyEditor` for a given type name. It first checks if the type name corresponds to a primitive type using the `Classes.getPrimitiveTypeForName` method. If the type is not a primitive, it attempts to load the class using the current thread's context class loader. originalComment: Convert a string value into the true value for typeName using the PropertyEditor associated with typeName.

It first checks if the type is a primitive type and retrieves the corresponding class. If not, it loads the class using the current thread's context class loader. It then finds a `PropertyEditor` for the class and uses it to set the value from the string. If no `PropertyEditor` is found, it throws an `IntrospectionException`.
codeFunctions: public static Object convertValue (String text,String typeName) throws ClassNotFoundException,IntrospectionException { // see if it is a primitive type first Class <?> typeClass = Classes.getPrimitiveTypeForName (typeName);if (typeClass == null) { ClassLoader loader = Thread.currentThread ().getContextClassLoader ();typeClass = loader.loadClass (typeName);} PropertyEditor editor = PropertyEditorManager.findEditor (typeClass);if (editor == null) { throw new IntrospectionException ("No property editor for type=" + typeClass);} editor.setAsText (text);return editor.getValue ();}

originalComment: Timeout worker method.
codeComment: The `doWork` method continuously processes tasks from a queue until a cancellation signal is received. It retrieves tasks from the queue, wraps them in a `TimeoutWorker` to handle timeouts, and submits them to a thread pool for execution. If an error occurs during task submission, it is caught and logged. Once a task is completed, it is marked as done. If the method is cancelled, it cancels the `TimeoutFactory`.
codeFunctions: private void doWork () { while (cancelled.get () == false) { TimeoutExt work = queue.take ();// Do work, if any if (work != null) { // Wrap the TimeoutExt with a runnable that invokes the target callback TimeoutWorker worker = new TimeoutWorker (work);try { threadPool.run (worker);} catch (Throwable t) { // protect the worker thread from pool enqueue errors ThrowableHandler.add (ThrowableHandler.Type.ERROR,t);} synchronized (work) { work.done ();} } } // TimeoutFactory was cancelled queue.cancel ();}

originalComment: Checks an object implements the given class

codeComment:
The `jar` method is a recursive function that adds files and directories to a JAR archive. It takes three parameters: a `File` object representing the source file or directory, a `String` prefix for the archive entry, and a `JarInfo` object containing information about the JAR output stream and a buffer for reading file contents.

- If the source is a directory, the method creates a `ZipEntry` for the directory, sets its metadata (time, method, size, and CRC), and adds it to the JAR output stream. It then recursively processes each file and subdirectory within the source directory.
  
- If the source is a file, the method creates a `ZipEntry` for the file, sets its metadata, and adds it to the JAR output stream. It reads the file's contents into a buffer and writes them to the JAR output stream.

The method handles both files and directories, ensuring that the entire directory structure is preserved in the JAR archive.
codeFunctions: private static void jar (File src,String prefix,JarInfo info) throws IOException { JarOutputStream jout = info.out;if (src.isDirectory ()) { // create / init the zip entry prefix = prefix + src.getName () + "/";ZipEntry entry = new ZipEntry (prefix);entry.setTime (src.lastModified ());entry.setMethod (JarOutputStream.STORED);entry.setSize (0L);entry.setCrc (0L);jout.putNextEntry (entry);jout.closeEntry ();// process the sub-directories File [ ] files = src.listFiles (info.filter);for (int i = 0;i < files.length;i ++) { jar (files [ i ],prefix,info);} } else if (src.isFile ()) { // get the required info objects byte [ ] buffer = info.buffer;// create / init the zip entry ZipEntry entry = new ZipEntry (prefix + src.getName ());entry.setTime (src.lastModified ());jout.putNextEntry (entry);// dump the file FileInputStream in = new FileInputStream (src);int len;while ((len = in.read (buffer,0,buffer.length)) != - 1) { jout.write (buffer,0,len);} in.close ();jout.closeEntry ();} }

codeFunctions: public static String join (final String [ ] list) { // zero, empty or one element if (list == null) { return null;} else if (list.length == 0) { return "";} else if (list.length == 1) { return list [ 0 ];} // two or more elements final StringBuilder builder = new StringBuilder ();for (String item:list) { if (builder.length () > 0) { builder.append (", ");} builder.append (item);} return builder.toString ();}

originalComment: Verifies that the entity has exactly one id field of type long.

codeFunctions: private void inspectId () { if (entityModel.getIdField () == null) { // Default to field named "id" List < FieldModel > fields = entityModel.getFields ();for (FieldModel f:fields) { if (EntityModel.DEFAULT_ID_FIELD.equals (f.getFieldName ())) { entityModel.setIdField (f);} } } FieldModel idField = entityModel.getIdField ();if (idField != null && "long".equals (idField.getJavaType ())) { return;} else { abort ("Entity must contain a field named id or annotated with @Id of type long");} }

originalComment: Renders this object as JPQL query string.
codeComment: The `render` method constructs a SQL query string based on various components such as `select`, `deleteFrom`, `update`, `set`, `from`, `where`, `group`, and `order`. It uses a `StringBuilder` to efficiently build the query. The method checks if each component is not empty and appends the corresponding SQL syntax to the `StringBuilder`. Finally, it returns the constructed SQL query as a string.
codeFunctions: public String render () { StringBuilder query = new StringBuilder ();if (!select.isEmpty ()) { query.append ("SELECT ");query.append (StringUtils.join (select.items));} if (!deleteFrom.isEmpty ()) { query.append ("DELETE FROM ");query.append (deleteFrom.item);} if (!update.isEmpty ()) { query.append ("UPDATE ");query.append (update.item);if (!set.isEmpty ()) { query.append (" SET ");query.append (StringUtils.join (set.items));} } if (!from.isEmpty ()) { query.append (" FROM ");query.append (StringUtils.join (from.items));} if (!where.isEmpty ()) { query.append (" WHERE ");query.append (where.render ());} if (!group.isEmpty ()) { query.append (" GROUP BY ");query.append (StringUtils.join (group.items));} if (order.isEmpty () == false) { query.append (" ORDER BY ");query.append (StringUtils.join (order.items));} return query.toString ();}

originalComment: Add the set of bindings for a given plan to this store.Any previously stored bindings for this plan will be replaced.
codeComment: This method, `add`, manages a collection of plan bindings. It first checks if the provided `plan` is null and returns immediately if it is. If the `plan` already exists in the `bindings` map, it removes the existing bindings, updates the `cachedsize` accordingly, and then adds the new bindings. The `cachedsize` is adjusted based on whether the old or new bindings are null or empty.
codeFunctions: public void add (Plan plan,Set < Belief > planBindings) { if (plan == null) { return;} // remove any old bindings, making sure to decrement the cached size if (this.bindings.containsKey (plan)) { Set < Belief > oldBindings = this.bindings.remove (plan);if (oldBindings == null || oldBindings.isEmpty ()) { cachedsize --;} else { cachedsize -= oldBindings.size ();} } // add this binding and update the cached size this.bindings.put (plan,planBindings);if (planBindings == null || planBindings.isEmpty ()) { cachedsize ++;} else { cachedsize += planBindings.size ();} }

originalComment: Selects a plan instance from the set of plan bindings using the given policy.
codeComment:
The `selectPlan` method selects a plan based on a given `PlanSelectionPolicy`. It initializes a `Plan` object `plan` to `null` and an `index` to `0`. The method uses a `switch` statement to handle different policies:

- **FIRST**: Retrieves all plans from `bindings` and selects the first plan. It sets the `index` to `0` and calls `setPlanVariables` with the selected plan.
- **LAST**: Retrieves all plans from `bindings` and selects the last plan. It sets the `index` to the last position and calls `setPlanVariables` with the selected plan.
- **RANDOM**: Calls `selectPlanAtRandom` to select a plan randomly.
- **DEFAULT**: Ignores any remaining policies.

Finally, the method returns the selected `plan`.
codeFunctions: public Plan selectPlan (PlanSelectionPolicy policy) { Plan plan = null;int index = 0;switch (policy) { case FIRST:case LAST:Plan [ ] plans = bindings.keySet ().toArray (new Plan [ 0 ]);plan = (policy == PlanSelectionPolicy.FIRST)?plans [ 0 ]:plans [ plans.length - 1 ];index = (policy == PlanSelectionPolicy.FIRST)?0:plans.length - 1;setPlanVariables (plan.getAgent (),plan,bindings.get (plan),index);break;case RANDOM:plan = selectPlanAtRandom ();break;default:// TODO: ignore remaining polic break;} return plan;}

originalComment: Selects a plan instance at random from the set of plan bindings.
codeComment: The method `selectPlanAtRandom` randomly selects a plan from a set of plans. It uses a random index generated by `rand.nextInt(size())` to determine which plan to select. The method iterates through the plans and their associated beliefs (variables). If a plan has associated beliefs, it adjusts the index based on the number of beliefs. Once the index points to a plan, it sets the plan's variables if there are any associated beliefs and returns the selected plan.
codeFunctions: private Plan selectPlanAtRandom () { Plan plan = null;Set < Belief > vars = null;int index = rand.nextInt (size ());int idx = 0;boolean bindingsExist = false;for (Plan p:bindings.keySet ()) { vars = bindings.get (p);bindingsExist = (vars != null &&!vars.isEmpty ());idx += bindingsExist?vars.size ():1;if (idx > index) { plan = p;if (bindingsExist) { index = index - (idx - vars.size ());setPlanVariables (plan.getAgent (),plan,vars,index);} break;} } return plan;}

originalComment: Sets the plan instance variables using the given results set.
codeComment: The `setPlanVariables` method sets the variables of a given plan instance based on a selected belief from a set of results. It first checks if the agent or plan instance is null and returns if so. It retrieves a belief at a specified index from the results set and checks if it is null. If the belief's tuple is null, it returns. It then iterates over the tuple, retrieves the field names associated with each element, and stores them in a HashMap. If an exception occurs while retrieving a field name, it logs an error. Finally, it sets the plan variables using the HashMap.
codeFunctions: private final void setPlanVariables (Agent agent,Plan planInstance,Set < Belief > results,int choice) { if (agent == null || planInstance == null) { return;} Belief belief = getResultAtIndex (results,choice);if (belief == null) { return;} Object [ ] tuple = belief.getTuple ();if (tuple == null) { return;} int index = 0;HashMap < String,Object > vars = new HashMap < String,Object > ();for (Object o:belief.getTuple ()) { try { String fieldname = ABeliefStore.getFieldName (agent.getId (),belief.getBeliefset (),index);vars.put (fieldname,o);} catch (BeliefBaseException e) { Log.error ("Agent " + agent.getId () + " could not retrive belief set field: " + e.getMessage ());} index ++;} planInstance.setPlanVariables (vars);}

originalComment: Gets the result at the given index from the results set.
codeComment: This method retrieves a `Belief` object from a set of `Belief` objects at a specified index. It first checks if the set is null or if the index is out of bounds. If these conditions are not met, it iterates through the set and returns the `Belief` at the specified index. If the index is invalid or the set is null, it returns null.
codeFunctions: private Belief getResultAtIndex (Set < Belief > results,int index) { Belief belief = null;if (!(results == null || index < 0 || index >= results.size ())) { int idx = 0;for (Belief b:results) { if (idx == index) { belief = b;break;} idx ++;} } return belief;}

originalComment: Creates a new logger.
codeComment:
This method, `createLogger`, sets up a logger with a specified name, logging level, and output file. It uses the SLF4J and Logback libraries to configure the logger. Here's a summary of the steps:

1. **Logger Context Initialization**: Retrieves the `LoggerContext` from the `LoggerFactory`.
2. **Pattern Layout Encoder Setup**: Creates a `PatternLayoutEncoder` to define the log message format, including date, level, thread, logger name, file, line number, and message.
3. **File Appender Configuration**: Sets up a `FileAppender` to write logs to a specified file, using the configured pattern layout encoder. The appender is set to overwrite the file each time it starts.
4. **Logger Creation and Configuration**: 
   - Retrieves a logger instance with the specified name.
   - Detaches and stops all existing appenders from the logger.
   - Adds the file appender to the logger.
   - Sets the logging level and ensures the logger is additive (i.e., it will also log to the root logger).

The method returns the configured logger.
codeFunctions: public static Logger createLogger (String name,Level level,String file) { LoggerContext lc = (LoggerContext) LoggerFactory.getILoggerFactory ();PatternLayoutEncoder ple = new PatternLayoutEncoder ();ple.setPattern ("%date %level [%thread] %logger{10} [%file:%line]%n%msg%n%n");ple.setContext (lc);ple.start ();FileAppender < ILoggingEvent > fileAppender = new FileAppender < ILoggingEvent > ();fileAppender.setFile (file);fileAppender.setEncoder (ple);fileAppender.setAppend (false);fileAppender.setContext (lc);fileAppender.start ();logger = (Logger) LoggerFactory.getLogger (name);logger.detachAndStopAllAppenders ();// detach console (doesn't seem to work) logger.addAppender (fileAppender);// attach file appender logger.setLevel (level);logger.setAdditive (true);// set to true if root should log too return logger;}

originalComment: Creates a given number of agents of a given Class and adds the newly created agents to the given store.
codeComment:
The `loadAgent` method is responsible for loading an agent class, registering it in the global agent catalog, and creating a specified number of instances of that agent. Here's a summary of the method's steps:

1. **Load the Agent Class**: The method attempts to load the specified agent class using the `loadClass` method. If the class cannot be loaded, it returns `false`.

2. **Register the Agent Type**: It creates an `AgentType` object for the loaded class and registers it in the global agent catalog.

3. **Retrieve Goals**: The method retrieves the goals associated with the agent class using the `getGoalsFromAgentInfoAnnotation` method. If no goals are found, it returns `false`.

4. **Load Goal-Plan Nodes**: It performs a first pass to load the goals and their associated plans into the `AgentType` object.

5. **Complete Goal-Plan Hierarchy**: It completes the goal-plan hierarchy by calling `completeGoalPlanHierarchy`.

6. **Create Agent Instances**: Finally, it creates the specified number of instances of the agent type and adds them to the provided `AObjectCatalog`.

7. **Return Success**: If all steps are successful, the method returns `true`.
codeFunctions: public static boolean loadAgent (String className,int num,AObjectCatalog agents) { // Load the Agent class Class <?> aclass = loadClass (className,Agent.class);if (aclass == null) { return false;} // Save this agent type to the catalog of known agent types AgentType atype = new AgentType (className);atype.setAgentClass (aclass);GlobalState.agentTypes.push (atype);// Find the goals that this agent has String [ ] goals = getGoalsFromAgentInfoAnnotation (aclass);if (goals.length == 0) { return false;} // First pass: get the goals and their plans (flat goal-plan list) loadGoalPlanNodes (atype,goals);// Second pass: complete the goal-plan hierarchy completeGoalPlanHierarchy ();// Now create the specified number of instances of this agent type createAgentsInCatalog (agents,atype,aclass,num);// return success return true;}

codeComment:
This method, `createAgentsInCatalog`, is responsible for creating a specified number of agent instances and adding them to an agent catalog. Here's a summary of its functionality:

1. **Parameters**:
   - `agents`: An `AObjectCatalog` object where the created agents will be stored.
   - `atype`: An `AgentType` object that provides the goal plan tree hierarchy for the agents.
   - `aclass`: A `Class<?>` object representing the class of the agent to be instantiated.
   - `num`: An integer specifying the number of agents to create.

2. **Process**:
   - Initializes a counter `added` to track the number of successfully created agents.
   - Uses a `try-catch` block to handle potential exceptions during agent creation.
   - Iterates `num` times to create each agent:
     - Constructs a new agent instance using the class's constructor that takes a `String` parameter, naming each agent with a prefix 'a' followed by an index.
     - Assigns the goal plan tree hierarchy from `atype` to the newly created agent.
     - Adds the agent to the `agents` catalog.
     - Increments the `added` counter.
   - Logs the number of agents successfully added.

3. **Exception Handling**:
   - Catches and logs errors related to method not found, security issues, instantiation, illegal access, illegal argument, and invocation target exceptions, indicating failure to create an instance of the specified class.

4. **Logging**:
   - Uses a logger to log the completion of agent creation and any errors encountered during the process.
codeFunctions: private static void createAgentsInCatalog (AObjectCatalog agents,AgentType atype,Class <?> aclass,int num) { int added = 0;try { for (int i = 0;i < num;i ++) { // Create a new instance (name prefix 'a' for agents) Agent agent = (Agent) (aclass.getConstructor (String.class).newInstance ("a" + Integer.toString (i)));// Assign the static goal plan tree hierarchy to this instance agent.setGoals (atype.getGoals ());// Add this instance to the catalog of agent instances agents.push (agent);added ++;} logger.info ("Finished loading {} agents",added);} catch (NoSuchMethodException | SecurityException | InstantiationException | IllegalAccessException | IllegalArgumentException | InvocationTargetException e) { logger.error ("Could not create instance of class " + aclass.getName ());} }

2. Tries to load the class using `Class.forName(className)`.
3. Checks if the loaded class is assignable from `JillExtension`. If not, it logs an error and returns `null`.

Finally, the method returns the instantiated `JillExtension` object or `null` if an error occurred.
codeFunctions: public static JillExtension loadExtension (String className) { JillExtension extension = null;Class <?> eclass;try { // Check that we have the extension class, else abort eclass = Class.forName (className);if (!JillExtension.class.isAssignableFrom (eclass)) { logger.error ("Class '" + className + "' does not implement " + JillExtension.class.getName ());return null;} logger.info ("Loading extension " + className);extension = (JillExtension) (eclass.newInstance ());} catch (ClassNotFoundException | SecurityException | InstantiationException | IllegalAccessException | IllegalArgumentException e) { logger.error ("Could not load extension " + className,e);} return extension;}

originalComment: Parses the given command line arguments.
codeComment: The `parse` method processes command-line arguments provided in the `args` array. It iterates through each argument, checking for specific options like `--help` and handling arguments that require an accompanying option. If the `--help` option is encountered, it calls the `abort` method with `null`. For other arguments that need an option, it calls `parseArgumentWithOption` with the current argument and the next one in the array, incrementing the index to skip the processed option. After parsing, it checks if the configuration is valid, including the presence of agents, and calls `abort` with an appropriate message if any required configuration is missing.
codeFunctions: public static void parse (String [ ] args) { for (int i = 0;args != null && i < args.length;i ++) { // First parse args that don't require an option if ("--help".equals (args [ i ])) { abort (null);} // Now parse args that must be accompanied by an option if (i + 1 < args.length) { parseArgumentWithOption (args [ i ],args [ ++ i ]);// force increment the counter } } // Abort if required args were not given if (config == null) { abort ("Configuration file or string was not given");} else if (config.getAgents () == null || config.getAgents ().isEmpty ()) { abort ("Configuration is missing agents specification");} }

originalComment: Parses the given command line argument and associated option.Will abort if an unrecoverable error occurs.
codeComment:
The `parseArgumentWithOption` method processes command-line arguments and their corresponding options. It uses a `switch` statement to handle different argument types:

- `--config`: Loads configuration settings from a string.
- `--configfile`: Loads configuration settings from a file.
- `--exit-on-idle`: Sets a global constant to determine whether the application should exit when idle, based on a boolean value.
- `--plan-selection-policy`: Sets a global constant for the plan selection policy, parsing the option value to an enum. If the value is invalid, it aborts the process with an error message.
- `--plan-instances-limit`: Sets a global constant for the plan instances limit, parsing the option value to an integer. If the value is not a number, it aborts the process with an error message.

Any other arguments are ignored, as they may be used by external components.
codeFunctions: private static void parseArgumentWithOption (String arg,String opt) { switch (arg) { case "--config":config = loadConfigFromString (opt);break;case "--configfile":config = loadConfigFromFile (opt);break;case "--exit-on-idle":GlobalConstant.EXIT_ON_IDLE = Boolean.parseBoolean (opt);break;case "--plan-selection-policy":try { GlobalConstant.PLAN_SELECTION_POLICY = GlobalConstant.PlanSelectionPolicy.valueOf (opt);} catch (IllegalArgumentException e) { abort ("Unknown plan selection policy '" + opt + "'");} break;case "--plan-instances-limit":try { GlobalConstant.PLAN_INSTANCES_LIMIT = Integer.parseInt (opt);} catch (NumberFormatException e) { abort ("Option value '" + opt + "' is not a number");} break;default:// Ignore any other arguments (which may be used by components external to Jill) break;} }

codeComment:
The `run` method is a loop that continuously manages a pool of agents. It performs the following tasks:

1. **Initialization**: Initializes a set `toRemove` to keep track of agents that need to be removed.

2. **Loop Execution**:
   - **Idle Check**: Initializes a boolean `idle` to `true`, indicating that no agents are active.
   - **Remove Inactive Agents**: Calls `removeInactiveAgents()` to remove agents that have become idle due to external events.
   - **Add Active Agents**: Calls `addActiveAgents()` to add agents that have become active due to external events.
   - **Agent Processing**: Iterates over `activeAgents`:
     - Retrieves the agent and its execution stack.
     - Checks if the stack is valid; if not, marks the agent for removal.
     - If the stack is valid, sets `idle` to `false`.
     - Retrieves the top item of the stack.
     - If the item is a `Plan`, executes a plan step and manages the plan.
     - If the item is a `Goal`, finds a plan for it and puts it on the stack.
     - Calls `nextActiveStack()` to select the next active stack for the agent.
   - **Remove Finished Agents**: Removes agents that have finished executing plans and gone idle in the current cycle using `removeFinishedAgents(toRemove)`.

3. **Idle Handling**: If no agents are active (`idle` is `true`), waits for an external message using `waitOnExternalMessage()`. If a shutdown signal is received, the loop breaks.

4. **Exit**: Logs a debug message indicating that the pool is exiting.
codeFunctions: public void run () { Set < Integer > toRemove = new HashSet < Integer > ();do { boolean idle = true;// Remove agents that have have become idle due to an external event removeInactiveAgents ();// Add agents that have have become active due to an external event addActiveAgents ();for (Integer i:activeAgents) { Agent agent = (Agent) GlobalState.agents.get (i);Stack255 agentExecutionStack = (Stack255) (agent).getExecutionStack ();if (!isStackValid (agent,agentExecutionStack)) { // Mark this agent for removal toRemove.add (i);continue;} // At least one agent is active idle = false;// Get the item at the top of the stack Object node = (Object) agentExecutionStack.get ((byte) (agentExecutionStack.size () - 1));if (node instanceof Plan) { // If it is a plan then execute a plan step; and if it finished then remove it managePlan (i,agentExecutionStack,(Plan) node,toRemove);} else if (node instanceof Goal) { // If it is a goal then find a plan for it and put it on the stack manageGoal (i,agent,agentExecutionStack,(Goal) node);} agent.nextActiveStack ();// select the next active stack for next time } // remove agents that have finished executing plans and have gone idle in this cycle removeFinishedAgents (toRemove);if (idle) { waitOnExternalMessage ();if (shutdown) { break;} } } while (true);logger.debug ("Pool {} is exiting",poolid);}

codeComment: This method checks if the execution stack of an agent is valid. It returns `false` if the stack is `null`, empty, or full (reaching the size limit of 255). If the stack size is within the valid range, it logs the stack's current size and returns `true`.

Cannot continue.",Log.logPrefix (agent.getId ()));return false;} return true;}

originalComment: Manages the goal at the top of the execution stack of an agent.All relevant plans are evaluated to see if their context conditions hold.Plans deemed applicable are then added to the list of bindings from which a plan instane will be eventually selected.
codeComment:
The `manageGoal` method is responsible for managing a goal for a given agent by selecting an appropriate plan to handle it. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Retrieve Goal Type**: It retrieves the goal type associated with the given goal node.
2. **Initialize Plan Types**: It initializes the plan types based on the goal type.
3. **Clear Bindings**: It clears any previous plan bindings to ensure a fresh start.
4. **Evaluate Context Conditions**: For each plan type, it creates an instance of the plan and evaluates its context condition. If the condition is met, it adds the results to the bindings.
5. **Check for Applicable Plans**: If no applicable plans are found, it logs a message and returns `false`.
6. **Meta-Level Planning**: It notifies the agent about the pre-plan selection process.
7. **Select Plan**: It selects a plan using a specified policy.
8. **Push Plan to Stack**: It pushes the selected plan onto the agent's execution stack.
9. **Return Success**: It returns `true` indicating successful plan selection and execution.
codeFunctions: private boolean manageGoal (int agentIndex,Agent agent,Stack255 agentExecutionStack,Goal node) { // Get the goal type for this goal GoalType gtype = (GoalType) GlobalState.goalTypes.find (node.getClass ().getName ());byte [ ] ptypes = gtype.getChildren ();assert (ptypes != null);// Clear any previous plan bindings before adding any new ones bindings.clear ();for (int p = 0;p < ptypes.length;p ++) { PlanType ptype = (PlanType) GlobalState.planTypes.get (ptypes [ p ]);try { // Create an object of this Plan type, so we can // access its context condition Plan planInstance = (Plan) (ptype.getPlanClass ().getConstructor (Agent.class,Goal.class,String.class).newInstance (GlobalState.agents.get (agentIndex),node,"p"));// Clear previously buffered context results if any agent.clearLastResults ();// Evaluate the context condition if (planInstance.context ()) { // Get the results of context query just performed Set < Belief > results = agent.getLastResults ();// Add the results to the bindings bindings.add (planInstance,(results == null)?null:new LinkedHashSet < Belief > (results));} } catch (NoSuchMethodException | SecurityException | InstantiationException | IllegalAccessException | IllegalArgumentException | InvocationTargetException e) { logger.error ("Could not create plan object of type " + ptype.getClass ().getName (),e);} } int numBindings = bindings.size ();if (numBindings == 0) { // No plan options for this goal at this point in time, so move to the next agent logger.debug (Log.logPrefix (agent.getId ()) + " has no applicable plans for goal " + gtype + " and will continue to wait indefinitely");return false;} // Call the meta-level planning prior to plan selection agent.notifyAgentPrePlanSelection (bindings);// Pick a plan option using specified policy Plan planInstance = bindings.selectPlan (GlobalConstant.PLAN_SELECTION_POLICY);// Now push the plan on to the intention stack synchronized (agentExecutionStack) { logger.debug (Log.logPrefix (agent.getId ()) + " choose an instance of plan " + planInstance.getClass ().getSimpleName () + " to handle goal " + node.getClass ().getSimpleName ());agentExecutionStack.push (planInstance);} return true;}

originalComment: Move a disc from pin A to pin B.
codeComment:
The `move` method is responsible for moving a disc from one pin to another in a game, likely similar to the Tower of Hanoi puzzle. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Input Validation**: 
   - Checks if the pin numbers (`pinA` and `pinB`) are valid. If not, logs a warning and returns `false`.
   - Checks if the source pin (`pinA`) is empty. If it is, logs a warning and returns `false`.
   - Checks if the source and destination pins are the same. If they are, logs an informational message and returns `true` since no move is needed.

2. **Disc Comparison**:
   - Retrieves the disc number on the source pin (`pinA`).
   - Retrieves the disc number on the destination pin (`pinB`). If the destination pin is empty, it uses `Integer.MAX_VALUE` to ensure any disc can be moved there.
   - Compares the disc numbers. If the disc on the destination pin is smaller than the disc on the source pin, logs a warning and returns `false` because a larger disc cannot be placed on a smaller one.

3. **Move Execution**:
   - If all checks pass, removes the disc from the source pin and adds it to the destination pin.
   - Returns `true` to indicate the move was successful.
codeFunctions: public boolean move (int pinA,int pinB) { // Nothing to do if the pin number is invalid if (pinA < 0 || pinA >= pins.length || pinB < 0 || pinB >= pins.length) { Log.warn ("Invalid board pin specified " + pinA + ". Should be between 0.." + (pins.length - 1) + " (inclusive).");return false;} else if (pins [ pinA ].isEmpty ()) { Log.warn ("No disc on pin" + pinA);return false;} else if (pinA == pinB) { Log.info ("Moving disc from pin" + pinA + " on to itself (means the board will not change)");return true;} int discOnA = pins [ pinA ].get (pins [ pinA ].size () - 1);int discOnB = (pins [ pinB ].isEmpty ())?Integer.MAX_VALUE:pins [ pinB ].get (pins [ pinB ].size () - 1);if (discOnB < discOnA) { Log.warn ("Cannot move disc" + discOnA + " (pin" + pinA + ") on to smaller disc" + discOnB + " (pin" + pinB + ")");return false;} pins [ pinB ].add (pins [ pinA ].remove (pins [ pinA ].size () - 1));return true;}

originalComment: Initialises the Jill engine.
codeComment:
The `init` method initializes a system based on a provided configuration. It performs the following steps:

1. **User Input Pause**: If the configuration specifies, it pauses the program to wait for user input.
2. **Logging Configuration**: Sets up logging with the specified log level and file.
3. **Agent Count Calculation**: Calculates the total number of agents based on the configuration.
4. **Global State Reset**: Resets the global state and initializes the agent catalog.
5. **Belief Base Creation**: Creates a central belief base for the agents.
6. **Agent Creation**: Loads and creates agents based on the configuration, logging the duration of this process.
7. **Thread Pool Initialization**: Initializes thread pools for intention selection.
8. **Output Redirection**: Redirects agent program output to a specified file if provided, otherwise uses standard output.
9. **Intention Selection Threads Initialization**: Initializes threads for intention selection based on the configuration.
10. **Return Status**: Returns `true` if initialization is successful, `false` otherwise.
codeFunctions: public static boolean init (Config config) { // Pause for key press from user if requested if (config.isDoPauseForUserInput ()) { Program.pauseForUserInput ();} // Configure logging Log.createLogger (Main.LOGGER_NAME,config.getLogLevel (),config.getLogFile ());logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger (Main.LOGGER_NAME);int numAgents = 0;for (Config.AgentTypeData agentType:config.getAgents ()) { numAgents += agentType.getCount ();} final int increment = 10000;GlobalState.reset ();GlobalState.agents = new AObjectCatalog ("agents",numAgents,increment);// Create the central belief base GlobalState.beliefbase = new ABeliefStore (numAgents,config.getNumThreads ());long t0;// Create the agents t0 = System.currentTimeMillis ();for (Config.AgentTypeData agentType:config.getAgents ()) { if (!ProgramLoader.loadAgent (agentType.getClassname (),agentType.getCount (),GlobalState.agents)) { // return unsuccessful return false;} } long t1 = System.currentTimeMillis ();logger.info ("Created " + GlobalState.agents.size () + agentsIn + Log.formattedDuration (t0,t1));// Initialise the thread pools Program.initIntentionSelectionPools (numAgents,config.getNumThreads ());// Redirect the agent program output if specified if (config.getProgramOutputFile () != null) { try { writer = new PrintStream (config.getProgramOutputFile (),"UTF-8");} catch (FileNotFoundException | UnsupportedEncodingException e) { logger.error ("Could not open program outout file " + config.getProgramOutputFile (),e);} } else { writer = System.out;} // Initialise the intention selection threads Program.initIntentionSelectionThreads (config);// return success return true;}

originalComment: Termiantes the Jill engine.
codeComment: The `finish` method is responsible for terminating various components of a system in a controlled manner. It first calls the `finish` method on each extension in the `GlobalState.eventHandlers` list. Then, it shuts down the intention selection threads using `Program.shutdownIntentionSelectionThreads()`. Next, it iterates over all agents in the `GlobalState.agents` list, calling the `finish` method on each agent. Finally, if a writer is not null, it closes the writer. The method logs the number of agents terminated along with the duration of the termination process.
codeFunctions: public static void finish () { // Terminate the extensions first for (JillExtension extension:GlobalState.eventHandlers) { extension.finish ();} // Now shut down the threads Program.shutdownIntentionSelectionThreads ();// Finish the agents long t0 = System.currentTimeMillis ();for (int i = 0;i < GlobalState.agents.size ();i ++) { // Get the agent Agent agent = (Agent) GlobalState.agents.get (i);// Terminate the agent agent.finish ();} // Close the writer if (writer != null) { writer.close ();} long t1 = System.currentTimeMillis ();logger.info ("Terminated " + GlobalState.agents.size () + agentsIn + Log.formattedDuration (t0,t1));}

codeComment: This method checks if all pools are idle. It initializes a boolean variable `idle` to `true`. The `idle` variable is updated using the logical AND operator (`&=`) to ensure that it remains `true` only if all pools are idle. Finally, the method returns the value of `idle`.
codeFunctions: public static boolean arePoolsIdle () { boolean idle = true;for (int i = 0;i < npools;i ++) { idle &= (intentionSelectors [ i ] == null) || intentionSelectors [ i ].isIdle ();} return idle;}

originalComment: Create a new join or find an existing join on the specified attribute.
codeComment: The `join` method is designed to create a path expression for a given attribute in a JPA query. It takes two parameters: `attribute`, a string representing the attribute path, and `from`, a `From` object representing the starting point of the query. The method splits the attribute string by dots to handle nested properties. If the attribute has multiple parts, it recursively joins the properties and retrieves the final path. If the attribute is a single part, it directly retrieves the path from the `from` object. If an `IllegalArgumentException` occurs during this process, it wraps the exception with a `SeedException` and includes the attribute in the error message.
codeFunctions: public static Expression <?> join (String attribute,From <?,?> from) { Expression <?> path;try { String [ ] properties = attribute.split ("\\.");if (properties.length > 1) { path = joinRecursively (properties,findOrCreateJoin (properties [ 0 ],from),1).get (properties [ properties.length - 1 ]);} else { path = from.get (properties [ 0 ]);} } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) { throw SeedException.wrap (e,JpaErrorCode.UNABLE_TO_CREATE_JPA_JOIN_FOR_SPECIFICATION).put ("property",attribute);} return path;}

originalComment: Join recursively using the split property path.
codeComment: The `joinRecursively` method is a recursive function that takes an array of properties, a `Join` object, and an index as parameters. It iteratively constructs a join operation by calling itself with the next property and the updated join object until it reaches the last property in the array. The method returns the final join object after all properties have been processed.
codeFunctions: private static Join <?,?> joinRecursively (String [ ] properties,Join <?,?> join,int index) { if (index < properties.length - 1) { return joinRecursively (properties,findOrCreateJoin (properties [ index ],join),index + 1);} else { return join;} }

originalComment: Find an existing join for the property or create a new join.
codeComment: The method `findOrCreateJoin` searches for an existing join in the given `from` object that matches the specified `property`. If such a join is found, it returns the existing join. If no matching join is found, it creates a new join for the specified property and returns it.
codeFunctions: private static Join <?,?> findOrCreateJoin (String property,From <?,?> from) { for (Join <?,?> rootJoin:from.getJoins ()) { if (rootJoin.getAttribute ().getName ().equals (property)) { return rootJoin;} } return from.join (property);}
