codeComment: The `convert` method is designed to convert a `MultiTypeData` object to a specified class type. It checks the `typeFlags` of the `MultiTypeData` object to determine the type of data it contains and then compares it with the target class. If the types match, it returns the corresponding value from the `MultiTypeData` object. If no match is found, it throws a `ClassCastException`. The method supports conversions for boolean, int, char, byte, short, long, float, double, string, and object types.
codeFunctions: public static Object convert (MultiTypeData d,Class c) { // Check if it is an boolean convertion. if (((d.typeFlags & BOOLEAN) != 0) && (Boolean.TYPE.equals (c) || Boolean.class.equals (c))) { return d.booleanValue;} // Check if it is an int convertion. else if (((d.typeFlags & INT) != 0) && (Integer.TYPE.equals (c) || Integer.class.equals (c))) { return d.intValue;} // Check if it is an char convertion. else if (((d.typeFlags & CHAR) != 0) && (Character.TYPE.equals (c) || Character.class.equals (c))) { return d.charValue;} // Check if it is an byte convertion. else if (((d.typeFlags & BYTE) != 0) && (Byte.TYPE.equals (c) || Byte.class.equals (c))) { return d.byteValue;} // Check if it is an short convertion. else if (((d.typeFlags & SHORT) != 0) && (Short.TYPE.equals (c) || Short.class.equals (c))) { return d.shortValue;} // Check if it is an long convertion. else if (((d.typeFlags & LONG) != 0) && (Long.TYPE.equals (c) || Long.class.equals (c))) { return d.longValue;} // Check if it is an float convertion. else if (((d.typeFlags & FLOAT) != 0) && (Float.TYPE.equals (c) || Float.class.equals (c))) { return d.floatValue;} // Check if it is an double convertion. else if (((d.typeFlags & DOUBLE) != 0) && (Double.TYPE.equals (c) || Double.class.equals (c))) { return d.doubleValue;} // Check if it is a string convertion. else if (((d.typeFlags & STRING) != 0) && String.class.equals (c)) { return d.stringValue;} // Check if it is an object convertion and th object types match. else if (((d.typeFlags & OBJECT) != 0) && d.objectValue.getClass ().equals (c)) { return d.objectValue;} // Throw a class cast exception if the multi data type cannot be converted to the specified class. else { throw new ClassCastException ("The multi data type, " + d + ", cannot be converted to the class, " + c + ".");} }

originalComment: Clears entries up to and including the specified key from the map.This is a simple garbage collection operation to clear consumed data from the circular buffer.
codeComment: The `clearUpTo` method clears entries in a data array up to a specified key. If the key is within the range defined by `start` and `end - 1`, it iterates from `start` to the key, setting entries to `null` and decrementing the count. It then updates `start` to the next non-null entry or the end of the array. If the key is outside this range, it clears all entries from `start` to `end` and updates `start` accordingly.
codeFunctions: public void clearUpTo (int key) { if (((start <= key) && (key < (end - 1)))) { // Loop from the start of the data, up to the key to clear up to, clearing all data encountered in-between. int newStart;for (newStart = start;(newStart <= end) && (newStart <= key);newStart ++) { int offset = offset (newStart);if (data [ offset ] != null) { data [ offset ] = null;count --;} } // Continue on after the clear up to point, until the first non-null entry or end of array is encountered, // and make that the new start. for (;newStart <= end;newStart ++) { if (data [ offset (newStart) ] != null) { break;} } start = newStart;} else { // The key does not lie between the start and end markers, so clear the entire map up to the end int newStart;for (newStart = start;(newStart <= end);newStart ++) { int offset = offset (newStart);if (data [ offset ] != null) { data [ offset ] = null;count --;} } start = newStart;offset = - start;} }

originalComment: Expands the size of the storage to whichever is the larger of 1.5 times the old size or an array large enough to hold the proposed key that caused the expansion copying the old data into a new array.
codeComment: The `expand` method is designed to increase the size of an array when more space is needed to accommodate a new key. It calculates the new size as the larger of 1.5 times the current size or the space required for the new key. The method then creates a new array of the calculated size, copies the existing data from the old array to the new array, and updates the array reference and other relevant variables.
codeFunctions: private void expand (int key) { // Set the new size to whichever is the larger of 1.5 times the old size, or an array large enough to hold // the proposed key that caused the expansion. int newFactorSize = ((length * 3) / 2) + 1;int newSpaceSize = spaceRequired (key);int newSize = (newSpaceSize > newFactorSize)?newSpaceSize:newFactorSize;Object [ ] oldData = data;data = new Object [ newSize ];// The valid data in the old array runs from offset(start) to offset(end) when offset(start) < offset(end), and // from offset(start) to length - 1 and 0 to offset(end) when offset(start) >= offset(end). int offsetStart = offset (start);int offsetEnd = offset (end);if (offsetStart < offsetEnd) { System.arraycopy (oldData,offsetStart,data,0,end - start);} else { System.arraycopy (oldData,offsetStart,data,0,length - offsetStart);System.arraycopy (oldData,0,data,length - offsetStart,offsetEnd);} offset = - start;length = newSize;}

originalComment: Parses a flat list of terms which are literals variables functors or operators into a tree in such a way that the operators associativity and precendence is obeyed.
codeComment: The `parseOperators` method is designed to parse a sequence of terms into a functor, handling operators and terms according to a predefined state machine. It initializes the parser's state and iterates through the input terms. For each term, it determines whether the term is an operator or a regular term, or if it has reached the end of the terms. It then looks up the appropriate action in an action table based on the current state and the type of the next symbol (operator, term, or final). The action is applied, which modifies the parser's state and output stack. Finally, it returns the parsed functor from the output stack.
codeFunctions: public Term parseOperators (Term [ ] terms) throws SourceCodeException { // Initialize the parsers state. stack.offer (0);state = 0;position = 0;nextTerm = null;// Consume the terms from left to right. for (position = 0;position <= terms.length;) { Symbol nextSymbol;// Decide what the next symbol to parse is; candidate op, term or final. if (position < terms.length) { nextTerm = terms [ position ];if (nextTerm instanceof CandidateOpSymbol) { nextSymbol = Symbol.Op;} else { nextSymbol = Symbol.Term;} } else { nextSymbol = Symbol.Final;} // Look in the action table to find the action associated with the current symbol and state. Action action = actionTable [ state ] [ nextSymbol.ordinal () ];// Apply the action. action.apply ();} return (Functor) outputStack.poll ();}

originalComment: Checks if a candidate operator symbol can have one of the specified fixities and resolve it to an oeprator with that fixity if so.If it cannot be resolved an exception is raised.
codeComment: This method, `checkAndResolveToFixity`, takes a `CandidateOpSymbol` and a variable number of `OpSymbol.Fixity` values as input. It iterates through the provided fixities to find a matching operator in the candidate's possible operators. If a match is found, it returns the corresponding `OpSymbol`. If no match is found, it throws a `SourceCodeException` indicating that the operator must be one of the specified fixities but does not have the required form.
codeFunctions: protected static OpSymbol checkAndResolveToFixity (CandidateOpSymbol candidate,OpSymbol.Fixity ... fixities) throws SourceCodeException { OpSymbol result = null;for (OpSymbol.Fixity fixity:fixities) { result = candidate.getPossibleOperators ().get (fixity);if (result != null) { break;} } if (result == null) { throw new SourceCodeException ("Operator " + candidate + " must be one of " + Arrays.toString (fixities) + ", but does not have the required form.",null,null,null,candidate.getSourceCodePosition ());} return result;}

originalComment: Makes a new node of the same type as this one from a Successor state.
codeComment: The `makeNode` method creates a new search node based on a given successor. It initializes the new node with the successor's state, the current node as its parent, the operator applied, an incremented depth, and an updated path cost. If a repeated state filter is present, it is also set for the new node. The method handles exceptions related to instantiation and illegal access, rethrowing them as `IllegalStateException`.
codeFunctions: public SearchNode < O,T > makeNode (Successor successor) throws SearchNotExhaustiveException { SearchNode newNode;try { // Create a new instance of this class newNode = getClass ().newInstance ();// Set the state, operation, parent, depth and cost for the new search node newNode.state = successor.getState ();newNode.parent = this;newNode.appliedOp = successor.getOperator ();newNode.depth = depth + 1;newNode.pathCost = pathCost + successor.getCost ();// Check if there is a repeated state filter and copy the reference to it into the new node if so if (repeatedStateFilter != null) { newNode.setRepeatedStateFilter (repeatedStateFilter);} return newNode;} catch (InstantiationException e) { // In practice this should never happen but may if the nodes if some class loader error were to occur whilst // using a custom node implementation. Rethrow this as a RuntimeException. throw new IllegalStateException ("InstantiationException during creation of new search node.",e);} catch (IllegalAccessException e) { // In practice this should never happen but may if the nodes to use are not public whilst using a custom node // implementation. Rethrow this as a RuntimeException. throw new IllegalStateException ("IllegalAccessException during creation of new search node.",e);} }

originalComment: Right pads a string with a given string to a given size.This method will repeat the padder string as many times as is necessary until the exact specified size is reached.If the specified size is less than the size of the original string then the original string is returned unchanged.
codeComment: The `rightPad` method pads a given string (`stringToPad`) with a specified padding character(s) (`padder`) until the resulting string reaches a specified size (`size`). If the padding string is empty, the original string is returned unchanged. The method uses a `StringBuffer` to build the padded string and a `CharacterIterator` to iterate over the padding characters, appending them to the `StringBuffer` until the desired length is reached.
codeFunctions: public static String rightPad (String stringToPad,String padder,int size) { if (padder.length () == 0) { return stringToPad;} StringBuffer strb = new StringBuffer (stringToPad);CharacterIterator sci = new StringCharacterIterator (padder);while (strb.length () < size) { for (char ch = sci.first ();ch != CharacterIterator.DONE;ch = sci.next ()) { if (strb.length () < size) { strb.append (String.valueOf (ch));} } } return strb.toString ();}

codeFunctions: public String getOptionsInForce () { // Check if there are no properties to report and return and empty string if so. if (parsedProperties == null) { return "";} // List all the properties. String result = "Options in force:\n";for (Map.Entry < Object,Object > property:parsedProperties.entrySet ()) { result += property.getKey () + " = " + property.getValue () + "\n";} return result;}

originalComment: Generates a usage string consisting of the name of each option and each options argument description and comment.
codeComment: The `getUsage` method constructs a formatted string that lists command line options and their descriptions. It calculates the maximum width for the options and arguments to align them properly. Then, it iterates through a map of `CommandLineOption` objects, formatting each option and its argument with spaces to match the calculated widths, and appends a comment. The result is a neatly aligned usage string that includes all options, their arguments, and descriptions.
codeFunctions: public String getUsage () { String result = "Options:\n";int optionWidth = 0;int argumentWidth = 0;// Calculate the column widths required for aligned layout. for (CommandLineOption optionInfo:optionMap.values ()) { int oWidth = optionInfo.option.length ();int aWidth = (optionInfo.argument != null)?(optionInfo.argument.length ()):0;optionWidth = (oWidth > optionWidth)?oWidth:optionWidth;argumentWidth = (aWidth > argumentWidth)?aWidth:argumentWidth;} // Print usage on each of the command line options. for (CommandLineOption optionInfo:optionMap.values ()) { String argString = ((optionInfo.argument != null)?(optionInfo.argument):"");String optionString = optionInfo.option;argString = rightPad (argString," ",argumentWidth);optionString = rightPad (optionString," ",optionWidth);result += "-" + optionString + " " + argString + " " + optionInfo.comment + "\n";} return result;}

If `trailingProperties` is not null, it iterates over each key in `trailingProperties`, retrieves the corresponding value, and sets this key-value pair in the provided `properties` object.
codeFunctions: public void addTrailingPairsToProperties (Properties properties) { if (trailingProperties != null) { for (Object propKey:trailingProperties.keySet ()) { String name = (String) propKey;String value = trailingProperties.getProperty (name);properties.setProperty (name,value);} } }

codeFunctions: public void addOptionsToProperties (Properties properties) { if (parsedProperties != null) { for (Object propKey:parsedProperties.keySet ()) { String name = (String) propKey;String value = parsedProperties.getProperty (name);// This filters out all trailing items. if (!name.matches ("^[0-9]+$")) { properties.setProperty (name,value);} } } }

It takes several parameters including the option name, comment, argument, whether the option is mandatory, and a format regular expression. The method first checks if the option expects arguments by verifying if the argument is not null or empty. It then creates a new `CommandLineOption` object with the provided parameters and adds it to the `optionMap`.
codeFunctions: protected void addOption (String option,String comment,String argument,boolean mandatory,String formatRegexp) { // Check if usage text has been set in which case this option is expecting arguments. boolean expectsArgs = (!((argument == null) || "".equals (argument)));// Add the option to the map of command line options. CommandLineOption opt = new CommandLineOption (option,expectsArgs,comment,argument,mandatory,formatRegexp);optionMap.put (option,opt);}

originalComment: Converts the free arguments into property declarations.After parsing the command line the free arguments are numbered from 1 such that the parsed properties contain values for the keys 1 2 ... This method converts any free arguments declared using the name = value syntax into properties with key name value value.
codeComment: The method `takeFreeArgsAsProperties` takes a `Properties` object and an integer `from` as input. It iterates over the properties starting from the index specified by `from`, extracting key-value pairs from the properties where the keys are integers starting from `from`. It stops when it encounters a null value, indicating the end of the free arguments. Each key-value pair is split on the `=` character, and any leading or trailing whitespace is removed before setting the property in a new `Properties` object, which is then returned.
codeFunctions: private Properties takeFreeArgsAsProperties (Properties properties,int from) { Properties result = new Properties ();for (int i = from;true;i ++) { String nextFreeArg = properties.getProperty (Integer.toString (i));// Terminate the loop once all free arguments have been consumed. if (nextFreeArg == null) { break;} // Split it on the =, strip any whitespace and set it as a system property. String [ ] nameValuePair = nextFreeArg.split ("=");if (nameValuePair.length == 2) { result.setProperty (nameValuePair [ 0 ],nameValuePair [ 1 ]);} } return result;}

originalComment: Checks the format of an argument to an option against its specified regular expression format if one has been set.Any errors are added to the list of parsing errors.
codeComment: This method, `checkArgumentFormat`, verifies if a command-line option's argument matches a specified format. It takes two parameters: `optionInfo`, which contains information about the command-line option, and `matchedArg`, the argument to be validated. If the option specifies a format using a regular expression (`argumentFormatRegexp`), the method compiles this pattern and checks if the argument matches it. If the argument does not conform to the required format, an error message is added to the `parsingErrors` list.
codeFunctions: private void checkArgumentFormat (CommandLineOption optionInfo,CharSequence matchedArg) { // Check if this option enforces a format for its argument. if (optionInfo.argumentFormatRegexp != null) { Pattern pattern = Pattern.compile (optionInfo.argumentFormatRegexp);Matcher argumentMatcher = pattern.matcher (matchedArg);// Check if the argument does not meet its required format. if (!argumentMatcher.matches ()) { // Create an error for this badly formed argument. parsingErrors.add ("The argument to option " + optionInfo.option + " does not meet its required format.\n");} } }

originalComment: Walks down two iterators comparing them element by element using the equals method.
codeComment: This method, `compareIterators`, takes two iterators and a mapping function as input. It compares the elements of the first iterator, after applying the mapping function, with the elements of the second iterator. If any elements do not match, it appends an error message indicating the expected and actual values. The method returns the accumulated error message.
codeFunctions: public static < T,U > String compareIterators (Iterator < U > iterator,Iterator < T > expectedIterator,Function < U,T > mapping) { String errorMessage = "";while (iterator.hasNext ()) { U next = iterator.next ();T nextMapped = mapping.apply (next);T nextExpected = expectedIterator.next ();if (!nextMapped.equals (nextExpected)) { errorMessage += "Expecting " + nextExpected + " but got " + nextMapped;} } return errorMessage;}

originalComment: Returns an enumeration describing the available options.
codeComment:
This method, `listOptions`, generates a list of configuration options for a text processing system. It returns an `Enumeration` of `Option` objects, each representing a different configuration parameter. The options include:

1. **Stemmer Algorithm Type**: Allows selection of a stemmer algorithm from a predefined list of options. The default value is set to "ORENGO".
2. **Named Entities to Ignore**: Specifies a file containing named entities to be ignored during processing. The file format is a simple text file with one entity per line. This option is optional.
3. **Stopwords File**: Specifies a file containing stopwords to be ignored during processing. The file format is a simple text file with one stopword per line. This option is also optional.
4. **Cache Size**: Sets the size of the cache used by the system. A value of 0 disables the cache. The default cache size is 1000.

Each option is represented by an `Option` object, which includes a description, a short name, a default value, and a command-line option format. The method iterates over a list of predefined stemmer tags to generate the description for the stemmer algorithm type option.

public Enumeration listOptions () { Vector < Option > result;String desc;SelectedTag tag;int i;result = new Vector < Option > ();desc = "";for (i = 0;i < TAGS_STEMMERS.length;i ++) { tag = new SelectedTag (TAGS_STEMMERS [ i ].getID (),TAGS_STEMMERS);desc += "	" + tag.getSelectedTag ().getIDStr () + " = " + tag.getSelectedTag ().getReadable () + "
";} result.addElement (new Option ("	The type of stemmer algorithm to use:
" + desc + "	(default: " + new SelectedTag (STEMMER_ORENGO,TAGS_STEMMERS) + ")","S",1,"-S " + Tag.toOptionList (TAGS_STEMMERS)));result.addElement (new Option ("	The file with the named entities to ignore (optional).
" + "	File format: simple text file with one entity per line.
" + "	(default: none)
","N",1,"-N <file>"));result.addElement (new Option ("	The file with the stopwords (optional).
" + "	File format: simple text file with one stopword per line.
" + "	(default: none)
","W",1,"-W <file>"));result.addElement (new Option ("	The size of the cache. Disable with 0.
" + "	(default: 1000)
","C",1,"-C <int>"));return result.elements ();}

originalComment: Returns the stemmer to use.
codeComment:
This method, `getActualStemmer`, is responsible for initializing and returning a stemmer object based on the specified stemmer type. It first checks if the `m_ActualStemmer` is null. If it is, the method determines which stemmer algorithm to use based on the value of `m_Stemmer`. It then creates an instance of the appropriate stemmer class (`OrengoStemmer`, `PorterStemmer`, or `SavoyStemmer`). If an unhandled stemmer type is encountered, it throws an `IllegalStateException`.

After initializing the stemmer, the method configures it to ignore named entities and stopwords if the respective directories are not provided. It also sets up caching based on the value of `m_Cache`. Finally, the method returns the initialized stemmer object.
codeFunctions: protected synchronized ptstemmer.Stemmer getActualStemmer () throws PTStemmerException { if (m_ActualStemmer == null) { // stemmer algorithm if (m_Stemmer == STEMMER_ORENGO) m_ActualStemmer = new OrengoStemmer ();else if (m_Stemmer == STEMMER_PORTER) m_ActualStemmer = new PorterStemmer ();else if (m_Stemmer == STEMMER_SAVOY) m_ActualStemmer = new SavoyStemmer ();else throw new IllegalStateException ("Unhandled stemmer type: " + m_Stemmer);// named entities if (!m_NamedEntities.isDirectory ()) m_ActualStemmer.ignore (PTStemmerUtilities.fileToSet (m_NamedEntities.getAbsolutePath ()));// stopwords if (!m_Stopwords.isDirectory ()) m_ActualStemmer.ignore (PTStemmerUtilities.fileToSet (m_Stopwords.getAbsolutePath ()));// cache if (m_Cache > 0) m_ActualStemmer.enableCaching (m_Cache);else m_ActualStemmer.disableCaching ();} return m_ActualStemmer;}

originalComment: Creates a new float range type with the specified name if it does not already exist.
codeComment: This method, `createInstance`, creates a new instance of a `FloatRangeType` with a specified name and range defined by `min` and `max` values. It ensures that `min` is less than or equal to `max`, throwing an `IllegalArgumentException` if not. The method also checks if a type with the same name already exists, and if so, it either reuses the existing type if the definitions are identical or throws an exception if they differ. The method is synchronized to ensure thread safety when accessing and modifying the shared `FLOAT_RANGE_TYPES` map.
codeFunctions: public static Type createInstance (String name,float min,float max) { // Ensure that min is less than or equal to max. if (min > max) { throw new IllegalArgumentException ("'min' must be less than or equal to 'max'.");} synchronized (FLOAT_RANGE_TYPES) { // Add the newly created type to the map of all types. FloatRangeType newType = new FloatRangeType (name,min,max);// Ensure that the named type does not already exist, unless it has an identical definition already, in which // case the old definition can be re-used and the new one discarded. FloatRangeType oldType = FLOAT_RANGE_TYPES.get (name);if ((oldType != null) &&!oldType.equals (newType)) { throw new IllegalArgumentException ("The type '" + name + "' already exists and cannot be redefined.");} else if ((oldType != null) && oldType.equals (newType)) { return oldType;} else { FLOAT_RANGE_TYPES.put (name,newType);return newType;} } }

originalComment: Resets the machine to its initial state.This clears any programs from the machine and clears all of its stacks and heaps.
codeComment: The `reset` method initializes and resets various components of a machine, including memory areas, registers, and pointers. It allocates direct buffers for data and code, sets up heap, stack, and trail pointers, and initializes other machine states such as the instruction pointer, write mode, and suspension status. It also resets the call table and sets internal function addresses. Finally, it notifies any attached debug monitor of the reset event.

codeFunctions: private static int ceilingLog2 (int n) { int oa;int i;int b;oa = n;b = 32 / 2;i = 0;while (b != 0) { i = (i << 1);if (n >= (1 << b)) { n /= (1 << b);i = i | 1;} else { n &= (1 << b) - 1;} b /= 2;} if ((1 << i) == oa) { return i;} else { return i + 1;} }

originalComment: Captures the fields of the associated object.
codeComment:
The `capture` method is designed to extract property values from an object by invoking its public getter methods. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Class Retrieval**: The method starts by obtaining the class of the object (`ob`) for which a memento is being created.

2. **Method Iteration**: It retrieves all public methods of the class, including those from super-interfaces and super-classes.

3. **Getter Method Identification**: For each method, it checks if the method is a valid getter method:
   - The method name starts with "get".
   - The method name has at least four characters.
   - The fourth character is an uppercase letter.
   - The method is public.
   - The method takes no arguments.

4. **Property Name Extraction**: If a method is identified as a getter, the property name is derived by converting the fourth character to lowercase and appending the rest of the method name.

5. **Property Value Extraction**: The method invokes the getter to extract the property value. If `ignoreNull` is false or the value is not null, the property value is stored in a map (`values`).

6. **Exception Handling**: The method handles `IllegalAccessException` and `InvocationTargetException` by throwing an `IllegalStateException`.

7. **Setter Method Check**: The method includes a comment suggesting that it should also check for setter methods, but this functionality is not implemented in the provided code.
codeFunctions: private void capture (boolean ignoreNull) { // Get the class of the object to build a memento for. Class cls = ob.getClass ();// Iterate through all the public methods of the class including all super-interfaces and super-classes. Method [ ] methods = cls.getMethods ();for (Method nextMethod:methods) { // Get the next method. /*log.fine("nextMethod = " + nextMethod.getName());*/ // Check if the method is a 'getter' method, is public and takes no arguments. String methodName = nextMethod.getName ();if (methodName.startsWith ("get") && (methodName.length () >= 4) && Character.isUpperCase (methodName.charAt (3)) && Modifier.isPublic (nextMethod.getModifiers ()) && (nextMethod.getParameterTypes ().length == 0)) { String propName = Character.toLowerCase (methodName.charAt (3)) + methodName.substring (4);/*log.fine(methodName + " is a valid getter method for the property " + propName + ".");*/ try { // Call the 'getter' method to extract the properties value. Object [ ] params = new Object [ ] { };Object value = nextMethod.invoke (ob,params);/*log.fine("The result of calling the getter method is: " + value);*/ // Store the property value for the object. if (!ignoreNull || (value != null)) { values.put (propName,value);} } catch (IllegalAccessException e) { /*log.log(java.util.logging.Level.FINE, "IllegalAccessException during call to getter method.", e);*/ throw new IllegalStateException (e);} catch (InvocationTargetException e) { /*log.log(java.util.logging.Level.FINE, "InvocationTargetException during call to getter method.", e);*/ throw new IllegalStateException (e);} } // Should also check if the method is a 'setter' method, is public and takes exactly one argument. } }

codeComment: The method `isVoidVariable` checks if a given `WAMInstruction` involves a variable that is a singleton, appears only in non-argument positions, and is not permanently allocated. It retrieves the `SymbolKey` from the instruction, then fetches related information from the `symbolTable` such as occurrence count, non-argument position status, and allocation details. Based on these attributes, it determines if the variable qualifies as a "void" variable according to the specified conditions.
codeFunctions: private boolean isVoidVariable (WAMInstruction instruction) { SymbolKey symbolKey = instruction.getSymbolKeyReg1 ();if (symbolKey != null) { Integer count = (Integer) symbolTable.get (symbolKey,SymbolTableKeys.SYMKEY_VAR_OCCURRENCE_COUNT);Boolean nonArgPositionOnly = (Boolean) symbolTable.get (symbolKey,SymbolTableKeys.SYMKEY_VAR_NON_ARG);Integer allocation = (Integer) symbolTable.get (symbolKey,SymbolTableKeys.SYMKEY_ALLOCATION);boolean singleton = (count != null) && count.equals (1);boolean nonArgPosition = (nonArgPositionOnly != null) && TRUE.equals (nonArgPositionOnly);boolean permanent = (allocation != null) && ((byte) ((allocation & 0xff00) >> 8) == WAMInstruction.STACK_ADDR);if (singleton && nonArgPosition &&!permanent) { return true;} } return false;}

originalComment: Provides an iterator over the child terms if there are any.Only functors and clauses are compound and build across a list of child arguments.
codeComment: This method, `getChildren`, retrieves an iterator for the children of a logical structure, which can be traversed in either forward or reverse order. It first checks if a `traverser` object is available and if it is an instance of `ClauseTraverser`. If so, it uses the `traverser` to traverse the structure and return an iterator. If not, it manually constructs a list of children using either a `LinkedList` or a `StackQueue` based on the `reverse` flag. The method then adds the `head` and all elements from the `body` to this list and returns an iterator for the list.
codeFunctions: public Iterator < Operator < Term > > getChildren (boolean reverse) { if ((traverser != null) && (traverser instanceof ClauseTraverser)) { return ((ClauseTraverser) traverser).traverse (this,reverse);} else { LinkedList < Operator < Term >> resultList = null;if (!reverse) { resultList = new LinkedList < Operator < Term > > ();} else { resultList = new StackQueue < Operator < Term > > ();} if (head != null) { resultList.add (head);} if (body != null) { for (Term bodyTerm:body) { resultList.add (bodyTerm);} } return resultList.iterator ();} }

codeComment: This method, `getChildren`, returns an iterator over the children of a node in a tree-like structure. The method takes a boolean parameter `reverse` which determines the order of iteration. If a `FunctorTraverser` is available, it uses it to traverse the node. Otherwise, it directly iterates over the `arguments` array. If `reverse` is `false`, it iterates in the original order; if `true`, it iterates in reverse order. codeFunctions: public Iterator < Operator < Term > > getChildren (boolean reverse) { if ((traverser != null) && (traverser instanceof FunctorTraverser)) { return ((FunctorTraverser) traverser).traverse (this,reverse);} else { if (arguments == null) { return new LinkedList < Operator < Term > > ().iterator ();} else if (!reverse) { return Arrays.asList ((Operator < Term > [ ]) arguments).iterator ();} else { List < Operator < Term >> argList = new LinkedList < Operator < Term > > ();for (int i = arity - 1;i >= 0;i --) { argList.add (arguments [ i ]);} return argList.iterator ();} } }

codeComment:
The `executeQuery` method is a generic method that takes a `SqlQueryBuilder` object as input and returns a list of objects of type `T` that extends `MeasureAppender`. The method performs the following steps:

1. **Builds the SQL Query**: It calls the `buildQuery` method on the `sqlQueryBuilder` to construct the SQL query.
2. **Retrieves the Query String**: It retrieves the constructed SQL query string using the `getQueryString` method.
3. **Logs the Query**: It logs the query string at the debug level.
4. **Executes the Query**: It records the start time, then executes the SQL query using the `jdbcTemplate.query` method, passing the query string, parameter source, and the `sqlQueryBuilder` itself.
5. **Logs Execution Time**: If logging at the info level is enabled, it logs the time taken to execute the query.
6. **Logs Parameters**: If logging at the debug level is enabled, it logs the parameters used in the query.
7. **Returns the Result**: Finally, it returns the list of results obtained from the query execution.
codeFunctions: private < T extends MeasureAppender > List < T > executeQuery (final SqlQueryBuilder < T > sqlQueryBuilder) throws NovieRuntimeException { sqlQueryBuilder.buildQuery ();final String queryString = sqlQueryBuilder.getQueryString ();LOG.debug (queryString);long beforeQuery = System.currentTimeMillis ();List < T > returnValue = jdbcTemplate.query (queryString,sqlQueryBuilder.getMapSqlParameterSource (),sqlQueryBuilder);if (LOG.isInfoEnabled ()) { LOG.info ("SQL query successfully ran in " + (System.currentTimeMillis () - beforeQuery) + "ms.");} if (LOG.isDebugEnabled ()) { StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder ();for (Entry < String,Object > e:sqlQueryBuilder.getMapSqlParameterSource ().getValues ().entrySet ()) { if (sb.length () > 0) { sb.append (",");} sb.append (e.getKey ());sb.append ("=");sb.append (e.getValue ());} sb.insert (0,"Parameters [");sb.append ("]");LOG.debug (sb.toString ());} return returnValue;}

originalComment: A dedicated thread loop for reading the stream and sending incoming packets to the appropriate router.
codeComment:
The `run` method attempts to execute the `readStream` method. It handles several exceptions:

1. **EOFException**: Catches end-of-file exceptions, indicating a normal disconnection.
2. **SocketException**: Catches socket exceptions. If the component is not shutting down, it logs the error and attempts to re-establish the connection.
3. **XmlPullParserException**: Catches XML parsing exceptions and logs the error.
4. **Exception**: Catches any other exceptions and logs them as warnings.
codeFunctions: public void run () { try { readStream ();} catch (EOFException eof) { // Normal disconnect } catch (SocketException se) { // Do nothing if the exception occured while shutting down the // component otherwise // log the error and try to establish a new connection if (!shutdown) { component.getManager ().getLog ().error (se);component.connectionLost ();} } catch (XmlPullParserException ie) { component.getManager ().getLog ().error (ie);} catch (Exception e) { component.getManager ().getLog ().warn (e);} }

originalComment: Read the incoming stream until it ends.
codeComment: The `readStream` method continuously reads packets from a stream until a shutdown signal is received. It parses XML documents to identify different types of packets (message, presence, or IQ) and creates corresponding packet objects. These packets are then processed by a component. If an unknown packet type is encountered, an `XmlPullParserException` is thrown.
codeFunctions: private void readStream () throws Exception { while (!shutdown) { Element doc = reader.parseDocument ().getRootElement ();if (doc == null) { // Stop reading the stream since the server has sent an end of // stream element and // probably closed the connection return;} Packet packet;String tag = doc.getName ();if ("message".equals (tag)) { packet = new Message (doc);} else if ("presence".equals (tag)) { packet = new Presence (doc);} else if ("iq".equals (tag)) { packet = getIQ (doc);} else { throw new XmlPullParserException ("Unknown packet type was read: " + tag);} // Request the component to process the received packet component.processPacket (packet);} }

codeComment: This method generates a unique time value suitable for creating UUIDs (Universally Unique Identifiers). It ensures that the time value is incremented correctly even if multiple UUIDs are generated in the same millisecond. The method uses a counter to track the number of UUIDs generated in the same millisecond and increments the timestamp if the counter exceeds a predefined limit. The final time value is calculated by adding an offset to the current time in milliseconds and converting it to 100-nanosecond ticks, then adding the counter value.
codeFunctions: private static long getUUIDTime () { if (_currentMillis != System.currentTimeMillis ()) { _currentMillis = System.currentTimeMillis ();_counter = 0;// reset counter } // check to see if we have created too many uuid's for this timestamp if (_counter + 1 >= MILLI_MULT) { // Original algorithm threw exception. Seemed like overkill. // Let's just increment the timestamp instead and start over... _currentMillis ++;_counter = 0;} // calculate time as current millis plus offset times 100 ns ticks long currentTime = (_currentMillis + GREG_OFFSET) * MILLI_MULT;// return the uuid time plus the artificial tick counter incremented return currentTime + _counter ++;}

codeComment:

1. **Null Check**: It first checks if the `byteBuffer` is `null`. If it is, the method returns immediately without doing anything.

2. **Direct Buffer Check**: It verifies if the `byteBuffer` is a direct buffer. If not, it throws an `IllegalArgumentException`.

3. **Privileged Action**: It uses `AccessController.doPrivileged` to execute a block of code with elevated privileges. This is necessary because accessing the cleaner method involves reflection, which may require higher permissions.

4. **Reflection to Access Cleaner Method**:
   - It retrieves the `cleaner` method from the `ByteBuffer` class using reflection.
   - It sets the `cleaner` method accessible to bypass Java's access control checks.
   - It invokes the `cleaner` method on the `byteBuffer` to get the cleaner object.

5. **Reflection to Invoke Clean Method**:
   - It retrieves the `clean` method from the cleaner object's class.
   - It sets the `clean` method accessible.
   - It invokes the `clean` method on the cleaner object to clean the buffer.

6. **Exception Handling**: If any reflection-related exceptions occur (such as `NoSuchMethodException`, `SecurityException`, `IllegalAccessException`, `IllegalArgumentException`, or `InvocationTargetException`), it throws a `RuntimeException` indicating that the `MappedByteBuffer` could not be cleaned, which might leave the file locked.

7. **Return Statement**: The method returns `null` as there is nothing to return from the `PrivilegedAction`.

codeComment:
The `putAll` method is designed to add all key-value pairs from a given map `m` to the current map. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Check for Empty Input**: If the input map `m` is empty, the method returns immediately without making any changes.

2. **Determine Capacity Needs**: The method calculates the number of keys to be added (`numKeysToBeAdded`). If this number is greater than the current threshold, it means the map needs to be resized to accommodate the new entries.

3. **Calculate Target Capacity**: The target capacity is calculated based on the number of keys to be added and the load factor. If the calculated capacity exceeds the maximum allowed capacity (`MAXIMUM_CAPACITY`), it is capped at this maximum.

4. **Resize the Map**: If the new capacity is greater than the current table length, the map is resized to the new capacity using the `resize` method.

5. **Add Entries**: The method iterates over the entries of the input map `m` and adds each key-value pair to the current map using the `put` method.

This method ensures that the map is resized appropriately to handle the addition of new entries efficiently.

         * is greater than or equal to threshold.  This is conservative; the
         * obvious condition is (m.size() + size) >= threshold, but this
         * condition could result in a map with twice the appropriate capacity,
         * if the keys to be added overlap with the keys already in this map.
         * By using the conservative calculation, we subject ourself
         * to at most one extra resize.

codeFunctions: private static String xmlAttribEncodeBinary (String value) { StringBuilder s = new StringBuilder ();char buf [ ] = value.toCharArray ();for (char c:buf) { switch (c) { case ' ':s.append ("<");break;case ' ':s.append (">");break;case ' ':s.append ("&");break;case ' ':s.append (""");break;case ' ':s.append ("'");break;default:if (c <= 0x1f || (0x7f <= c && c <= 0x9f)) { // includes \t, \n, // \r s.append ("&#x");s.append (String.format ("%X",(int) c));s.append (' ');} else { s.append (c);} } } return s.toString ();}

The `removeCached` method is designed to remove an entry from a cache and the underlying storage system. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Parameters**: The method takes three parameters: `keySpace`, `columnFamily`, and `key`, which identify the specific entry to be removed.

2. **Cache Handling**:
   - If `sharedCache` is not null, it proceeds to mark the entry as deleted in the cache.
   - It constructs a `cacheKey` using the provided `keySpace`, `columnFamily`, and `key`.
   - It then puts a `CacheHolder` with a null value and the `managerId` into the cache to mark the entry as deleted.

3. **Logging**: It logs a debug message indicating that the entry has been marked as deleted in the cache.

4. **Disposer Registration**:
   - If the `client` implements the `Disposer` interface, it registers a `Disposable` action.
   - This action checks if the `CacheHolder` associated with the `cacheKey` was locked by the current `managerId`.
   - If so, it removes the deleted marker from the cache and logs a debug message.

5. **Storage Removal**: Finally, it calls the `remove` method on the `client` to remove the entry from the underlying storage system.

The `putCached` method is responsible for inserting data into a storage system while managing a shared cache. Here's a summary of its functionality:

1. **Cache Key Generation**: If a shared cache is available, it generates a cache key using the provided `keySpace`, `columnFamily`, and `key`.

2. **Cache Check**: If the cache is available and the data is not probably new, it checks if the item is already in the cache and if it is locked by another manager. If so, it logs a debug message and returns without performing any further operations.

3. **Logging**: It logs a debug message indicating the data being saved.

4. **Data Insertion**: It inserts the data into the storage system using the `client.insert` method, passing the `keySpace`, `columnFamily`, `key`, `encodedProperties`, and `probablyNew` flag.

5. **Cache Management**: If the cache is available, it removes the cache key to ensure that any stale state, including previously deleted objects, is cleared.

This method ensures that data is inserted into the storage system while managing cache state to prevent race conditions and ensure data consistency.

As long as the dwell time // in the cache is longer than the lifetime of an active session // then this will be true. // if the lifetime of an active session is longer (like with a // long running background operation) // then you should expect to see race conditions at this point // since the marker in the cache will have // gone, and the marker in the database has gone, so the put // operation, must be a create operation. // To change this behavior we would need to differentiate more // strongly between new and update and change // probablyNew into certainlyNew, but that would probably break // the BASIC assumption of the whole system. // Update 2011-12-06 related to issue 136 // I am not certain this code is correct. What happens if the // session wants to remove and then add items. // the session will never get past this point, since sitting in // the cache is a null CacheHolder preventing the session // removing then adding. // also, how long should the null cache holder be placed in // there for ? // I think the solution is to bind the null Cache holder to the // instance of the caching manager that created it, // let the null Cache holder last for 10s, and during that time // only the CachingManagerImpl that created it can remove it. } } LOGGER.debug ("Saving {} {} {} {} ",new Object [ ] { keySpace,columnFamily,key,encodedProperties });client.insert (keySpace,columnFamily,key,encodedProperties,probablyNew);if (sharedCache != null) { // if we just added a value in, remove the key so that any stale // state (including a previously deleted object is removed) sharedCache.remove (cacheKey);} }

codeComment:
The `includeJar` method processes a given file to include its contents in a location map. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Check if the file is a directory**: If the file is a directory, the method returns immediately.
2. **Create a JAR URL**: Constructs a JAR URL from the file's canonical path.
3. **Open the JAR file**: Attempts to open the JAR file using the JAR URL. If any `MalformedURLException` or `IOException` occurs, the method returns.
4. **Check if the JAR file is null**: If the JAR file is null, the method returns.
5. **Add the JAR URL to the location map**: Adds the JAR URL to the location map, handling any `URISyntaxException`.
6. **Iterate through JAR entries**: Iterates through each entry in the JAR file.
   - **Skip entries based on package filter**: If a package filter is set and the entry name starts with the filter, the entry is skipped.

codeComment:
This method, `verifyCapabilities`, checks if a given command is supported by a set of capabilities. It takes a `String` command and a `Capabilities` object as parameters. The method uses a `switch` statement to determine which capability to check based on the command. It returns `true` if the command is supported by the capabilities, and `false` otherwise. The supported commands and their corresponding capability checks are as follows:

- `PLAY` and `PAUSE`: Checks if the device has play/pause control.
- `SELECT_TRACK`: Checks if the device can select a track.
- `NEXT` and `PREVIOUS`: Checks if the device supports next/previous track navigation.
- `JUMP`: Checks if the device can jump to a specific track.
- `CHANGE_PLAYBACK`: Checks if the playback mode can be changed.
- `CHANGE_VOLUME`: Checks if the volume can be changed.
- `STOP`: Always returns `true`, indicating that stopping is always supported.
codeFunctions: public static boolean verifyCapabilities (String command,Capabilities capabilities) { switch (command) { case PLAY:return capabilities.hasPlayPauseControl ();case PAUSE:return capabilities.hasPlayPauseControl ();case SELECT_TRACK:return capabilities.isAbleToSelectTrack ();case NEXT:return capabilities.hasNextPrevious ();case PREVIOUS:return capabilities.hasNextPrevious ();case JUMP:return capabilities.isAbleToJump ();case CHANGE_PLAYBACK:return capabilities.isPlaybackChangeable ();case CHANGE_VOLUME:return capabilities.canChangeVolume ();case STOP:return true;} return false;}

If not, it throws an `ExceedMaxAsyncJobsException` or calls the callback with the exception if a callback is provided. If the semaphore allows, it attempts to execute the batch asynchronously using `CqlUtils.executeBatchAsync`. If a callback is provided, it adds a callback to the `ResultSetFuture` using `Futures.addCallback`. If an exception occurs during execution, it releases the semaphore and logs the error.
codeFunctions: public void executeBatchAsync (FutureCallback < ResultSet > callback,Statement ... statements) throws ExceedMaxAsyncJobsException { if (!asyncSemaphore.tryAcquire ()) { if (callback == null) { throw new ExceedMaxAsyncJobsException (maxSyncJobs);} else { callback.onFailure (new ExceedMaxAsyncJobsException (maxSyncJobs));} } else { try { ResultSetFuture rsf = CqlUtils.executeBatchAsync (getSession (),statements);if (callback != null) { Futures.addCallback (rsf,wrapCallbackResultSet (callback),asyncExecutor);} } catch (Exception e) { asyncSemaphore.release ();LOGGER.error (e.getMessage (),e);} } }

codeFunctions: public Set < Class <?> > getSubclasses (Class <?> clazz) { Set < Class <?> > ret = new HashSet < Class <?> > ();Set < Class <?> > w = null;if (clazz != null) { this.clear ();Map < URI,String > locations = this.locator.getCfLocations ();for (Entry < URI,String > entry:locations.entrySet ()) { try { w = search (clazz,entry.getKey (),locations.get (entry.getKey ()));if (w != null && (w.size () > 0)) { ret.addAll (w);} } catch (MalformedURLException ex) { } } } return ret;}

originalComment: Returns all known subclasses for a given class location and package name
codeComment: The method `search` takes three parameters: a `Class<?>` object, a `URI` object, and a `String` representing a package name. It returns a `Set<Class<?>>`. The method first checks if either the `Class<?>` or `URI` is null, returning an empty `HashSet` if so. It then converts the `URI` to a `File` and checks if the file exists. If the file exists, it calls `searchDirectory` to search within the directory; otherwise, it calls `searchJar` to search within a JAR file. The method returns the set of classes found by these methods.
codeFunctions: private final Set < Class <?> > search (Class <?> clazz,URI location,String packageName) throws MalformedURLException { if (clazz == null || location == null) { return new HashSet < Class <?> > ();} File directory = new File (location.toURL ().getFile ());if (directory.exists ()) { return this.searchDirectory (clazz,directory,location,packageName).keySet ();} else { return this.searchJar (clazz,location).keySet ();} }

originalComment: Returns all known subclasses found in a given directory.
codeComment: This method, `searchDirectory`, searches a specified directory for `.class` files, loads the corresponding classes, and checks if they are subclasses of a given class (`clazz`). If they are, it adds them to a map with their URI location. The method returns this map.
codeFunctions: protected final Map < Class <?>,URI > searchDirectory (Class <?> clazz,File directory,URI location,String packageName) { Map < Class <?>,URI > ret = new HashMap <> ();String [ ] files = directory.list ();for (int i = 0;i < files.length;i ++) { if (files [ i ].endsWith (".class")) { String classname = files [ i ].substring (0,files [ i ].length () - 6);try { Class <?> c = Class.forName (packageName + "." + classname);if (clazz.isAssignableFrom (c) &&!clazz.getName ().equals (packageName + "." + classname)) { ret.put (c,location);} } catch (Exception ex) { errors.add (ex);} } } return ret;}

codeComment:
The `searchJar` method searches for classes within a JAR file that are assignable from a specified class. It takes a `Class<?>` object and a `URI` representing the JAR file's location as parameters. The method returns a `Map<Class<?>, URI>` where the keys are the found classes and the values are the URI of the JAR file.

Here's a step-by-step summary of the method:

1. **Initialization**: 
   - A `HashMap` named `ret` is created to store the found classes and their corresponding JAR file URIs.
   - The method attempts to open a connection to the JAR file using the provided URI.

2. **Reading the JAR File**:
   - A `JarURLConnection` is established, and the `JarFile` is retrieved.
   - The method iterates over each entry in the JAR file.

3. **Processing Each Entry**:
   - For each entry, the method checks if it has already been processed. If so, it skips to the next entry.
   - If the entry is not a directory and ends with ".class", it processes the entry as a class file.
   - The class name is extracted from the entry name, cleaned up, and checked against a list of excluded names.

4. **Loading and Checking Classes**:
   - If the class name is not excluded, the method attempts to load the class using `Class.forName`.
   - It checks if the loaded class is assignable from the specified class and not the same as the specified class.
   - If both conditions are met, the class and its JAR file URI are added to the `ret` map.

5. **Error Handling**:
   - Any exceptions or errors encountered during class loading are added to an `errors` list.

6. **Return**:
   - The method returns the `ret` map containing the found classes and their URIs.

This method is useful for dynamically discovering classes within a JAR file that meet certain criteria, such as being subclasses of a specific class.
codeFunctions: protected final Map < Class <?>,URI > searchJar (Class <?> clazz,URI location) { Map < Class <?>,URI > ret = new HashMap <> ();try { JarURLConnection conn = (JarURLConnection) location.toURL ().openConnection ();JarFile jarFile = conn.getJarFile ();for (Enumeration < JarEntry > e = jarFile.entries ();e.hasMoreElements ();) { JarEntry entry = e.nextElement ();String entryname = entry.getName ();if (this.processed.contains (entryname)) { continue;} this.processed.add (entryname);if (!entry.isDirectory () && entryname.endsWith (".class")) { String classname = entryname.substring (0,entryname.length () - 6);if (classname.startsWith ("/")) { classname = classname.substring (1);} classname = classname.replace (' ',' ');if (!StringUtils.startsWithAny (classname,this.excludedNames)) { try { Class <?> c = Class.forName (classname);if (clazz.isAssignableFrom (c) &&!clazz.getName ().equals (classname)) { ret.put (c,location);} } catch (Exception exception) { errors.add (exception);} catch (Error error) { errors.add (error);} } } } } catch (IOException ignore) { errors.add (ignore);} return ret;}

The method returns a sublist of the filtered objects and updates the `RSM` object with relevant metadata such as count, index, first, and last identifiers.
codeFunctions: public static List < Identifiable > filterRSMResponse (List < Identifiable > objects,RSM rsm) throws IllegalArgumentException { String after = rsm.getAfter ();String before = rsm.getBefore ();int initialIndex = rsm.getIndex ();int lastIndex = objects.size ();if (after != null || (before != null &&!before.isEmpty ())) { boolean afterItemFound = false;boolean beforeItemFound = false;int i = 0;for (Identifiable object:objects) { if (after != null && after.equals (object.getId ())) { initialIndex = i + 1;afterItemFound = true;} if (before != null && before.equals (object.getId ())) { lastIndex = i;beforeItemFound = true;} i ++;} if (after != null &&!afterItemFound) { throw new IllegalArgumentException ();} if (before != null &&!before.isEmpty () &&!beforeItemFound) { throw new IllegalArgumentException ();} } if (rsm.getMax () != null) { if (before != null) { initialIndex = lastIndex - rsm.getMax ();} else { lastIndex = initialIndex + rsm.getMax ();} } boolean outOfRange = initialIndex > lastIndex || initialIndex < 0 || lastIndex > objects.size ();List < Identifiable > filteredList = outOfRange?new LinkedList < Identifiable > ():objects.subList (initialIndex,lastIndex);rsm.setCount (objects.size ());rsm.setIndex (initialIndex);if (!filteredList.isEmpty ()) { rsm.setFirst (filteredList.get (0).getId ());rsm.setLast (filteredList.get (filteredList.size () - 1).getId ());} return filteredList;}

originalComment: Reloads the entire roster from the server.This is an asynchronous operation which means the method will return immediately and the roster will be reloaded at a later point when the server responds to the reload request.
codeComment:
The `reload` method performs the following steps:

1. Checks if the user is authenticated. If not, it throws an `IllegalStateException` indicating that the user is not logged in to the server.
2. Checks if the user is anonymous. If so, it throws an `IllegalStateException` indicating that anonymous users cannot have a roster.
3. Creates a new `Roster` object.
4. If `rosterStore` is not null and the connection supports roster versioning, it adds a version attribute to the `query` element of the `Roster` packet using the version from `rosterStore`.
5. Adds a packet listener to the connection to handle the roster result, using a `PacketIDFilter` to filter packets by the ID of the sent packet.
6. Sends the `Roster` packet over the connection.
codeFunctions: public void reload () { if (!connection.isAuthenticated ()) { throw new IllegalStateException ("Not logged in to server.");} if (connection.isAnonymous ()) { throw new IllegalStateException ("Anonymous users can't have a roster.");} Roster packet = new Roster ();if (rosterStore != null && connection.isRosterVersioningSupported ()) { packet.getElement ().element ("query").addAttribute ("ver",rosterStore.getRosterVersion ());PacketFilter filter = new PacketIDFilter (packet.getID ());connection.addPacketListener (new RosterResultListener (),filter);} connection.sendPacket (packet);}

codeComment:
This method, `createEntry`, is responsible for adding a new contact to a user's roster in an XMPP (Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol) system. Here's a summary of the steps it performs:

1. **Authentication Check**: It first checks if the user is authenticated. If not, it throws an `IllegalStateException` indicating that the user is not logged in.

2. **Anonymous User Check**: It checks if the user is anonymous. If so, it throws an `IllegalStateException` because anonymous users cannot have a roster.

3. **Create Roster Packet**: It creates a new `Roster` packet with the type set to `IQ.Type.set`. It then adds a new item to this packet with the user's JID, name, and groups.

4. **Send Roster Packet**: It sends the roster packet to the server and waits for a response using a `PacketCollector`. If no response is received within the specified timeout, it throws an `XMPPException`.

5. **Handle Server Response**: If the server responds with an error, it throws an `XMPPException` with the error details.

6. **Send Presence Subscription**: Finally, it creates and sends a presence subscription packet to the new contact to request their presence updates.

This method ensures that the contact is added to the user's roster and that a subscription request is sent to the new contact.
codeFunctions: public void createEntry (String user,String name,String [ ] groups) throws XMPPException { if (!connection.isAuthenticated ()) { throw new IllegalStateException ("Not logged in to server.");} if (connection.isAnonymous ()) { throw new IllegalStateException ("Anonymous users can't have a roster.");} // Create and send roster entry creation packet. Roster rosterPacket = new Roster ();rosterPacket.setType (IQ.Type.set);rosterPacket.addItem (new JID (user),name,null,null,Arrays.asList (groups));// Wait up to a certain number of seconds for a reply from the server. PacketCollector collector = connection.createPacketCollector (new PacketIDFilter (rosterPacket.getID ()));connection.sendPacket (rosterPacket);IQ response = (IQ) collector.nextResult (SmackConfiguration.getPacketReplyTimeout ());collector.cancel ();if (response == null) { throw new XMPPException ("No response from the server.");} // If the server replied with an error, throw an exception. else if (response.getType () == IQ.Type.error) { throw new XMPPException (response.getError ());} // Create a presence subscription packet and send. Presence presencePacket = new Presence (Presence.Type.subscribe);presencePacket.setTo (user);connection.sendPacket (presencePacket);}

codeComment:
The `initProperties` method initializes properties for an application by performing the following steps:

1. **Construct Properties Path**: It constructs the path to the properties file using the context's files and add-ons information.
2. **Create Properties File**: If the properties file does not exist, it attempts to create a new file. If an error occurs during creation, it logs an error.
3. **Load Properties**: It reads the properties file using a `BufferedReader` and loads them into a `Properties` object. If an error occurs during loading, it logs an error.
4. **Check Default Properties**: If a default properties path is provided and the default properties file exists, it checks if the current properties are empty.
5. **Copy Default Properties**: If the current properties are empty, it copies the default properties file to the current location. If an error occurs during copying, it logs an error.
6. **Write and Reload Properties**: It writes the default properties to the current properties file and reloads the properties if successful. If writing fails, it returns without further action.
codeFunctions: public void initProperties () { propertiesPath = getContext ().getFiles ().getPropertiesLocation () + File.separator + getContext ().getAddOns ().getAddOn ().getID () + ".properties";this.propertiesFile = new File (propertiesPath);if (!this.propertiesFile.exists ()) try { this.propertiesFile.createNewFile ();} catch (IOException e) { error ("Error while trying to create the new Properties file",e);} try { BufferedReader in = new BufferedReader (new InputStreamReader (new FileInputStream (this.propertiesFile),"UTF8"));try { properties.load (in);} catch (IOException e) { error ("unable to load the InputStream for the PropertiesFile",e);} } catch (FileNotFoundException | UnsupportedEncodingException e) { error ("Error while trying to read Properties-File",e);} if (defaultPropertiesPath != null && new File (defaultPropertiesPath).exists ()) { @ SuppressWarnings ("unchecked") Enumeration < String > keys = (Enumeration < String >) properties.propertyNames ();if (!keys.hasMoreElements ()) { try { createDefaultPropertyFile (defaultPropertiesPath);} catch (IOException e) { error ("Error while trying to copy the Default-Properties File",e);} if (new File (defaultPropertiesPath).exists () &&!writeToPropertiesFile (defaultPropertiesPath)) return;reloadProperties ();} } }

codeComment: The `reloadProperties` method reloads the properties from a specified file. It creates a temporary `Properties` object and a `BufferedReader` to read the file. The file is read using UTF-8 encoding, and the properties are loaded into the temporary object. If successful, the method updates the `properties` field with the new properties and notifies all registered listeners. If an `IOException` occurs during the process, an error message is logged. The `BufferedReader` is closed in the `finally` block to ensure resources are released properly.
codeFunctions: private void reloadProperties () { Properties temp = new Properties ();BufferedReader bufferedReader = null;try { File properties = new File (propertiesPath);bufferedReader = new BufferedReader (new InputStreamReader (new FileInputStream (properties),"UTF8"));temp.load (bufferedReader);this.properties = temp;listeners.removeIf (weakReference -> weakReference.get () == null);listeners.forEach (weakReference -> { Consumer < PropertiesAssistant > consumer = weakReference.get ();if (consumer != null) consumer.accept (this);});} catch (IOException e) { error ("Error while trying to load the Properties-File: " + propertiesPath,e);} finally { if (bufferedReader != null) { try { bufferedReader.close ();} catch (IOException e) { error ("Unable to close input stream",e);} } } }

codeComment: The `parsePacketExtension` method is designed to parse XML data and create a `DefaultPacketExtension` object. It takes three parameters: `elementName`, `namespace`, and an `XmlPullParser` object. The method initializes a `DefaultPacketExtension` with the provided element name and namespace. It then iterates through the XML using the `XmlPullParser` to extract data. If it encounters a start tag, it checks if the tag is empty and sets the value accordingly. If the tag is not empty, it retrieves the text content and sets it. The loop continues until the end tag of the specified element is reached, at which point the method returns the constructed `DefaultPacketExtension` object.
codeFunctions: public static PacketExtension parsePacketExtension (String elementName,String namespace,XmlPullParser parser) throws Exception { DefaultPacketExtension extension = new DefaultPacketExtension (elementName,namespace);boolean done = false;while (!done) { int eventType = parser.next ();if (eventType == XmlPullParser.START_TAG) { String name = parser.getName ();// If an empty element, set the value with the empty string. if (parser.isEmptyElementTag ()) { extension.setValue (name,"");} // Otherwise, get the the element text. else { eventType = parser.next ();if (eventType == XmlPullParser.TEXT) { String value = parser.getText ();extension.setValue (name,value);} } } else if (eventType == XmlPullParser.END_TAG) { if (parser.getName ().equals (elementName)) { done = true;} } } return extension;}

originalComment: Purges the specified reference.
codeComment:
The `purge` method is designed to remove a specific entry from a hash table based on a given reference. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Calculate Hash and Index**: The method starts by calculating the hash code of the provided reference and then determines the index in the hash table where the entry might be located using the `hashIndex` method.

2. **Initialize Variables**: It initializes two variables: `previous` to keep track of the previous entry in the chain and `entry` to start from the entry at the calculated index.

3. **Iterate Through Chain**: The method iterates through the linked list of entries at the calculated index. For each entry, it checks if the entry can be purged using the `purge` method of the `ReferenceEntry` class.

4. **Remove Entry**: If an entry is found that can be purged:
   - If `previous` is `null`, it means the entry to be removed is the first in the chain, so it updates the index in the `data` array to point to the next entry.
   - Otherwise, it updates the `next` pointer of the `previous` entry to skip the entry to be removed.
   - It decrements the size of the hash table.

5. **Return**: The method returns after removing the entry. If no matching entry is found, the method completes without making any changes.
codeFunctions: protected void purge (Reference ref) { // The hashCode of the reference is the hashCode of the // mapping key, even if the reference refers to the // mapping value... int hash = ref.hashCode ();int index = hashIndex (hash,data.length);HashEntry < K,V > previous = null;HashEntry < K,V > entry = data [ index ];while (entry != null) { if (((ReferenceEntry < K,V >) entry).purge (ref)) { if (previous == null) { data [ index ] = entry.next;} else { previous.next = entry.next;} this.size --;return;} previous = entry;entry = entry.next;} }

This method initializes the output directory for an application. It first retrieves the current working directory and constructs the target directory path. It then checks if the target directory exists:

1. If the target directory exists, it verifies that it is a directory and that the application has write permissions. If either condition fails, it prints an error message and returns -1.
2. If the target directory does not exist, it checks if the parent directory exists and is writable. If the parent directory is not a directory or is not writable, it prints an error message and returns -1.

1. **Initialization**: 
   - Two collections, `addresses` and `result`, are initialized to store IP addresses.

2. **Address Handling**:
   - If `addr` is `null`, the method attempts to add all local network addresses to the `addresses` collection. If an exception occurs, it throws a `FireRESTException`.
   - If `addr` is not `null`, it adds `addr` directly to the `addresses` collection.

3. **Scanning**:
   - The method iterates over each `InetAddress` in the `addresses` collection.
   - For each address, it checks if it is an instance of `Inet4Address`.
   - If it is, it calculates the starting address of the subnet (assuming a 24-bit subnet mask) and calls `scanRangeCore` to perform the actual scanning.
   - The results from `scanRangeCore` are added to the `result` collection.

4. **Return**:
   - The method returns the `result` collection containing the active IP addresses found.

This method is designed to scan a specified range of IP addresses and identify which ones are active, using a core scanning function (`scanRangeCore`) that performs the actual network checks.

codeComment:
The `executeApplication` method is designed to execute an application based on the provided service object (`svc`), arguments (`args`), and the original class name (`orig`). Here's a summary of its functionality:

1. **Check if `svc` is not null and is an instance of `ExecS_Application`:**
   - If `svc` is an instance of `Gen_RunScripts`, it sets the class map for `Gen_RunScripts`.
   - If `svc` is an instance of `Gen_ExecJarScripts`, it sets the class map for `Gen_ExecJarScripts`.
   - It then calls the `executeApplication` method on `svc`, passing the arguments array with the first element removed.

2. **Handle cases where `svc` is null:**
   - Prints an error message indicating that the object for the class or application name could not be created.
   - Returns `-1`.

3. **Handle cases where `svc` is not an instance of `ExecS_Application`:**
   - Prints an error message indicating that the given class or application name is not an instance of `ExecS_Application`.
   - Returns `-2`.

4. **Handle unexpected errors:**
   - Prints an error message indicating an unexpected error during processing.
   - Returns `-3`.

This method checks if the current application is running inside an executable JAR file. It does so by:

1. Retrieving the class name and its path.
2. Checking if the class path starts with "jar", indicating it's inside a JAR.
3. If not, it prints an error message and returns `false`.
4. It then constructs the path to the manifest file within the JAR.
5. Attempts to open and read the manifest file.
6. If an exception occurs while reading the manifest, it prints an error message and returns `false`.
7. It checks if the manifest contains a "Main-Class" attribute.
8. If the "Main-Class" attribute is missing, it prints an error message and returns `false`.
9. If all checks pass, it returns `true`, indicating the application is running inside an executable JAR.

codeComment:
The `escapeForXML` method is designed to escape special characters in a given string to ensure it is safe for use in XML. It processes each character in the input string and replaces certain characters with their corresponding XML entity codes. Specifically, it replaces:

- Spaces with `<` (less than)
- Greater than signs (`>`) with `>`
- Ampersands (`&`) with `&`
- Double quotes (`"`) with `"`

The method handles null input by returning null immediately. It uses a `StringBuffer` to efficiently build the output string, appending characters and entity codes as needed. The method iterates through the input string, checking each character and performing the necessary replacements. If no replacements are made, the original string is returned.
codeFunctions: public static final String escapeForXML (String string) { if (string == null) { return null;} char ch;int i = 0;int last = 0;char [ ] input = string.toCharArray ();int len = input.length;StringBuffer out = new StringBuffer ((int) (len * 1.3));for (;i < len;i ++) { ch = input [ i ];if (ch > ' ') { continue;} else if (ch == ' ') { if (i > last) { out.append (input,last,i - last);} last = i + 1;out.append (LT_ENCODE);} else if (ch == ' ') { if (i > last) { out.append (input,last,i - last);} last = i + 1;out.append (GT_ENCODE);} else if (ch == ' ') { if (i > last) { out.append (input,last,i - last);} // Do nothing if the string is of the form ë (unicode // value) if (!(len > i + 5 && input [ i + 1 ] == ' ' && Character.isDigit (input [ i + 2 ]) && Character.isDigit (input [ i + 3 ]) && Character.isDigit (input [ i + 4 ]) && input [ i + 5 ] == ' ')) { last = i + 1;out.append (AMP_ENCODE);} } else if (ch == ' ') { if (i > last) { out.append (input,last,i - last);} last = i + 1;out.append (QUOTE_ENCODE);} } if (last == 0) { return string;} if (i > last) { out.append (input,last,i - last);} return out.toString ();}

The `challengeReceived` method processes a received challenge string, evaluates it using a security context (`sc`), and sends an appropriate response back to the server. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Input Handling**: The method takes a `String` parameter `challenge` which may be `null`.
2. **Challenge Evaluation**:

3. **Response Construction**:
   - If the evaluation result (`response`) is `null`, it creates a `Response` stanza without any data.
   - If `response` is not `null`, it encodes the response in base64 and creates a `Response` stanza with this encoded data.
4. **Sending the Response**: The method sends the constructed `Response` stanza to the server using `getSASLAuthentication().send(responseStanza)`.
codeFunctions: public void challengeReceived (String challenge) throws IOException { byte response [ ];if (challenge != null) { response = sc.evaluateChallenge (StringUtils.decodeBase64 (challenge));} else { response = sc.evaluateChallenge (new byte [ 0 ]);} Packet responseStanza;if (response == null) { responseStanza = new Response ();} else { responseStanza = new Response (StringUtils.encodeBase64 (response,false));} // Send the authentication to the server getSASLAuthentication ().send (responseStanza);}

originalComment: Handles an event from OSGi and places it in the appropriate queue.
codeComment: The `handleEvent` method processes an incoming event by determining the appropriate queue to store it based on the event's TTL (Time To Live) property. It first retrieves the event's topic and checks if there are any associated `IndexingHandler` objects. If there are, it calculates the effective TTL by considering the TTLs of any `QoSIndexHandler` objects. The method then selects a queue from an ordered list of queues based on the TTL. If the TTL is less than the batch delay of the fastest queue, the event is posted to that queue. Otherwise, it iterates through the queues to find the first one that can satisfy the TTL and posts the event there. If no suitable queue is found, the event is posted to the fastest queue. If an `IOException` occurs during this process, it is logged as a warning.
codeFunctions: public void handleEvent (Event event) { String topic = event.getTopic ();LOGGER.debug ("Got Event {} {} ",event,handlers);Collection < IndexingHandler > contentIndexHandler = handlers.get (topic);if (contentIndexHandler != null && contentIndexHandler.size () > 0) { try { int ttl = Utils.toInt (event.getProperty (TopicIndexer.TTL),Integer.MAX_VALUE);for (IndexingHandler indexingHandler:contentIndexHandler) { if (indexingHandler instanceof QoSIndexHandler) { ttl = Math.min (ttl,Utils.defaultMax (((QoSIndexHandler) indexingHandler).getTtl (event)));} } QueueManager q = null;// queues is ordered by ascending ttl, so the fastest queue is queues[0], // if the ttl is less that that, we can't satisfy it, so we will put it // in the fastest queue if (ttl < queues [ 0 ].batchDelay) { LOGGER.warn ("Unable to satisfy TTL of {} on event {}, posting to the highest priority queue. " + "If this message is logged a lot please adjust the queues or change the event ttl to something that can be satisfied. " + "Filling the highest priority queue is counter productive. ",ttl,event);queues [ 0 ].saveEvent (event);} else { for (QueueManager qm:queues) { if (ttl < qm.batchDelay) { q.saveEvent (event);q = null;break;} q = qm;} if (q != null) { q.saveEvent (event);} } } catch (IOException e) { LOGGER.warn (e.getMessage (),e);} } }

codeComment:
This method, `hash`, computes a hash code for a given object `key`. It uses a series of bitwise operations to mix the bits of the original hash code, aiming to reduce collisions in hash-based data structures. The steps are as follows:

1. Start with the hash code of the key.
2. Apply a bitwise NOT and left shift operation, then add the result to the original hash code.
3. Perform a bitwise XOR with the result of a right shift operation.
4. Add the result of a left shift operation to the hash code.
5. Finally, perform a bitwise XOR with the result of another right shift operation.

The method returns the final computed hash code.

originalComment: Changes the size of the data structure to the capacity proposed.
codeComment:
The `ensureCapacity` method is designed to increase the capacity of a hash table if the new capacity exceeds the current capacity. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Check Current Capacity**: It first checks if the `newCapacity` is less than or equal to the current `oldCapacity`. If so, it returns immediately as no resizing is needed.

2. **Initialize New Data Array**:
   - If the `size` of the hash table is zero, it calculates a new threshold using the `calculateThreshold` method and initializes a new `data` array with the `newCapacity`.

3. **Resize Existing Data**:
   - If the `size` is not zero, it creates a temporary array `oldEntries` to hold the current entries and a new array `newEntries` with the `newCapacity`.
   - It increments the `modCount` to indicate a structural modification.
   - It iterates over the `oldEntries` array from the end to the beginning. For each non-null entry, it rehashes the entry to find its new index in the `newEntries` array and links it to the existing entries at that index.
   - This process continues until all entries are rehashed and placed in the new array.

4. **Update Threshold and Data**:
   - After rehashing, it recalculates the `threshold` using the `calculateThreshold` method with the new capacity and load factor.
   - Finally, it updates the `data` array to the new `newEntries` array.

This method ensures that the hash table can accommodate more entries by resizing the underlying array and rehashing the existing entries.

originalComment: Calculates the new capacity of the map.This implementation normalizes the capacity to a power of two.
codeComment: This method calculates a new capacity for a data structure, ensuring it does not exceed a predefined maximum capacity. It starts with a new capacity of 1 and doubles it in a loop until it meets or exceeds the proposed capacity. If the proposed capacity exceeds the maximum capacity, the new capacity is set to the maximum capacity.
codeFunctions: protected int calculateNewCapacity (int proposedCapacity) { int newCapacity = 1;if (proposedCapacity > MAXIMUM_CAPACITY) { newCapacity = MAXIMUM_CAPACITY;} else { while (newCapacity < proposedCapacity) { newCapacity <<= 1;// multiply by two } if (newCapacity > MAXIMUM_CAPACITY) { newCapacity = MAXIMUM_CAPACITY;} } return newCapacity;}

originalComment: Fires listeners when a reconnection attempt has failed.
codeComment: This method, `notifyReconnectionFailed`, is responsible for notifying all registered `ConnectionListener` objects about a failed reconnection attempt. It first checks if reconnection is allowed using the `isReconnectionAllowed` method. If reconnection is permitted, it iterates through the list of `ConnectionListener` objects associated with the `connection` and calls the `reconnectionFailed` method on each listener, passing the `exception` as an argument.
codeFunctions: protected void notifyReconnectionFailed (Exception exception) { if (isReconnectionAllowed ()) { for (ConnectionListener listener:connection.connectionListeners) { listener.reconnectionFailed (exception);} } }

originalComment: Fires listeners when The Connection will retry a reconnection.Expressed in seconds.
codeComment: This method, `notifyAttemptToReconnectIn`, is designed to notify all registered `ConnectionListener` objects about an upcoming reconnection attempt. It takes an integer `seconds` as a parameter, which indicates the number of seconds before the reconnection attempt is scheduled. The method first checks if reconnection is allowed by calling the `isReconnectionAllowed` method. If reconnection is allowed, it iterates over all `ConnectionListener` objects in the `connection.connectionListeners` list and calls the `reconnectingIn` method on each listener, passing the `seconds` parameter.
codeFunctions: protected void notifyAttemptToReconnectIn (int seconds) { if (isReconnectionAllowed ()) { for (ConnectionListener listener:connection.connectionListeners) { listener.reconnectingIn (seconds);} } }
